The `indeterminate` rule is the load-bearing D-272 §2.4 invariant — an evidence-incomplete probe means the claim could not be fully evaluated, so it is not Verified regardless of the other probes (re-runnable, never a silent pass). NO threshold, NO "most-passed", NO partial credit: one non-pass probe sinks the claim. **Three fail-loud disciplines:** (1) **N=0 RAISES** `ValueError` — an empty bva set is a wiring/generation bug (a bva claim mints ≥1 applicable probe at generation, D-272 §2.1), NEVER vacuously Verified (returning True for "no probes" would silently Verify an un-probed claim — the exact overstate-what-you-know failure the strict semantics forbid; this is the bva counterpart to `single`'s N≠1 raise); (2) an **unrecognized `outcome`** value RAISES (no implicit default), and the loop does NOT short-circuit on the first `fail` so a bad value anywhere in the set still surfaces; (3) `polarity` is **NOT read** (same as `single` — S4 already folds accept/reject into each probe's pass/fail outcome; polarity is carried for diagnostics only). **Completeness is the CALLER's contract**, not this arm's: `_apply_bva` assumes it receives the COMPLETE applicable probe set and ANDs outcomes; membership/expected-count (a batch missing a probe ⇒ incomplete ⇒ not Verified) is the batch reader's job (Slice 4c) — stated explicitly in code so the boundary can't drift. `single` left byte-identical; the unknown-KIND `ValueError` unchanged. **PURE + DORMANT:** `strategy.py` still imports only stdlib (the AST purity-guard test holds); `apply_strategy(_, "bva", _)` is called by NOTHING in `primeqa/` (the D-278 router routes every claim to `single` until §4a records a kind) — zero live effect, no consumer until Slice 4d. **Verification:** 10 new bva unit tests (all-pass N=2/5→True; one-fail→False; one-indeterminate→False; mixed fail+indeterminate→False; N=1 pass→True / N=1 fail→False; **N=0 raises — asserted it raises, does NOT return True**; unrecognized-outcome-amid-a-fail raises; polarity-invariance) + the existing `single`/adapter/byte-identity/purity tests unchanged; full unit suite 3240 green; diff touches ONLY `strategy.py` (+51) + its test (no reader, no decision engine, no schema, no migration; pure function — zero claim writes). Scope OUT (deferred): the batch reader + completeness (4c), the decision-engine bva branch (4d), the async companion (4e), §4a authoring (4f). See D-272 / D-274 / D-278.

## D-280 — wire `Verified` into the decision engine (S6 build Slice 4b; governed by ADR-001 D-270 + the Slice-2a applier D-274). The release decision's per-claim **good state** is now a single `Verified` predicate, `_claim_verified(c)` in `primeqa/intelligence/substrate_decision.py`, derived via `apply_strategy('single', [probe_result_from_outcome(latest_run.outcome, expect_rejection=False)])` — replacing the inline `latest_run.outcome == 'passed'` rule that was scattered across the engine. **The first non-dormant S6 slice** (it runs on every claim, every decision, immediately on deploy) — but **provably BEHAVIOR-NEUTRAL**: `s4_execution_runs.outcome` is DB-enum-locked to exactly `{passed,failed,errored,skipped}` (the four the adapter maps, so a persisted row can never make it raise), and Slice 2a proved on live data that `apply_strategy('single',…) == (outcome=='passed')` for every claim. The proof IS the gate: the FULL `compute_substrate_decision` output (recommendation + pass_rate + reasoning + blocking + metrics) was re-derived for real requirements (SQ-205 `no_go`/20.0%, SQ-212 `no_go`/33.3%, both `no_go`/14.3% — mixed passed/errored) on `main` vs the branch with a fixed `now` and is **byte-for-byte identical**. **Every good-state read routes through `_claim_verified`**: the flaky-quarantine gate (`_claim_quarantined`), the `passed` count that feeds `pass_rate`, the per-claim blocker list, and the `latest_run` cause-phrase gate — grep-proven that no `outcome == 'passed'` good-state check survives outside the predicate (the `failed`/`errored` counts stay raw — they are outcome-category tallies for the metrics breakdown, not a good-vs-not-good grade; the blocking entry's `"outcome"` stays raw — it reports the actual string for display). **Polarity is a NO-OP on the single arm** (S4 already folds accept/reject into the outcome — 2a's `test_polarity_does_not_change_single_verdict`), so `expect_rejection=False` is exact, not an assumption — no `is_prohibition` derivation needed. **Never-run** (`latest_run is None`) stays a separate `never_run`/`has_runs` blocker — it is NEVER routed through the applier (single requires N=1, which would raise on an empty set); `_claim_verified` returns `False` for it without calling the applier. `_assemble_claim_evidence` computes `verified` ONCE and attaches it to each evidence dict (available to UI / Slice 4c); `_claim_verified` prefers that attached value and derives the same rule only for a hand-built evidence dict that lacks it — so the diff stays within `substrate_decision.py` + its test (no fixture edits in sibling test files). **`_claim_verified` is THE single place good state is decided — Slice 4d adds the bva branch HERE** (`if c.get('strategy_kind') == 'bva': return _verified_bva(c)`). **Verification:** the byte-identical full-decision re-derivation (above); a read-only live-parity integration test (attached `verified == (outcome=='passed')` over real SQ-205/SQ-212 assembled evidence) + the 2a live-parity, both run green against the Railway DB; 8 new offline unit tests (the predicate truth table, never-run-without-applier, attached-value-preference, pass_rate/passed driven by `verified`, blocker list driven by `verified`); full unit suite 3248 green; diff touches ONLY `substrate_decision.py` (+60) + its test (no schema, no migration, no run path, no reader, zero claim writes). Scope OUT (deferred): the bva branch in the decision engine (4d), the batch reader + completeness (4c), the async companion (4e), §4a authoring (4f). See D-274 / D-279.

## D-281 — run-all batch manifest (expected applicable set, C2) (S6 build Slice 4c.0; governed by the Slice-4c recon decision A=C2). Run-all now records, per invocation, a **batch manifest** — the EXPECTED applicable recipe set as it was AT BATCH TIME — so the completeness check (Slice 4c.1) is a **drift-immune set-compare against persisted data**, not a read-time recompute. New tenant table `s4_runall_batch_manifests` (migration `20260627_0010`, additive `CREATE TABLE`): `batch_id UUID PK` (shared with `s4_execution_runs.batch_id`), `claim_test_id UUID NOT NULL`, `expected_recipe_ids UUID[] NOT NULL`, `env_key VARCHAR NULL`, `created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL`. **C2 over an env-key (the recon's decisive finding):** `select_recipes_for_execution` depends on FIVE inputs — the approved-claim version walk, recipe `valid_to` supersession, recipe status, recipe priority, AND env satisfiability — and four are MUTABLE after the batch runs, so recomputing the applicable set at read time (even pinned to an env-key, "C1") is NOT drift-immune; recording the actual `expected_recipe_ids` is. `env_key` is **optional audit only, NOT load-bearing** (the recorded membership subsumes the env, since it was computed under that env). **The producer write commits EARLY — its OWN transaction, BEFORE the probe loop** (`_write_batch_manifest` opens its own `get_tenant_connection`) — a correctness requirement, not a nicety: a batch that crashes before any probe persists is still readable as `expected=N` / `present=0` → INCOMPLETE → not-Verified (4c.1); a manifest-less batch is unknowable → not-Verified (the safe default). Wired into BOTH run-all paths right after the applicable set is confirmed non-empty (sync threads `tenant_id` from the router — `run_claim_execution_for_tenant` now passes it — since the sync entry takes a `session` not a `tenant_id`; async already had it). Empty applicable set ⇒ NO manifest (no batch runs). The write is injectable (`manifest_writer`, default `_write_batch_manifest`) for tests, and the default no-ops when `tenant_id` is None (no tenant context). **ADDITIVE + DORMANT:** nothing routes to run-all until §4a, so the producer write never fires in prod; the single run path + the existing run-all loop are byte-identical (the manifest write precedes the loop and is its own txn). **Verification:** the migration applied to a THROWAWAY schema (NOT prod) — columns/types/PK correct (`expected_recipe_ids` = `uuid[]`), the producer `UUID[]` INSERT round-trips, downgrade drops cleanly; 5 new unit tests (manifest written FIRST before any probe with the threaded tenant_id + batch_id + full applicable set; empty-set → no manifest; manifest intact when a probe errors mid-batch; default writer no-ops without tenant context; async records the expected set before probes); the existing run-all failure-isolation tests still green (the manifest write didn't perturb the loop); full unit suite 3253; diff = the migration + `run.py` + its test only (no reader, no completeness logic, no decision-engine touch, no other schema). **MIGRATE-FIRST** at the push gate (run the tenant migration + read back before relying on the table). Scope OUT (deferred): the batch reader + completeness gate (4c.1), the decision-engine bva branch (4d), the async companion (4e), §4a authoring (4f). See D-275 / D-277 / D-279 / D-280.

## D-282 — batch reader + completeness gate (S6 build Slice 4c.1; governed by the Slice-4c recon decisions A/B/C). New DORMANT module `primeqa/interpretation/batch_reader.py` (same S6 home as `strategy.py`): `read_batch_completeness(session, claim_test_id) -> BatchCompleteness{complete, probes, batch_id, reason}` — the gate that makes "partial batch ⇒ not-Verified" true. **(A) drift-immune membership:** the EXPECTED set is read from the persisted `s4_runall_batch_manifests.expected_recipe_ids` (D-281), **never** recomputed via `select_recipes_for_execution` at read time; completeness = `expected ⊆ present` (the recipe_ids that have a batch row) — `⊆` not `==`, so an extra row never makes a batch incomplete; the load-bearing direction is "every expected probe has a row". **(B) short-circuit (the load-bearing correctness):** an INCOMPLETE batch (an expected recipe has NO row — persist-fault or never-ran) returns `complete=False, probes=None` — **NO ProbeResults are built and the bva arm is never reached**, preserving the arm's "trusts the set is complete" contract (D-279); an `errored`-row-PRESENT probe is COMPLETE-but-indeterminate (the row exists → membership satisfied; the row's `outcome=errored` maps to `indeterminate`, and the arm then returns not-Verified). **(C) latest-is-truth:** `select_most_recent_batch` orders by `max(finished_at)` over a batch's rows — NOT by `batch_id` (uuid4 is non-chronological); a newer incomplete batch is not-Verified / re-run, with **NO fallback to an older complete batch** (aligns with the single path, which grades the latest counted run and never falls back). On COMPLETE, builds one `ProbeResult` per EXPECTED recipe (manifest order) via `probe_result_from_outcome(s4_run.outcome, expect_rejection=<recipe's observation_realization mutation step>)`; `expect_rejection` is **not load-bearing** (the bva arm reads only `outcome` — polarity is carried for diagnostics) and defaults `False` on a missing recipe body. The reader does NOT call `apply_strategy`: it returns `{complete, probes}`; **Slice 4d** does `incomplete → not-Verified` / `complete → apply_strategy(claim, 'bva', probes)`. A missing manifest for a batch with rows (shouldn't happen given 4c.0's early-commit) → `complete=False, reason='no_manifest'` (safe default, like row-absent). **DORMANT + read-only:** no caller in `primeqa/` until 4d; no schema, no migration, never writes. **Verification (the tests are the deliverable):** 18 offline tests — pure `_assess` (complete-all-pass→Verified; complete-one-errored→indeterminate→not-Verified; **INCOMPLETE row-absent → probes=None, arm never built — the load-bearing test**; `⊆`-not-`==` extra-row; manifest-order; one-failed) + `_extract_expect_rejection` polarity + fake-session orchestration (complete / incomplete / no-batch / no-manifest) + a **no-recompute guard** (patch `select_recipes_for_execution` to RAISE → the reader still works, proving drift-immunity / no live env-resolve); 2 integration tests (seed-in-txn-ROLLBACK, prod left 0 manifest rows) — **most-recent by `finished_at` not `batch_id` with NO fallback** (the later/incomplete batch given the SMALLER uuid, so a wrong `ORDER BY batch_id` would pick the earlier/complete one) + a complete batch end-to-end; full unit suite 3271; diff = the new module + its test only. Deferred fidelity: the per-probe `boundary` marker stays `"single"` (the bva arm ignores it; §4a authors the real min/max/etc. markers); the s6 verdict is carried best-effort in the row read for future diagnostics. Scope OUT: the decision-engine bva branch (4d), the async companion (4e), §4a authoring (4f). See D-279 / D-281.

## D-283 — bva branch in the decision engine (S6 build Slice 4d; governed by the Slice-4c recon + ADR-001 + D-272). `substrate_decision._claim_verified` gains the **bva branch** — the assembly point where the three already-built pieces finally connect: the seam 4b marked (D-280), the batch reader (4c.1 `read_batch_completeness`, D-282), and the bva arm (4a `apply_strategy(_, 'bva', _)`, D-279). When a claim records `strategy_kind == 'bva'`, good state comes from the claim's most-recent run-all batch: an INCOMPLETE batch (a probe row absent, or no batch — the reader already short-circuited with `probes=None`) ⇒ **return False directly**, NOT-Verified, **without calling the arm**; a COMPLETE batch ⇒ `apply_strategy(claim, 'bva', result.probes)` (strict-AND, D-279). The arm is therefore **only ever called with a reader-certified COMPLETE set** — never `probes=None`/empty (which the arm raises on by design) — preserving 4a's "trusts the set is complete" contract. **A DEAD BRANCH:** nothing in `primeqa/` records `strategy_kind='bva'` (grep-confirmed: the only `== 'bva'` occurrences are READS — this branch + the 3.4 router — never an assignment), so it is unreachable until §4a authors the kind (4f). **Behavior-neutral because the branch is never taken — NOT by runtime equivalence**, and the byte-identical proof is the gate (the 4b discipline, since this touches the GO/NO-GO engine): the FULL `compute_substrate_decision` output for SQ-205 (`no_go`/20.0%) / SQ-212 (`no_go`/33.3%) / both (`no_go`/14.3%) was re-derived on `main` vs the branch with a fixed clock and is **byte-for-byte identical** — the dead branch does not perturb the single path. **Wiring details:** the branch sits AFTER the attached-`verified` short-circuit, so a production bva claim whose `verified` was already attached (4f's `_assemble` path) never needs a `session` here; `_claim_verified` gains an optional `session=None` only for the derive case (the 4f assemble-time read + the synthetic tests). An **ABSENT** kind (`None` — every claim today) takes the SINGLE path (the honest default); an **UNRECOGNIZED** kind RAISES `ValueError` (a wiring bug, never a silent single fallback — the 3.4 router discipline; ABSENT vs UNRECOGNIZED are two distinct branches). The single path is left **byte-identical** (the new code is two cheap checks that no-op for `strategy_kind=None`, before the unchanged single derivation). **Verification:** 8 new synthetic bva-branch tests (complete-all-pass→Verified; complete-one-errored→not-Verified via the arm's indeterminate rule; **INCOMPLETE → not-Verified with `apply_strategy` patched to RAISE, proving the arm is never called**; no-batch→not-Verified; attached-`verified` short-circuits before any batch read; absent→single unchanged; explicit `single`→single; **unrecognized→raises**) — the batch read canned via monkeypatch (the reader itself is 4c.1-tested); full unit suite 3279; diff = `substrate_decision.py` (+29) + its test only (no schema, no migration, no run path, no reader change). Scope OUT (deferred): §4a recording `strategy_kind` + `_assemble` reading it / attaching the bva `verified` + the `strategy_kind` column (4f); the async companion (4e). See D-279 / D-280 / D-282.

## D-284 — async run-all companion (S6 build Slice 4e; governed by D-275/D-277/D-278). The async consume path gains the SAME single-vs-bva routing as the 3.4 sync router, and the consumer learns to handle a `RunAllResult` — the async prerequisite that MUST land BEFORE §4a (4f) so an async-enqueued bva claim doesn't crash the consumer. **(1) async-entry routing:** new `async_run_claim_execution_for_tenant` in `execution_engine/run.py` — the async counterpart of `run_claim_execution_for_tenant` (D-278). It **REUSES** `route_strategy` + `_recorded_strategy_kind` (the ONE place single-vs-bva is decided — no second copy): resolve the claim's recorded kind in a brief read, then dispatch — `kind=='bva'` → `run_all_recipes_execution_async` (3.3); `kind=='single'`/absent → `run_recipe_execution_async` (existing); UNRECOGNIZED → raise (the same absent→single honest-default / unrecognized→raise two-branch discipline as 3.4). The consumer's `run_fn` default (`process_execution_job_for_tenant` + `run_s4_execution_tick`) is flipped to this router. **(2) the crash fix:** `consumer.py` read `result.evidence.outcome` directly — a `RunAllResult` carries `.probes`/`.batch_id`, NOT `.evidence`, so the direct read would `AttributeError` (the specific bug 4e prevents — a unit test asserts the old read raises). New `_async_log_outcome` handles BOTH shapes: a single `RunPathResult` returns the EXACT prior expression (byte-identical); a `RunAllResult` (duck-typed via `hasattr(result, 'batch_id')`) reports the batch + probe count — never assumes `.evidence`, never computes Verified (the decision engine reads the batch, 4d). `_map_run_result` (the sync console mapper) was already getattr-safe (no crash) but uninformative for a batch — it gains a `RunAllResult` branch (reports `batch_id` + `probe_count`); the single path is byte-identical. **ADDITIVE + DORMANT:** nothing records `strategy_kind='bva'` (grep-confirmed: only READS — the 4d branch + the 3.4/4e routers — never an assignment), so the async path ALWAYS routes single — byte-identical to calling `run_recipe_execution_async` directly (plus one cheap approved-claim read, the same resolution the async run does internally). Run-all is reachable only once §4a records the kind (4f). **Verification:** 11 new offline tests (5 async router dispatch — single/bva/unrecognized→raise/no-claim, fakes assert WHICH async path; 6 consumer/console — `_async_log_outcome` single byte-identical, the old direct read raises on a `RunAllResult`, a `RunAllResult` does NOT crash + reports the batch, `_map_run_result` single/no-run unchanged + `RunAllResult` reports the batch with no Verified) + the consumer default-run_fn drift-guard updated (default is now the async router); the integration consumer suite (10) green; full unit suite 3291; diff = `consumer.py` + `run.py` + `s4_execution_console.py` (+ their tests) only — no schema, no migration, no sync-path change, no decision-engine change. Scope OUT (deferred): §4a authoring (4f); batch-aware run-failure notify — the D-234 unattended-run notify still skips a `RunAllResult` (its `getattr(result,'evidence',None)` is None for a batch, so a batch with failed probes won't notify) — a future enhancement when batches go live, NOT a 4e crash. See D-277 / D-278.

## D-286 — generation is org-scoped (fixes the live two-org ambiguous-reference break). S3 generation read S1 **tenant-wide** (`SemanticOrgModel(conn)` with no org) while S4 execution correctly scopes per-org (D-260). Since env-78 synced (a second org on tenant_1, version_seq 82+), every standard entity resolves to TWO orgs → ambiguous-reference refusal for ALL generation on tenant_1 (req-283). This mirrors execution's shipped per-org pattern into generation. **(Decision number: D-286 — D-285 is reserved for the held, unpushed Slice-4f.0 branch.)** **Two unscoped points, fixed together (half-scoped is still wrong):** (a) **entity reads** — `run_generation` (`generation/run.py:66`) built `GovernanceCore(SemanticOrgModel(conn))` org-blind; now takes a required `environment_id` (its sole prod caller `consumer.py:66` passes `job.environment_id`), resolves env→org, and builds `SemanticOrgModel(conn, connected_org_id=org_id)`. (b) **version pin** — `resolve_current_s1_version` (`intake.py:44`) pinned the tenant-wide `MAX(version_seq)`; now takes `environment_id` (its caller `enqueue_s3_generation` already had it) and pins the **org's** latest seq. PROVEN both-together on live tenant_1: the org-blind pin is **seq 90** (env-78's latest sync) but env-59's own latest is **seq 89** — scoping reads to env-59 while pinning to 90 would read env-59's entities at a version env-59 never synced (the version-mismatch the half-fix produces). **One shared resolver (PROMOTE-TO-SHARED):** execution's fail-loud env→org wrapper is relocated to `sync/credentials.py` as `resolve_connected_org_or_raise(conn, environment_id)` (wraps the existing `get_connected_org_for_environment`, raises on None/unresolved); `_resolve_run_org` (S4) now delegates to it. `OrgResolutionError` moved to the shared cross-cutting home too — and the tension dissolved cleanly: it was an `ExecutionEngineError`, but `consumer._classify_error` maps **both** `ExecutionEngineError` *and* the fallthrough to `"execution_error"` (and the job is caught by a broad `except Exception`), so a NEUTRAL-based error in `sync/` keeps S4's `error_code` **byte-identical** with no `_classify_error` change and no S1→S4 backward dependency; `execution_engine/errors.py` re-exports it so `from …errors import OrgResolutionError` still resolves (the identical object). **Fail-loud everywhere** env→org is resolved (incl. a `None` `environment_id`) — never a silent org-blind read (org-blind on a 2-org tenant IS the bug). **No schema** (the `connected_org_id` columns + the env→org map already exist from D-255/D-257). **The 4 other unscoped `SemanticOrgModel(conn)` consumers are FLAGGED, not fixed** (each a latent copy of this regression on a 2-org tenant): S7 `/ask` (`conversation_bridge.py:102`), the decision engine staleness read (`substrate_decision.py:173`), the sync console (`s1_sync_console.py:301`), and S8 grounding recompute (`evolution/recompute.py:167` — already D-265-GUARDED: it refuses on >1-org tenants rather than computing wrong). **PROOF 1 (live two-org tenant_1, read-only, zero writes):** scoped to env-59, `Opportunity`/`Account`/`Case` each resolve **2 → 1** (the #283 break fixed at the resolution layer). **PROOF 2 (single-org NO-OP, the no-regression guarantee):** the test world is now org-aware (one org); explicit `scoped == blind` assertions on a single-org seed prove the predicate is vacuous on one org — identical rows for reads, and the org's-latest == tenant-MAX for the pin (a fresh org owning the newest version) — so a single-org / env-59-only tenant's generation is byte-identical to pre-D-286. **Test world made honest (Option A):** the shared generation conftest provisions one `connected_org` and tags its entities/edges/versions with it — ADDITIVE for the org-blind verticals (they ignore the column) and correct for the org-scoped paths (`run_generation` / `enqueue`), so the test world mirrors production rather than working around it. **Verification:** full unit suite **3300** green; full generation integration suite **108 passed / 1 skipped** (live-eval); new tests = the shared resolver fail-loud (None/unresolved → raise; re-export identity) + the synthetic **2-org discrimination** (mirrors PROOF 1: blind 2, scoped 1) + the **single-org no-op** (reads + pin); execution byte-identical (its per-org resolution units green; the 4 red `test_stranded_cleanup` tests are PRE-EXISTING — `relation "environments" does not exist`, confirmed identical with the diff stashed — environmental, unrelated). Diff = `sync/credentials.py` + `execution_engine/{errors,run}.py` + `generation/{run,intake,consumer}.py` (+ the generation conftest/test-threading + 2 new test files); no schema, no migration. Op note: PROOF 1 + all live work read-only at the resolution layer — no stray claims written to tenant_1. See D-255 / D-257 / D-260.
## D-285 — strategy_kind column on test_claims (S6 build Slice 4f.0; governed by the 4f recon, Fork C). The one missing piece of the otherwise-built bva pipeline: a place for a claim to **affirmatively record** its evaluation strategy. The two readers already in place — the run router (`run.py` `_recorded_strategy_kind` → `getattr(claim,'strategy_kind',None)`, D-278) and the decision engine (`substrate_decision._claim_verified` → `c.get('strategy_kind')`, D-280/D-283) — have ALWAYS read a top-level `strategy_kind` off the claim and harmlessly gotten `None`; **nothing persisted it**. This slice adds the column + plumbs it through write/read, DORMANT. **Fork C (LOCKED):** a DEDICATED nullable `strategy_kind VARCHAR` column on `test_claims` — persisted by `write_claim`, exposed via `ClaimRead`, **READ never DERIVED** (the router-test discipline: the kind is claim-derived ONCE at generation, 4f.2, never re-inferred at dispatch). **NOT** folded into `asserted_truth` JSONB (which carries a key-presence CHECK) and **NOT** a CHECK-constrained column (open text, code owns the `{single, bva}` vocabulary so a future strategy needs no migration). The column lives on the bitemporal claim-version row (`test_claims` PK `(test_id, version_seq)`): a new version carries its strategy, existing versions stay NULL. **Changes (4 points, additive):** (1) tenant migration `20260627_0020` — pure `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS strategy_kind VARCHAR` (nullable, no default, no backfill, no CHECK; downgrade DROPs it), idempotent per the 016+ convention; (2) the `TestClaim` ORM model gains `strategy_kind = Column(String, nullable=True)` (mirrors the 4c.0 `source VARCHAR` precedent); (3) `write_claim` gains a trailing keyword-only `strategy_kind: Optional[str] = None` param, written through to the row INSERT — every existing caller (only `generation/persistence.py` + tests) omits it → NULL; (4) `ClaimRead` gains a trailing optional `strategy_kind: Optional[str] = None` field, set by `_hydrate_claim_row` from the column. **DORMANT + byte-identical:** all-NULL after migrate → the router reads NULL → routes single (was a getattr-default None — same value), and the decision engine's `c.get('strategy_kind')` is unaffected (the `_assemble` dict doesn't carry it until 4f.1) — so every claim still routes single and every decision is unchanged. Nothing writes `'bva'` until generation sets it (4f.2). **MIGRATE-FIRST (third schema change of the arc):** the `ClaimRead` projection now eagerly SELECTs `strategy_kind`, so **every** `TestClaim` load fails against an un-migrated DB (`UndefinedColumn`) — prod MUST be migrated before this code deploys (the precise reason MIGRATE-FIRST exists). The 3 prod-reading unit tests (`test_real_approved_claims_route_single_dormant`, `test_single_matches_live_latest_run_rule`, `test_assembled_verified_matches_live_passed_rule`) are red against un-migrated prod by design and go green at the push-gate read-back (after the prod migration) — they are NOT regressions and were NOT weakened. **Verification:** migration applied to a fresh local schema via the substrate-2 alembic chain (column present, `character varying`, nullable, no default; downgrade drops it + reverts head `20260627_0020 → 20260627_0010`, upgrade restores it); 5 new offline unit tests (`ClaimRead` field default None / exposes value / explicit None; the router reads the REAL ClaimRead value → None routes single, `'bva'` routes run-all) + 3 integration round-trips (`write_claim` omitting it → NULL → `None`; `'bva'` and `'single'` round-trip through `ClaimRead`); the `write_claim` signature drift-guard updated to admit the additive tail param; `test_representation` unit dir 907 green; boot clean; diff = the migration + `models_db.py` (+9) + `coordinator.py` (+13) + the 3 test files only — no generation, no decision engine, no run path, no router. Scope OUT (deferred): `_assemble` reading the kind / attaching the bva `verified` (4f.1, the 4d precondition); §4a authoring that SETS `'bva'` from the constraint shape (4f.2); the gated single-claim live turn-on (4f.3). See D-278 / D-280 / D-283.

## D-287 — _assemble passes strategy_kind + test_id + session into _claim_verified (S6 build Slice 4f.1; the 4d precondition). `_assemble_claim_evidence` (`substrate_decision.py`) computed the per-claim good state via `_claim_verified({"latest_run": latest_run})` — a MINIMAL dict with NO `strategy_kind`, NO `test_id`, NO `session`. So even though 4d wired the bva branch into `_claim_verified` and 4f.0 (D-285) made `strategy_kind` readable via `ClaimRead`, a bva claim reaching the decision engine would STILL silently take the single path AND would trip the 4d guard (which raises `ValueError` if a bva claim reaches `_claim_verified` with a kind but no session). 4f.1 SATISFIES that precondition: the call becomes `_claim_verified({"latest_run": latest_run, "test_id": str(tid), "strategy_kind": getattr(approved, "strategy_kind", None)}, session=session)`. The call site already had everything in scope — `approved` (the `ClaimRead`, now carrying `.strategy_kind`), `tid`, `session`, `latest_run`; `getattr(approved, "strategy_kind", None)` is None-safe even when `approved` is None. **Kind AND session, both, deliberately:** the kind tells `_claim_verified` to take the bva branch; the session lets that branch read the batch — pass only the kind and 4f.2's first `'bva'` write would hit the guard. **BEHAVIOR-NEUTRAL today:** every claim's `strategy_kind` is NULL (4f.0 shipped the column all-NULL; nothing writes `'bva'` until 4f.2) → `_claim_verified` falls through to the SINGLE path exactly as before; the kind/test_id/session are inert on that path. The never-run / quarantine / pass_rate blockers are untouched — ONLY the good-state derive call changed. **A decision-engine touch → byte-identical proof is the gate** (the 4b/4d discipline): the FULL `compute_substrate_decision` output (recommendation + pass_rate + reasoning + blocking + metrics) for SQ-205 / SQ-212 / both was re-derived on `main` vs the branch with a fixed clock and is **byte-for-byte identical** (388 lines each), the captures CONFIRMED real + non-empty (the 4b false-IDENTICAL lesson — and the same lesson caught the `tail`-pipe masking pytest's exit code in the 4f.0 push). **Verification:** the byte-identical re-derivation (above); 6 new offline unit tests proving the `_assemble` call-SHAPE satisfies the precondition — a None-kind claim through the shape (with session+test_id) grades IDENTICALLY to the old minimal dict (single, session inert); a **bva** claim through the shape runs the bva branch **WITH its session — NO guard** (batch read monkeypatched, the 4d pattern); and the precondition made concrete — the SAME bva shape WITHOUT a session trips the guard, so the session is exactly what 4f.1 supplies. The bva branch stays a DEAD BRANCH on real data (grep-confirmed: nothing assigns `strategy_kind='bva'`) — 4f.1 makes it reachable-IN-PRINCIPLE, not reachable-on-real-data (that is 4f.2). Full unit suite **3310** green (the 3 prod-reading tests now pass — prod has the column from 4f.0); boot clean; diff = `substrate_decision.py` (+14/−2) + its test (+56) ONLY — no generation, no schema, no migration, no reader, no run path. Scope OUT (deferred): §4a authoring that records `'bva'` (4f.2 — the first reachable-on-real-data slice); the gated single-claim live turn-on (4f.3). See D-280 / D-283 / D-285.

## D-288 — EmissionBundle.strategy_kind slot + batch-shaped run-failure notify (S6 build Slice 4f.2-prep; the two decision-NEUTRAL pieces split off the held 4f.2). The 4f.2 build held when its locked plan ("draft a bva version of the metadata property-claim `15bb2020` / `SLA_Code__c` length=8") proved STRUCTURALLY INCOHERENT: ADR-001 bva is a field-VALUE constraint ("x ∈ [min,max]") realized by DATA probes, but `15bb2020` is a metadata PROPERTY-claim (a length=8 *attribute*); a data-create boundary probe under a property-claim is writable (`write_recipe` doesn't cross-check claim archetype ↔ recipe kind) but semantically dishonest. The "what S2 claim does a constraint-bva realize" question is deferred to **4f.2a** (design) and the authoring helper to **4f.2b** — both pending that decision. This slice ships ONLY the two pieces that are independent of the claim-shape question AND decision-neutral. **PIECE 1 — the `strategy_kind` slot (the generation→persistence wire for the 4f.0 column):** `EmissionBundle` (`generation/emission.py`) gains `strategy_kind: Optional[str] = None` (after `secondary_recipes`; both have defaults so dataclass ordering holds); `persistence._write_emission` reads `getattr(emission, "strategy_kind", None)` → passes it to `coordinator.write_claim(..., strategy_kind=...)` (the D-285 param). Today NO authoring path stamps the slot — every `author_emission` bundle carries `None` → `write_claim` persists NULL → the router (D-278) / decision engine (D-280/D-283) read `None` → single, **byte-identical** with pre-D-288. The wire is DORMANT until 4f.2b's helper sets `'bva'`; `getattr` keeps hand-built / legacy bundles (no slot) working. **PIECE 2 (NOT built here):** the bva-authoring helper — deferred to 4f.2b. **PIECE 3 — the D-234 batch-notify discriminator (closes the D-284 deferred gap):** the unattended-run failure notify (`consumer.py`, D-234) read `getattr(result, "evidence", None)` and so SKIPPED a `RunAllResult` (a batch has `.probes`/`.batch_id`, NO `.evidence`) — a run-all batch with failing probes would silently not notify (flagged in D-284's scope-out). The hook now discriminates on `hasattr(result, "batch_id")` (the SAME duck-type as 4e's `_async_log_outcome`): a **batch** with `ran=True` and ANY failed/errored probe calls a new `notify_substrate_batch_failed`; the **single** path is the unchanged D-234 code in the `else` branch — **byte-identical** (reached for the single shape and for `result is None`). New `notify_substrate_batch_failed(tenant_id, *, batch_id, test_id, environment_id, failed_count, run_ids)` (`shared/notifications.py`) is a SIBLING of `notify_substrate_run_failed` (not a param-widening — keeps the scalar notifier + its tests untouched): a `ProbeRun` carries no per-probe error message or environment_id, so it reports `batch_id` + failed-probe count + the failing `run_ids`, with `test_id` + `environment_id` from the JOB; same best-effort discipline (never raises, quarantine-skip, brief public session for recipient resolution). **Documented over-notify:** the hook fires off RAW probe outcomes, not the bva *Verified* verdict (the decision engine computes that later, 4d), so a transient `errored` probe notifies even though a re-run might clear it — acceptable for an unattended-run alert; tightening to the verdict is deferred. **DORMANT for PIECE 1, REACHABLE-but-untriggered for PIECE 3:** nothing records `'bva'` yet, so no batch runs come through the queue → the batch branch is exercised only by tests until 4f.2b+4f.3 author + run a bva claim. **Decision-NEUTRAL — no decision-engine touch, so no byte-identical re-derivation needed** (unlike 4f.1): the diff does not touch `substrate_decision.py`; PIECE 1's only decision-path effect is "claims still carry NULL strategy_kind" (already proven byte-identical in 4f.1's gate). **Verification:** full unit suite **3324** green (3310 + 14 new: 1 emission-slot default-None across all 4 negative shapes; 4 persistence-threading via a fake Coordinator — `'bva'` threads, explicit `None` threads, legacy-no-slot → `None`, same-hash no-op still passes the kind + writes no recipe; 9 notify — 4 `notify_substrate_batch_failed` (recipients/body/extras, quarantine-skip, no-recipients no-op, never-raises-on-db-error) + 5 consumer discriminator (batch failed-probe → batch sibling fires + single does NOT; errored-probe counts; all-passed → neither; not-ran → no notify; single shape → run_failed fires + batch sibling does NOT)); boot clean; diff = `generation/emission.py` + `generation/persistence.py` + `execution_engine/consumer.py` + `shared/notifications.py` (+ the 3 test files) ONLY — no schema, no migration, no decision engine, no authoring helper, no run path. Scope OUT (deferred): **4f.2a** — settle which S2 claim a constraint-bva realizes (claim_kind; how accept+reject probes both realize one claim; how it grounds from S1 bounds) — lean: a behavioral value-constraint claim, NOT the metadata property-claim; **4f.2b** — the guarded bva-authoring helper that stamps `EmissionBundle.strategy_kind='bva'` (after 4f.2a); **4f.3** — the gated single-claim LIVE flip (approve/enqueue/run on env-59, watched). See D-234 / D-284 / D-285.

## D-289 — bva implementation intentionally suspended at the architecture boundary (NOT unfinished work). The bva/evaluation-strategy execution pipeline is COMPLETE to the extent possible without resolving claim/evaluation semantics: both strategy arms (single 2a / bva 4a), the decision-engine Verified seam + bva branch (4b/4d), the run-all execution path + batch manifest (3.1–3.4/4c.0), the completeness reader (4c.1), the async companion (4e), the strategy_kind column + EmissionBundle slot + batch-notify (4f.0/4f.1/4f.2-prep) — ALL built, tested, and DORMANT (nothing writes strategy_kind='bva'; every claim routes single; zero live behavior change; zero Salesforce cost). Everything shipped is DECISION-NEUTRAL, so it does not bias the eventual claim model. The next step (4f.2a) is NOT implementation — it is a core modelling decision (what is the identity of a constraint/bva claim; how a mixed-polarity probe set relates to one canonical claim; whether bva is a new claim_kind or an evaluation strategy over an existing claim), which would COMMIT the architecture and touches the parked semantic_conditions / IDENTITY_HASH_VERSION work. Per the roadmap (S4 is the keystone; every strategy executes through it), bva is left dormant and effort returns to S4 proper. When bva resumes, frame it as 'what is the relationship between a claim and an evaluation strategy?' (not 'how do we build bva') and open it as a dedicated, TA-pressure-tested architecture review — NOT a build. Resumption is gated on a mature S4 execution/interpretation foundation. See ADR-001 (D-270), evaluation-semantics-v1 (D-272), D-273 through D-288.

## D-290 — S4 prohibition grading recognizes permission-based rejections (403/INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS) as the org enforcing the prohibition (S4 foundational correctness, slice F-c from the S4 keystone recon). A prohibition-shaped data-recipe expects the org to REJECT a mutation; S4's grade treated **only** a VR-shaped rejection (HTTP 400 + a structured error code) as the prohibition being correctly enforced (→ `passed`). An **FLS/sharing rejection** — the org enforcing a prohibition by *access control* rather than a validation rule — can surface as **HTTP 403** and so fell to the "non-2xx, non-400 → couldn't-attempt → `errored`" branch: a whole class of permission-based negatives mis-graded as `errored` ("we couldn't evaluate") instead of `passed` ("the org enforced it"). D-225 already surfaced the structured FLS signal (the access-denial `errorCode`s, enumerated in `failure_taxonomy._PERMISSION_CODES`); this slice extends the **grade** to consume it. **The fix (two mirror sites, `data_executor.py`):** `_run_create` (1-step create-rejected, where the create IS the prohibited action) and `_run_mutation_attempt` (the prohibited update/delete, D-203) each gain — *before* the final `errored` branch, *after* the unchanged HTTP-400 business-rejection branch — a permission-rejection branch that routes through the SAME 4-way grade as a 400 VR (`_matches(expect_rejection, body)` → `passed` iff matched, else `failed`). So a permission rejection that MATCHES the recipe's expectation → `passed` (the prohibition holds); a mutation that SUCCEEDS when it should reject → still `failed` + the leaked record deleted (unchanged); a rejection of the WRONG kind / mismatched expectation → `failed` (never silently passed); a genuine couldn't-attempt (transport/transient) → still `errored`. **The discriminator + over-broadening guard (`_is_permission_rejection`):** a rejection reclassifies ONLY when its body carries an `errorCode` the failure taxonomy classifies as `FailureCategory.PERMISSION` (the unambiguous D-225 access-denial signal) — consuming the taxonomy's classification, NOT re-parsing raw HTTP/status. A **bare 403** with no recognized permission code (API-disabled, IP-range, empty body — which classify `unknown`) is NOT reclassified; it stays `errored`. This is the honesty guard: a wrong optimistic-`pass` is worse than the original `errored` mis-grade, so anything short of "the org unambiguously enforced THIS prohibition by access control" stays errored. **No S2 schema / RejectionExpectation extension:** `RejectionExpectation` is scalars-only (`error_code` + `error_message_pattern`); a permission-prohibition recipe expresses its expectation by setting `error_code` to the permission code (e.g. `INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS`), which the existing `_matches` already honors — code-only, **no migration**. **VR path byte-identical:** the permission branch is only reached for non-400 statuses, so the 400 VR grade is untouched (proven by the unchanged VR tests + an explicit byte-identity test). **D-273 (indeterminate/permanent) intact, no collision:** a graded-`passed` permission rejection is never `errored`, so it never reaches the errored-only indeterminate/permanent split; the rejection-expecting path (`_run_create`/`_run_mutation_attempt`) is structurally distinct from the POSITIVE path (where a permission denial on a create we wanted to succeed correctly stays `errored` → indeterminate / environment-not-satisfiable, D-272 §2.4) — the same `errorCode` carries two meanings disambiguated by *which function* (does the recipe expect a rejection) handles it; the positive path is untouched. The 2-step **setup** create (`execute_data_recipe`, the non-violating staging create) is also untouched — a permission denial there is a staging failure → `errored` (`SetupRejected`), never the graded prohibition. **Verification:** genuine before→after on the SAME synthetic input (stash-proven — `403 + INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS, recipe expects it`: `main` → `errored`, branch → `passed`); 11 new unit tests (permission-403→passed for create + update + delete; permission-400-already-business; wrong-kind→failed; ambiguous-403→errored + bare-403-no-code→errored, the guard; VR-400 byte-identical; the `_is_permission_rejection` discriminator unit across all permission codes vs VR/normalization/transient/no-code); full unit suite **3335** green; boot clean; diff = `data_executor.py` (+58) + 2 test files only — no schema, no migration, no S2 change, no other capability work. This changes a real verdict (errored→passed for permission-prohibition negatives), so it is a LIVE-correctness change, gated at push on an adversarial review of the over-broadening guard + the VR byte-identity + the D-273 interaction. The other DEFERRED capability edges (matches_pattern/not_equals predicates, is_required/field_type properties, ui/event/callout executors) are NOT this slice. See D-203 / D-225 / D-272 / D-273.

## D-290.1 — adversarial-review hardening of the permission-rejection guard (tighten the code set + gate on HTTP 403). The pre-push adversarial review of D-290 (4 independent skeptics, one per claim) cleared the VR byte-identity, the positive/setup-create isolation + D-273 interaction, and the wrong-kind/no-leak claims, but **broke the over-broadening guard**: D-290 reclassified on `category_for(None, code) == FailureCategory.PERMISSION`, i.e. the FULL `_PERMISSION_CODES` set — which is sized for **sync data-loss detection**, not prohibition grading. Two defects: **(1) the dual-meaning code.** `INVALID_FIELD_FOR_INSERT_UPDATE` is a taxonomy permission code, but Salesforce returns it for an FLS denial **AND** for a STRUCTURALLY non-writable field (a formula / roll-up / auto-number / system audit field). A prohibition recipe expecting that code would grade `passed` when the org returned it for the non-permission (structural) reason — a **false `passed`**, the exact optimistic mis-grade the honesty guard claims to prevent. **(2) status-blindness.** `_is_permission_rejection` inspected only the body, never `http_status`, so the permission branch fired for ANY non-2xx-non-400 status — a transient 5xx / 429 whose multi-error body happened to carry a permission sub-error (e.g. `[SERVER_UNAVAILABLE, INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS]`) would be reclassified as a business outcome, **losing the re-runnable (indeterminate, D-272/D-273) signal**. **The fix (root, two parts, `data_executor.py`):** (a) the discriminator now reclassifies on the UNAMBIGUOUS access-denial family only — a taxonomy PERMISSION code **MINUS** `_AMBIGUOUS_PERMISSION_CODES = {INVALID_FIELD_FOR_INSERT_UPDATE}` — leaving the `INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS*` family (INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS / _OR_READONLY / _FIELD_ACCESS / _ON_CROSS_REFERENCE_ENTITY), which all literally mean "insufficient access"; the dual-meaning code stays `errored` (honest-uncertainty); (b) both grading sites (`_run_create`, `_run_mutation_attempt`) gate the new branch on `http_status == _PERMISSION_REJECTION_STATUS` (403) — a 400 + INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS is ALREADY the VR business-rejection path, and a permission/FLS denial on a data mutation surfaces as 403, so gating on EXACTLY 403 keeps transient (5xx/429) / auth (401) responses — even with a permission sub-error in the body — on the `errored` path. This still **consumes** the taxonomy's classification (it remains the upper bound) rather than re-parsing raw HTTP; the 403 gate is a refinement, not a raw-status re-parse. The third amplifier the review noted — a message-pattern-only `RejectionExpectation` (`error_code=None`) making `_matches` code_ok unconditionally True — is PRE-EXISTING `_matches` behavior (identical on the 400 VR path), not introduced by D-290, and is now bounded to a genuine 403 access-denial with an author-chosen pattern; left as-is (out of scope, the established 4-way-grade contract). **Verification:** the legitimate case is unchanged (403 + INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS, expected → `passed`, stash-proven before→after still holds); 2 new unit tests encode the reviewer's exact breaks — `INVALID_FIELD_FOR_INSERT_UPDATE` at 403, even when expected → `errored`; a 503 multi-error body carrying `INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS` → `errored` (the status gate); the `_is_permission_rejection` guard-unit updated (the dual-meaning code now → False); full unit suite green; diff = `data_executor.py` (the helper + 2 call-site gates + 2 constants) + the 2 test files. No schema, no migration. The adversarial review caught a real false-`passed` vector BEFORE it shipped — the review investment paid for itself on a live-verdict change. See D-290.

## D-291 — S1 close-on-change fixes the asymmetric edge-close that leaves source-dangling current edges (root cause + env-59 twin-guarded history backfill). A read-only diagnostic (env-59, HEAD `72671e5`) found **55 source-dangling current edges** — a current edge (`valid_to_seq IS NULL`) whose `source_entity_id` references an entity-version row that is no longer current. **Root cause:** `edges.source_entity_id`/`target_entity_id` FK the entity-**VERSION** surrogate PK (`REFERENCES entities(id)`, where `id` is per-version), NOT a stable identity. The sync change path (`materialize.py:201-210`) handles a re-versioned (attribute-only-changed) entity by `_batch_close_superseded(prior_ids)` + `_batch_insert_new_entities` — **and does nothing to the prior version's edges**. The edge phase (`materialize_edges_for_entities` → `batched_materialize_edges`) re-materializes the **new** version's outbound edges fresh (its existing-edge read is keyed `WHERE source_entity_id = <new id>`, so the new version starts edge-empty → all outbound inserted = the healthy twins), but the **old** version's outbound edges (`source_entity_id = <old id>`) are invisible to that diff and are **never closed**. The ONLY path that closes a superseded entity's edges is the **deletion** reconcile (`_close_edges_for_entities`, sole call site `:792`) — which fires on SF deletion, not on re-version. So every source re-version leaks the prior version's outbound edges as current → source-danglers. (Inbound edges from unchanged neighbors are structurally re-pointed under a full fetch — the neighbor is in the fetch set, the diff resolves the target to current and closes `Y→X_old`/inserts `Y→X_new` — so env-59's full-fetch reconcile leaves only a transient 1 target-dangler; a delta-only sync would leak inbound, a distinct class.) **Characterization (env-59, identity = `COALESCE(sf_id, entity_type||':'||sf_api_name)` within `connected_org`):** all 55 are **B1 stale dups** — each has a **healthy current twin** (a current edge whose source identity's current version + target identity match), so closing all 55 loses **zero** relationships (blast radius D9 = 0). Verified directly on the VR `Opportunity.Contract_Value_Required_On_Closed_Won` (old v43→66 + current v66→open, both APPLIES_TO/BELONGS_TO have a dangling + a healthy current edge) and a NULL-sf_id Field. **Reader insulation (why this is latent, not active):** both S4 (`world.py` → `SemanticOrgModel` `get_related`) and S6 (`s1_reader.py` → `get_related`) read edges ONLY through the canonical reader; the only raw `FROM edges` reads are sync-side (`derivation.py`, write-side). The reader (`query.py:359-369`) requires the edge current (`_as_of('e')`), the far entity current (`_as_of('t')` join), and the near id = the caller's current entity id — so a source-dangling edge is filtered out either by the near-id mismatch (outbound) or the far-currency join (inbound). The 55 are a stored-history blemish, not a corrupting read. **Forward fix (root-cause, no reader workaround):** close-on-change, **OUTBOUND-only**. `_close_edges_for_entities` gains an `endpoints: str = "both"` param — `"both"` keeps the existing either-endpoint WHERE (the deletion call site `:792` is byte-unchanged at the default), `"source"` closes only `source_entity_id = ANY(...)`. The change path, immediately after `_batch_close_superseded` for `buckets.changed`, calls `_close_edges_for_entities(conn, ctx, prior_ids, endpoints="source")` at the SAME close seq (`ctx.logical_version_seq`) and on the SAME conn / same phase transaction as the entity supersession + edge phase. **Outbound-only over either-endpoint — deliberate:** closing the prior version's *inbound* edges (`target = prior`) from the changed entity's phase risks a cross-phase ordering orphan — if neighbor `Y`'s phase already ran this sync, closing `Y→X_old` here leaves `Y→X_new` uninserted until the next sync; a clean ownership model has each entity close its OWN outbound on re-version, with inbound being the neighbor's responsibility (matching today's full-fetch re-point). **Backfill (one-time, env-59-scoped, twin-guarded = loss-free by construction):** an alembic data-migration closes ONLY the P2 twin-guarded set (every current source-dangling edge in `connected_org=902850e3-…` that has a healthy current twin), at the **bitemporally-correct** seq — `valid_to_seq = the edge's own source version's `valid_to_seq`` (the seq that source version retired; equals the current version's `valid_from_seq` in the 2-version case), NOT "now". P3 (no-twin) edges are left untouched. Forward-only history correction; down = documented no-op (do NOT reopen). **Deferred (NOT pulled forward):** (a) store-wide twin-guarded backfill of the remaining ~4138 source-danglers (~4193 store-wide minus env-59's 55) — bucket first, D9=0 is proven for env-59 ONLY; (b) the target-re-version-under-delta inbound-dangler class — a structural neighbor re-point, distinct from this outbound fix; (c) the edge-FK-→-identity re-architecture (point edges at a stable identity rather than the version surrogate) — a standalone S1 hardening decision. Three commits on `phase-s1-edge-close-on-change` (design / forward-fix / migration); not merged.

## D-292 — S7 `/ask` org-scopes its S1 reader through the shared D-286 resolver (fixes the cross-org blend on a multi-org tenant; env-None → a graceful in-band refusal, never a 500). The conversation bridge (`intelligence/conversation_bridge.py`) opened a tenant connection and built `s1 = SemanticOrgModel(conn)` **org-less** (`:102`), even though the question's `environment_id` was already threaded all the way to it (route → `answer_question(environment_id=…)` → `QuestionContext.environment_id`, `:98`). `SemanticOrgModel` with `connected_org_id=None` omits the org predicate from every read (`_org_clause` → `None`), so a **name-resolving** retrieval — the EXPOSED path is `conversation/retrieval.py:144` `retrieve_impact` → `s1.get_entities("Object", filters={"sf_api_name": …})` + `get_related` — returns rows across **all** orgs on the tenant and blends them. On tenant_1 (env-59 `902850e3-…` + env-78 `6af2fa4b-…`, **146 shared Object api-names**) this is live-exploitable: a question naming a shared Object grounds its answer over a 2-org union → ambiguous reference, the same break class D-286 fixed for S3 generation (the req-283 break). This is one of the **four residual org-blind `SemanticOrgModel(conn)` consumers** characterized after D-286; S7 `/ask` is the only **mechanical, EXPOSED, live** one (the route already threads env — the reader just ignored it), so it is fixed first and alone. **The fix (root-cause, one resolver — not two; no reader-convention workaround):** inside the existing `with get_tenant_connection(tenant_id) as conn:` block, before constructing `s1`, resolve env→org through the **shared D-286 resolver** `resolve_connected_org_or_raise(conn, environment_id)` (`sync/credentials.py:140`, the SAME symbol S3 generation imports — `run.py:30`/`:75`) and build `SemanticOrgModel(conn, connected_org_id=org_id)`. No second resolver, no S7-local org lookup. **The env-None contract (a real, normal mode — not an edge case):** `views.py` (the SOLE caller, `:353`) deliberately sets `env_id = None` (`:348`) whenever the caller lacks access to the requested environment (the D-245 env-scope guard drops an out-of-scope filter), then passes `environment_id=None`. So the bridge receives `None` routinely. The bug the per-org work removes is precisely org-blind grounding on a multi-org tenant — so falling back to org-agnostic on `None` would **re-introduce the blend** the fix removes. Instead, `environment_id is None` returns a NEW structured **graceful in-band refusal** `_no_org()` — the existing `available: True, status: "refused"` shape (the same shape `no_intent_match` uses, `:78-79`: five keys `available`/`status`/`text`/`refusal_reason`/`citations`), with `refusal_reason="environment_required"` and a plain-text ask to pick a connected environment. It is deliberately the `available: True` (graceful, expected) shape, **not** `_unavailable()` (`available: False`, which means the service itself is down) and **never** a raw exception / HTTP 500. **Resolver-raise = the same refusal:** an env that is present but **unprovisioned** (no connected_org yet) makes the resolver raise `OrgResolutionError` (`credentials.py:32/152`); the bridge **catches that one exception** and returns the SAME `_no_org()` refusal (the user-facing answer is identical — "no usable connected org to ground against" — and there is no 500). Every OTHER failure (absent tenant schema, read error, LLM error) still falls through to the pre-existing outer `except Exception` → `_unavailable()`, byte-unchanged. **Isolation guarantee (so a revert is one line):** the org guard is the only added control flow in the connection block; reverting to the org-agnostic blend is a single-line change — delete the `is None` guard + the `OrgResolutionError` catch and restore `s1 = SemanticOrgModel(conn)`. **No schema, no migration, no S2/route/template change** — the route already passes `environment_id`; the fix is `conversation_bridge.py` only (the org-resolve + the `_no_org()` helper + the `OrgResolutionError` import) plus its bridge tests. **Verification:** three behavioral tests on the bridge — (1) env-selected resolves to ONE org (the reader is constructed with the resolver's `connected_org_id`, not org-less → no cross-org blend); (2) env-None → the `_no_org()` graceful refusal (`available: True`, `status: "refused"`, `refusal_reason="environment_required"`), no exception; (3) resolver-raise (`OrgResolutionError`) → the SAME `_no_org()` refusal, no 500; plus boot-clean and the bridge/conversation test scope green. **Deferred (the other three org-blind consumers — NOT pulled forward, each its own decision):** (a) the **sync console** browser (`s1_sync_console.py:301`) — NEEDS-DECISION (it has no single env in scope; lean = an env-scoped browser with a picker, not an auto-resolve); (b) the **decision engine** version-pin (`substrate_decision.py:173`, only `current_version_seq()`, a scalar — NOT name-resolving, so not the same exposure; low-stakes); (c) **S8 recompute** (`evolution/recompute.py:167`) — already GUARDED by the D-265 `org_count > 1` refuse. The eval harness (`generation/eval/runner.py`) is org-less but non-prod (single-org fixtures), excluded. Two commits on `phase-s7-ask-org-scope` (design / fix); not pushed, not merged. See D-286 (the shared resolver + the per-org break) / D-245 (the env-scope guard that produces env-None) / D-265 (the S8 multi-org guardrail).

## D-292.1 — adversarial review reframes the env-None refusal as a deliberate product stance (`/ask` is strictly environment-scoped) + the env selector becomes `required`. A pre-push adversarial review (4 independent skeptics, one per claim) of the D-292 fix found the org-scoping itself sound (the reader is genuinely org-bound and no org-less reader survives on the live path — verdict HOLDS) and the no-500 / test-soundness claims clean (two minor caveats, below), but **broke the "env-None refusal is correctly scoped" claim (verdict BROKEN, major)**: the env-None gate sits at the top of `answer_question` and refuses **all three** S7 intents, yet only **one** uses the org-scoped `s1`. Ground-truth confirmation in `conversation/retrieval.py`: `retrieve_failure_cause` (`:107`, S6 — reads only `session` scoped by `recipe_id`) and `retrieve_grounding_drift` (`:121`, S8 — reads only `session` scoped by `test_id`) take `s1` but **never use it**; only `retrieve_impact`'s **object branch** (`:138`, already guarded by `s1 is not None`) does the name-resolving `s1.get_entities`/`get_related` — the sole blend-prone read (its requirement branch `:150` uses `session`, not `s1`). The existing test `test_answered_failure_cause_over_seeded_s6` proves the env-blind faculty answers with `s1=None`. So the all-or-nothing gate strands the two env-independent intents on a tenant whose `/ask` env selector defaults empty and was **not** `required` (`conversation.html`). **The fork (surfaced to AK, who decided):** (A) push the gate down to only `retrieve_impact`'s object branch — answer the env-independent intents org-blind, decline only the object lookup; vs (B) keep the refuse-all gate AND make `/ask` strictly environment-scoped. **AK chose (B):** `/ask` answers are always grounded in **one** connected org — the S6 failure-cause and S8 grounding-drift questions now require an env too, a deliberate stricter posture over the S7-default env-blind answering. Two consequences: (1) the D-292 refuse-all gate in `conversation_bridge.answer_question` STANDS unchanged (it IS the product gate); the env-None / OrgResolutionError → `_no_org()` (`available:True`, `refusal_reason="environment_required"`) is the no-access / programmatic **backstop**, not the happy path. (2) `conversation.html`'s env `<select>` gains `required` with a `disabled selected` placeholder (a round-tripped valid env still pre-selects — last `selected` in document order wins), so the UI forces an env before submit. **Architecture note — the gate is a v1-bridge product policy, not a substrate change:** the pure inner `_answer(s1=None, …)` still answers the env-independent intents (the faculty is unchanged, still tested green); only the v1 wrapper `answer_question` enforces "env required for `/ask`". **The two review caveats (both no-code-change-needed, one folded into tests):** (i) a resolver failure that is NOT `OrgResolutionError` (e.g. a transient DB fault inside `get_connected_org_for_environment`'s SELECT) is correctly caught by the outer `except Exception` → `_unavailable()` (a service condition, retry — not a missing-org one); now pinned by a new test (`test_answer_question_unavailable_when_resolver_db_errors`). (ii) an ordering nicety — a fabricated positive-but-unprovisioned tenant with `environment_id=None` would hit the env-None refusal before the missing-schema query errors, returning `environment_required` instead of `unavailable`; NOT reachable via the sole real caller (`views.py` derives `tenant_id` from the authenticated JWT, so a logged-in user always has a provisioned schema), so left as-is. **Test hardenings folded in:** the bad-tenant test now pins `refusal_reason == "unavailable"` (was `available is False` only — could pass-stale); + the non-`OrgResolutionError` → `_unavailable()` test above. The 3 D-292 behavioral tests are unchanged and remain correct under (B) — env-None refusing a failure-cause question is now the **intended** strict behavior, not a regression. **Isolation (still one line):** to instead adopt fork (A) later, pass `s1 = None` when `environment_id is None` (the object branch declines on its own guard; the env-independent intents answer) — recorded in the bridge comment. **Diff:** `conversation_bridge.py` (comment only — the gate is byte-unchanged from D-292) + `conversation.html` (`required` + placeholder) + `test_s7_bridge.py` (1 new test + 1 hardened assert). No schema, no migration. The adversarial review changed the *framing* (over-scoping → deliberate product scope) and the *UI contract* (selector now required), not the backend gate. See D-292.

## D-293 — Behaviour-bearing condition for prohibition claims: the business state becomes identity-bearing (refines the Option-C invariant of D-110.3); on an incomplete behaviour instance, refuse — never silently degrade to a generic inspection.

**Date:** 2026-06-30 · **Status:** active (refines D-110.3). Design commit; the prohibition-first implementation follows as a separate commit.

**Context.** Generating req-302 ("Home Loan Opportunity Qualification") collapsed three distinct business rules — AC1 (Loan Amount mandatory), AC2 (Loan Amount > Property Value rejected), AC4 (no stage progress to Credit Assessment without KYC + Credit Score) — into **one** prohibition claim (observed live: `test_id` `363bb318` appears 3× in `claims_written`; `asserted_truth.operation=modify_record`, `expected_rejection={FIELD_CUSTOM_VALIDATION_EXCEPTION, field=null, message=null}`, `semantic_conditions=[]`). Mechanism: `_author_negative` (`generation/emission.py:766-819`) authors **every** prohibition condition-free with a generic rejection **by design** — the **Option-C identity_hash invariant** (D-110.3): the violating payload lives in the *recipe* so the claim body is byte-identical and `identity_hash` is recipe-rewrite-stable (`emission.py:778/810`; guarded by `tests/unit/generation/test_behavioral_negative_emission.py`). Since `compute_identity_hash = archetype + claim_kind + canonical(asserted_truth) + canonical(semantic_conditions)` (`test_representation/identity_hash.py:116-121`), three condition-free prohibitions on `Opportunity` hash identically → dedup to one. The D-247 `coverage_map` reported AC1/2/4 "covered" because it counts AC-intents *tagged*, not distinct grounded claims — masking the collapse. Net: three different assertions reduced to one generic "a VR APPLIES_TO Opportunity" inspection recipe. **Diagnosis:** "reject save when Loan Amount is blank" and "reject save when Loan > Property" are different *assertions*, not different *realisations* of one assertion (each can independently pass/fail). Option-C drew the State/Value line in the wrong place — it pushed both the business **state** and the violating **value** into the recipe.

**Decision (refines D-110.3; does NOT abandon recipe-stability).** (1) **The business STATE is identity-bearing.** A prohibition claim authors a populated `semantic_conditions` capturing the condition under which the rejection is asserted (derived from the grounded VR's scope/trigger). Distinct conditions ⇒ distinct `identity_hash` ⇒ distinct claims. The violating **VALUE/payload stays operational** (in the recipe). The line: **State → claim (identity); Value → recipe (operational).** (2) **Refuse, never silently degrade.** A Behaviour-Instance completeness gate before grounding: a prohibition / prevent-transition intent must carry Action + Business State + a derivable Observable; when the state is not determinable (or no violation is derivable for a behavioural recipe), the substrate **refuses** (`no_admissible_test` / a new `behaviour_incomplete` refusal) and surfaces the BA-facing reason via the D-247 coverage/refusal surface — it does **not** emit the generic caveated-inspection prohibition. Extends the D-247 honesty discipline from coverage to authoring. (3) **No `IDENTITY_HASH_VERSION` bump.** The canonicalisation policy (v1) is unchanged; only the *inputs* are richer (non-empty conditions). Old condition-free prohibition claims keep their v1 hashes; regenerated condition-bearing claims are distinct and supersede them via the normal draft → approve → deprecate path. No re-hash migration. (4) **Replace the Option-C stability test** (`test_behavioral_negative_emission.py`) with one asserting **both**: state-distinct ⇒ identity-distinct (the new guarantee) **and** value-rewrite under the *same* state ⇒ identity-stable (the preserved Option-C property).

**Reconciliation with D-110.3 / Option-C.** D-110.3's goal — a claim's identity stays stable when S8 rewrites its recipe — is **preserved**: S8 rewrites the violating *value* (operational), never the asserted *state*. D-110.3 erred only in treating the *state* as operational; the state is part of the claim's meaning. This refines the State/Value boundary; it does not reverse recipe-stability.

**Scope — prohibition-first.** Applies to `prohibition-claim` (create-rejected + the D-203 update/stage-rejected shape). Explicitly **out of scope** (each its own later decision): (a) **violation-derivation breadth** — even with a populated state, a prohibition gets a *behavioural* recipe only when the VR formula is numeric-derivable; `NOT-ISBLANK` / picklist / cross-field hit `_Undecidable` (`verified_negative.py:196/211/218`) and under decision-2 now **refuse** (honest) rather than degrade; widening derivation so boolean/cross-field rules (the AC1/AC4 mandatory-field + KYC-gate class) get behavioural recipes is a separate follow-on; (b) **bva / boundary analysis** stays parked (D-289); (c) `value-claim` / `state-transition` / `automation-effect` authoring unchanged (they already carry their own state/observable); (d) new archetypes (approval, notification, formula-output, journey) untouched.

**Consequence on req-302 (acceptance gate).** AC1/2/4 → three **distinct** prohibition claims (each with its own business state), or **honest refusals** for non-numeric VRs (until derivation widens) — never one collapsed generic claim. AC3 → refused (recalculation is not an existence claim), not degraded to existence. AC9 → still honestly refused (no approval archetype).

**Verification.** Unit (offline, no LLM/DB, like the D-247 enforcer tests): distinct states ⇒ distinct `identity_hash` (no collapse); an incomplete behaviour instance ⇒ refusal, not an inspection recipe; the replaced stability test. Live (deployed env, where creds exist): regenerate req-302 → assert AC1/2/4 distinctness / honest refusals and AC3 not existence-degraded.

**Code loci for the implementation that follows (not part of this decision).** `emission.py:766-819` (`_author_negative` — populate `semantic_conditions` from the grounded state; flip the no-derivation fallback from caveated-inspection to refuse); `governance_core._evaluate_negative` (the completeness gate); `test_behavioral_negative_emission.py` (replace the stability assertion). No schema, no migration. See D-110.3 (Option-C origin) · D-247 (the coverage/honesty discipline this extends to authoring) · D-289 (the parked bva arc this does not unpark).

## D-294 — Violation-derivation breadth: field-metadata-driven derivation for non-numeric VR shapes (the D-293 out-of-scope follow-on). Refuse stays the floor; S3 synthesizes the violating value from grounding-time S1 metadata.

**Date:** 2026-07-01 · **Status:** active (follows D-293; the D-293 §Scope-(a) follow-on). Design commit; the sliced impl follows as separate commits.

**Context.** D-293 made a prohibition with no *derivable* behavioural reject recipe REFUSE (`behaviour-incomplete`) instead of degrading. It explicitly deferred **violation-derivation breadth** (§Scope-(a)). Today `generation/verified_negative.py` derives a violating payload only for **field-vs-literal comparisons + plain `ISBLANK`/`ISPICKVAL`** (already live). It returns `NotDerivable` on: **field-to-field / cross-field** `Loan__c > Property__c` (`_orient`, line 181-182 — this is **req-302 AC2**); **`NOT(ISBLANK)`** (line 211, the "must be non-blank" mandatory shape); **`NOT(ISPICKVAL)`** (line 218); **bare boolean field** (`_satisfy`, line 137). Under D-293 those `NotDerivable`s become honest refusals via the `prohibition_recipe_derivable` gate (`emission.py:741`). **Diagnosis:** the refusals are a *missing-data* problem, not a certainty-bar problem — `derive()` has no field metadata (type; picklist values; both-operands-numeric). Grounding already resolves the fields; give `derive()` the read-only metadata and each violating value becomes **certain** with real data.

**Decision.** (1) **S3 synthesizes the violating value from grounding-time metadata** (approach A). Governance threads a new read-only `GroundedNegative.field_metadata` (bare-field-keyed `{field_type, length, is_calculated, picklist_values|None}`), read via a `_grounding_field_metadata` helper mirroring `_grounding_vr_formulas` (bulk `SemanticOrgModel.get_entity_details` + the `get_picklist_values` 2-hop, the pattern in `evolution/s1_reader.py`). `derive`/`derive_update`/`_satisfy*`/`_orient` gain a `field_metadata=None` param threaded through; **absent/insufficient metadata refuses exactly as today** (the certainty bar is preserved, not relaxed). (2) **Rejected approach B (S4-realizes an abstract `FieldConstraint`).** B honours a stricter reading of k16 but costs a new S2 recipe-body model, an S4 realizer, a wider recipe contract, and new `s1`-reader plumbing on the `s1`-less 1-step create-rejected path (`run.py`); B's own design flagged that plumbing as a HOLD. A leaves S4, the recipe models, the emission couriers, the D-293 gate, and the DB schema **unchanged** (all verified payload-agnostic). (3) **k16 reconciliation.** k16 is the *positive-path executor* boundary (S4 must not pick a value-claim's value-under-test). This is the **negative** vertical at **grounding** time: `GroundedNegative`'s violating value is *already S3-derived* (`emission.py:232`, "derived via D-107"; contrast `GroundedPositive`'s verbatim value) — widening `derive()` derives *more shapes*, moving nothing to S4. S3 already reads S1 at grounding (`_grounding_vr_formulas` reads attributes; `_ground_rejection_conditions` reads Field entities); reading `field_details.field_type`/picklist is the same character of read, at the same pinned version, no live-org effect. The value still rides the **recipe** (not the claim); `identity_hash` is unchanged. **The one widening this decision makes explicit:** S3's grounding reads grow from VR-formula-text + BELONGS_TO to include read-only `field_details` type/picklist metadata. (4) **Polarity is self-checked.** Each derived payload is verified against the existing `evaluate` primitive (`semantic/formula/eval.py`, three-valued Kleene) before it is returned — for `NOT(ISBLANK)`, `NOT(ISPICKVAL)`, and bare-boolean; **cross-field is `NonEvaluable`** there, so its correctness rests on the deterministic ordered-pair construction (from the parsed operator) + the live run + the 4-way grade's `error_code` match (a wrong-reason rejection grades `failed`, never `passed`). (5) **No `IDENTITY_HASH_VERSION` bump, no schema, no migration** — metadata is read at grounding, never stored, and does not enter `identity_hash`.

**Two forks settled.** (a) **Field-name key** — S1 stores fields object-qualified (`Opportunity.Loan__c`) but the formula parser/recipe speak bare (`path[0]`). Key the metadata dict by bare name; the derive lookup tries `path[0]` then `path[-1]` (dual-lookup) to survive a self-qualifying VR formula. (b) **Shared synthesizer** — extract `safe_nonblank_value(field_type, length)` from `execution_engine/world.py:_fill_value` into a neutral home so S3 (derivation) and S4 (padding) do not drift; if extraction crosses a boundary awkwardly, a small local copy in `verified_negative.py` is the fallback.

**Scope.** The four shapes above. **Out of scope** (stay honest refusals): org-state functions (`ISCHANGED`/`PRIORVALUE`), cross-object refs (`Account.Industry`), unparsed formulas (`REGEX`/`CASE`/…), multipicklist, inline picklists S1 did not capture, and `is_calculated`/non-writable fields. The systematic boundary/bva threshold **sets** remain the parked D-289 arc — this decision unblocks the *lone* cross-field negative, not the just-below/at/just-above set.

**Consequence on req-302 (acceptance gate).** AC2 (`Loan__c > Property__c`) → a **distinct cross-field behavioural reject-test**, not a refusal; AC1 (mandatory) and AC4 (KYC gate) derive too — closing D-293's "AC1/2/4 → distinct claims OR honest refusals" onto **three distinct behavioural claims**. Each runs live and the org's real rejection grades `passed`.

**Verification.** Unit (offline): the metadata-free refusals in `test_verified_negative.py` (lines 89/103/116) stay `NotDerivable`; new metadata-bearing overloads derive the correct payload; insufficient metadata (one non-numeric cross-field operand / single-value picklist / `is_calculated`) refuses; every `evaluate`-able payload asserts the expected polarity. Governance/emission flips only in metadata-bearing overloads (`test_governance_unit.py` truth-table + the `behaviour_incomplete` refusal; `test_behavioral_negative_emission.py`). Corpus fixtures for the four shapes. Live: regenerate req-302 on env-59 (AC2 → distinct cross-field claim, run green).

**Code loci for the implementation that follows (not part of this decision).** `verified_negative.py` (the four `NotDerivable` branches → metadata-backed derivation); `governance_core.py` (`_grounding_field_metadata` + thread it); `emission.py:200` (`GroundedNegative.field_metadata` slot) + `_derive_prohibition_recipe:712` (signature). Reuse (do not duplicate): `semantic/query.py` `get_entity_details`/`get_picklist_values` (+ `_bulk`), `evolution/s1_reader.py` (the 2-hop), `world.py:_fill_value`/`_NUMERIC` (→ shared `safe_nonblank_value`), `semantic/formula/eval.py:evaluate` (polarity self-check). Sliced dormant-first: rail (dormant) → cross-field (AC2) → NOT-ISBLANK + bare-boolean → NOT-ISPICKVAL → live req-302. See D-293 (the refuse-not-degrade this widens) · D-107 (the verified-vs-derivable gate) · D-110.3 (value rides the recipe) · D-289 (the parked bva/boundary sets) · k16 (the positive-path executor boundary this does not touch).

## D-295 — VR-to-claim alignment: ground each prohibition on the validation rule whose fields match the claim's conditions (deterministic field-overlap), refuse when none aligns. Unblocks D-294 by making the correct VR reachable; corrects D-294's AC2 acceptance gate.

**Date:** 2026-07-01 · **Status:** active (refines D-293 identity-selection; unblocks D-294 derivation-breadth). Design commit; the sliced impl follows as separate commits.

**Context.** Live regeneration of req-302 on prod tenant_1 (post D-293 `@4ad3c64` + D-294 `@a9e6c85`) produced two **distinct** prohibition claims — AC1 (`Loan_Type__c="Home Loan"` + `Loan_Amount__c is_null`, hash `a3498bf7`) and AC4 (`StageName="Credit Assessment"` + `KYC_Complete__c=false`, hash `ff08dd4a`), confirming D-293 de-collapse works live — but **both carry byte-identical recipes testing the WRONG rule**: create `{Opportunity.Amount:10000}` → update `{Amount:10001}`, `expect_rejection.error_code=FIELD_CUSTOM_VALIDATION_EXCEPTION` (verified in `test_recipes.observation_realization.steps`). That payload is the generic `Amount > 10000` VR, unrelated to either claim's asserted business rule. `Opportunity` carries 8 VRs; the rule matching each claim exists in S1 and was never selected — `Home_Loan_Required_Fields` (AC1), `Credit_Assessment_Prerequisites` (AC4), `Loan_Exceeds_Property_Value` (AC2), `Block_Approved_Without_Approval` (AC9).

**Root cause.** Grounding hands **every** VR formula on the subject object to derivation, and derivation returns the **first VR it can derive a violating payload for**. `_grounding_vr_formulas` (`governance_core.py:193`) returns a `tuple[str,...]` of ALL VR formula texts matching the Layer-1 `(edge_type, far_type)` dimension — no VR identity, order incidental to S1 traversal. `_derive_violation`/`_derive_update_violation` (`emission.py:696`/`:679`) iterate and return the first `Verified*`. On any multi-VR object the trivial numeric `Amount > 10000` derives first, so **every prohibition gets the same generic recipe regardless of the claim's asserted rule**. Two consequences: (a) recipes do not match claims; (b) **D-294's non-numeric shapes are dead code on any multi-VR object** — the numeric VR always wins the race, so the cross-field / bare-boolean / `NOT(ISBLANK)` / `NOT(ISPICKVAL)` branches never run. The "winner" is decided by S1 table-insertion order — a lucky-order bug, not a semantic choice. This is **pre-existing behaviour newly exposed by D-293** (which gave prohibitions distinctive conditions), not a regression of D-293/D-294.

**Decision.** (1) **Deterministic, grounding-time, S3-side VR-to-claim alignment.** A new pure helper `_align_vr_to_conditions(vr_formulas, grounded_conds)` narrows the candidate tuple to the single VR whose referenced fields best overlap the claim's D-293 grounded condition fields; when no VR aligns it returns `()`, driving the existing D-293 gate to REFUSE (`behaviour_incomplete`) rather than grounding a mismatched generic rule. **No LLM in the selection** — the LLM proposes the rule (already grounded to `semantic_conditions`), the substrate grounds it deterministically, the same division as everywhere else. (2) **Integration is upstream narrowing, not a second code path.** The helper is called in `_resolve_one`'s prohibition branch immediately after `vr_formulas = _grounding_vr_formulas(...)` (`~:776`) and before the D-293 gate (`:791`) and the `GroundedNegative` stash (`:809`); rebinding `vr_formulas` once means the gate (`prohibition_recipe_derivable`) and the persisted recipe see the SAME narrowed tuple — refusal and emission stay consistent with zero divergence. `emission.py` is **untouched** — `_derive_prohibition_recipe`/`_derive_violation`/`_derive_update_violation`/`prohibition_recipe_derivable` keep their first-derivable loops and signatures; they simply iterate a 0- or 1-element tuple.
