## D-299.2 — the LIVE env-59 proof lands (observed PASS): the grounded multi-field trigger fired the risk flow and the band stamped; S4a not needed; plus two findings the run surfaced (the Sonnet-5 elicitation miss and the multi-intent refusal swallow).

**Date:** 2026-07-02 · **Status:** active (closes D-299's documented open item, per the D-299.1 posture).

**OBSERVED (env-59, claim `3e65dbc9`, REQ-D299-LIVE-2, run `e4204622`, model pinned `claude-opus-4-7`).** Generation elicited the full v11 contract: the claim bound the requirement-NAMED flow (`HL_Auto_Risk_Rating` — the D-299 named-bind among the THREE Opportunity flows, live) and the create carried ALL THREE grounded `trigger_fields` (`StageName='Credit Assessment'`, `Credit_Score__c=720`, `KYC_Complete__c=true`) with the effect field absent (the k16 guard held). Execution: create → HTTP 201 (the trigger state satisfied `Credit_Assessment_Prerequisites` and tripped none of the other six active VRs); read-back → **`Risk_Rating__c='Medium'` on attempt 1** — the flow's RecordAfterSave stamp is synchronous, so **S4a (the null-read retry) is NOT needed** (the verify-at-live-first fork resolves: not built); assert equals held → `passed`; S6 verdict `automation_triggered`; teardown deleted the record (`succeeded=true`); zero `INVALID_SESSION_ID`. Honest scope: this proves the TC-029-shaped Medium-band case end-to-end; TC-028/030 are the same recipe shape at Low/High values (High additionally cascades the `HL_High_Risk_Task` flow — untested by design, per the D-299 plan).

**Finding 1 — the first Sonnet-vs-Opus datum (REQ-D299-LIVE-1 vs -2, same requirement).** The first attempt ran under the just-deployed Sonnet-5 default routing: the model PROPOSED the automation-effect intent (it reached admissibility, path c0 `admissibly_grounded`) but did not supply a verifiable effect (`field_name`/`expected_value`), so the stash gate refused it — while 3 sibling intents (an existence + two prerequisite prohibitions) drafted. The Opus-pinned retry elicited the full contract first try. One datum, not a verdict — but it lands exactly where predicted: model quality shows in ELICITATION completeness (coverage), never in truth (the substrate refused rather than authoring a wrong claim). Feeds the parallel Sonnet-A/B task.

**Finding 2 — a D-207-era transparency gap (recorded, NOT fixed here).** In the multi-intent merge (`governance_core.resolve_intent`), a per-intent refusal in a batch where OTHER intents ground is silently DISCARDED (`first_refusal` routes only when zero intents ground): the LIVE-1 automation-effect refusal left no refusal row and no coverage record — an admissibly-grounded path that simply never became a claim. This violates the D-247 refusal-visibility discipline for mixed batches. Named follow-on (surface per-intent refusals on the outcome / coverage_map); out of the D-299/D-300 lever scope.

**Operational note:** local (non-worker) harness runs intermittently fail the `llm_usage_log` write (a session-binding quirk of the script context — the gateway's best-effort log never raises), so the LIVE-1/LIVE-2 usage rows are absent; the D-300 generation logged fine (3 × `claude-opus-4-7`, $0.99 total, zero cache hits — pre-cache-fix branch code). The deployed daily run is the venue for the cache-fix + Sonnet-id live confirmation. See D-299/D-299.1 (the lever + the open item) · D-300.2 (the sibling closure) · D-207/D-247 (the merge + honesty disciplines Finding 2 touches).

## D-302 — Per-intent refusals survive the multi-intent merge: `partial_refusals` on `attempted_interpretation` records WHY every non-routing refusal directive refused (closes D-299.2 Finding 2, the D-207-era mixed-batch swallow).

**Date:** 2026-07-02 · **Status:** active. Fixes the D-299.2 Finding-2 transparency gap observed live on REQ-D299-LIVE-1 (env-59, tenant 1): 4 paths admissibly grounded, 3 claims written, and the automation-effect intent's stash-gate refusal (missing `field_name`/`expected_value`) vanished — no refusal row, no coverage record, an `admissibly_grounded` candidate path that silently never became a claim. A D-247 refusal-visibility violation for mixed batches.

**The defect, precisely — TWO swallow sites, one class.** (1) *In-merge:* `governance_core.resolve_intent`'s D-207 aggregator keeps only `first_refusal` and routes it ONLY when zero intents ground; in a mixed batch every per-intent `RefusalDirective` is dropped on the floor (the observed instance). In an all-refused multi-intent batch, siblings 2..n are equally dropped (only the first routes — the D-073 flat-list multiplicity exists on the outcome type but was never fed). (2) *Cross-turn:* the runtime's cumulative refuse guard (`if not state.presented_candidates: route`) swallows a wholly-refusing propose turn when a PRIOR turn grounded (the D-247 re-prompt hop is exactly the flow that produces this), and symmetrically swallows a first-turn refusal when the re-prompt `continue` bypasses the route. Same invariant broken at both sites: a substrate-authored refusal directive that does not route leaves no record.

**Mechanism — record-not-route, riding the existing reasoning artifact (NO schema change, verified).** New list key `partial_refusals` on `attempted_interpretation` (pydantic `extra='allow'`; JSONB column `generation_outcomes.attempted_interpretation`; `AttemptedInterpretation(**ai)` + `model_dump` carry extras through both the draft and refusal outcome constructors — checked end-to-end). Entry shape mirrors `RefusalEntry` plus the D-207 anchor: `{path_id: "c{i+offset}"` (the intent's re-indexed slot, joinable against `candidate_paths`), `ac_ref` (the D-247 coverage key, when the descriptor carried one), `archetype`, `claim_kind`, `refusal_kind` (enum value), `payload}` (the directive's payload verbatim). Three writers: (a) the multi-intent merge records an entry for EVERY refused intent, unconditionally — in a mixed batch these are the sole record (the named defect); in an all-refused batch they complete the D-073 multiplicity around the one directive that routes; (b) `runtime.merge_interpretation` gains append semantics for the key (the catch-all `ai[k]=v` would overwrite across the re-prompt hop); (c) the runtime stores the directive of a wholly-refused turn it declines to route (single-intent turns — the multi-intent case is already covered by (a), guarded against double-record by checking the just-merged delta). The substrate authors every entry (the directives are governance-authored; the spine stores verbatim — the D-072 store-never-author discipline holds).

**Deliberate NON-changes.** `coverage_map` semantics stay input-steered ("did the model address every AC" — the test-pinned D-247 contract, independent of grounding): a post-admissibility substrate refusal is a different fact from the model's `no_admissible_test`, and entries carry `ac_ref` so surfaces can join rather than conflate. Zero-ground single-intent refusals route exactly as before (byte-identical). `route_refusal` still writes one `RefusalEntry`; sibling reasons in an all-refused batch are visible via `partial_refusals` on the same outcome, not via the refusals column (widening that column's writer is a named non-goal).

**BA surface (the D-247 point of the fix).** `read_latest_generation_note` (D-206.1) additionally selects `attempted_interpretation->'partial_refusals'` and returns per-entry plain sentences via the existing `refusal_plain`; `requirements/detail.html` shows an amber note on DRAFT outcomes with partial refusals — "the engine generated N tests but declined M proposed tests, with reasons" — closing the "Generate silently did less than it understood" sibling of the SQ-205 confusion. See D-207 (the merge) · D-247 (coverage + refusal visibility) · D-073 (refusal multiplicity) · D-206.1 (the note surface) · D-299.2 Finding 2 (the live observation).

## D-304 — Lever 7b: formula-output verification as an automation-effect PRIMITIVE (`automation_primitive="formula"`) — a calculated field IS an automation; the D-299 observe machinery carries it end-to-end.

**Date:** 2026-07-02 · **Status:** active (lever 7, second sub-lever; follows D-303's band sweep). Design commit; impl slices follow on `phase-s3-l7b-formula-output`.

**Context.** TC-012/015/016 (the LTV formula asserts) are SHALLOW on the scorecard: no archetype verifies "given inputs X, the org COMPUTES field F = V". The recon confirmed the raw material: `field_details.is_calculated` is a hot column; the formula TEXT is captured on the raw describe shape (`attributes['calculatedFormula']` — live-verified on `Opportunity.Loan_to_Value__c`: `IF(Property_Value__c > 0, Loan_Amount__c / Property_Value__c, null)`); `extract_field_refs` (the VR formula parser) extracts same-object input refs from any formula text; and the S4 same-record observe path (create with `create_fields` → read → typed-tolerant assert) is exactly the needed executor — zero S4 change.

**Decision — a primitive, NOT a claim kind (D-053's own guardrail).** `AutomationEffectClaimBody.automation_primitive` exists precisely so mechanisms don't spawn claim-kinds; the Literal gains `"formula"` (additive; existing values/hashes untouched; the body's `automation: IdentityBearingRef` is entity-type-unconstrained, so the automation ref becomes the CALCULATED FIELD). The claim reads: "the org's formula on F computes V when the inputs are X" — same truth shape as a Flow stamp, different mechanism. Grounding dimension: the requirement-named automation resolves to a **Field with `is_calculated=true`** (the computation exists — the same character of verify as TRIGGERS_ON), via a shape-tolerant `field_formula_text`/`field_is_calculated` reader pair (the D-203.1/D-301 two-shape idiom: designed keys OR the raw describe `calculated`/`calculatedFormula`). The D-299 `trigger_fields` carry the formula INPUTS (same drop-never-refuse, same k16 exclude-the-observed-field guard — already shipped); when the formula text PARSES, proposed trigger fields that are not formula inputs are additionally dropped (they cannot move the output; unparseable formula → BELONGS_TO verification alone, the certainty floor). `GroundedAutomationEffect` gains `automation_primitive: str = "flow"` (dormant default — byte-identical) threaded through the author's three sites.

**Elicitation (prompt v12).** The data_behavior fragment teaches: a requirement asserting a CALCULATED/formula field's value ("Loan-to-Value is calculated as…", "the formula computes…") is an automation-effect with `automation_name` = the FIELD's api name, `trigger_fields` = the input fields + values, `field_name`/`expected_value` = the computed expectation. Freeze v12 (registry CURRENT bump + hash; v1..v11 immutable).

**Honest expectations for the live proof.** The org's LTV formula computes a RATIO (no ×100) at scale 2 — the suite's TC-012 expectation "62.50%" may honestly FAIL against a read-back of `0.63` (or pass at `62.5` if the field is percent-typed — the API read settles it). Either outcome is a WIN: a pass proves the archetype; a requirement-vs-org mismatch is a REAL finding the suite's author (AK) would want. TC-015 (decimal precision) and TC-016 (large values) ride the same requirement as sibling intents (the D-303 pattern). **TC-051 (formula field is read-only) is explicitly OUT** — a write-prohibition on a calculated field needs a non-VR prohibition grounding dimension (structural rejection), a named deferral.

**Slices.** S0 this entry → S1 the primitive end-to-end (S2 Literal + grounded-shape slot + author threading + the shape-tolerant field readers + grounding branch + unit/integration tests; the flow path byte-identical) → S2 prompt v12 freeze → S3 live env-59 proof (multi-intent: nominal + decimal + large-value ACs) + adversarial review → merge. No schema, no migration (the Literal is code-side; JSONB carries any string).

## D-304.1 — L7b closure: the formula primitive live-proven (3 PASSes at 62.5/63.17/90 — and the fail→diagnose→deprecate→regenerate loop that discovered the Percent-type semantics); the review's two blockers fixed pre-merge; the canonicalization float law now substrate-enforced at every hint ingress.

**Date:** 2026-07-02 · **Status:** active (closes D-304; branch `phase-s3-l7b-formula-output` merged to `main`).

**OBSERVED (env-59, REQ-L7B-LTV-1/-2, model pinned `claude-opus-4-7`).** v12 elicited three formula automation-effect claims first try (each binding `Opportunity.Loan_to_Value__c` AS the automation, creates carrying only the two inputs). The first pass produced the arc's best advertisement for the machinery: (1) three creates VR-rejected on padding roulette (`AmbiguousRejection`, honest errored — fixed at dispatch with D-235 `field_overrides`, the designed knob); (2) three honest FAILS with the observed values in evidence — `62.5 / 63.17 / 90.0`, revealing the field is a **Percent-type formula (API returns ratio ×100)** and that the 55-suite's "62.50%" expectation was RIGHT while my org-truthful-ratio guess was wrong; (3) the three wrong-expectation claims **deprecated with reasons** (the coordinator's human-gated op), the requirement corrected, regenerated, **all three PASSED** — TC-012/TC-015/TC-016 live-proven. Teardown: 9 runs, 6 created+cleaned, 3 created nothing, zero leaks. The fail-loop itself is the QA workflow the product exists to power.

**The float law (found live, fixed substrate-side).** The first generation CRASHED persistence: canonicalization v1 FORBIDS floats in identity-bearing content (SPEC §6.3.2) and the LLM proposed `0.63`. Fix: `_identity_safe` — float hints coerce to shortest-repr STRINGS at **all seven** hint→claim ingresses (value/state/automation expected+effect values, the state-transition staged trigger, and — review S1 — the D-293 `rejection_conditions` clause values, element-wise for `in_set` lists); the S4 typed-tolerant equals (D-211) grades `"0.63" == 0.63` numerically, so recipes grade identically. This also fixes the PRE-EXISTING crash for any decimal value-claim/state-transition/prohibition-condition hint. Residual (named): a coerced-string staged-trigger value reaching a NUMERIC create field relies on SF REST's string→number tolerance — unexercised live; watch at the next state-transition live run.

**The review's second blocker (B2): the formula/effect-field coherence guard.** Adversarial review (5 dimensions, 10 findings) confirmed the core sound (flow-path byte-identity; all 12 frozen prompt hashes recomputed clean) and found the same-record stash never required the automation binding and observed field to cohere — three crossed-binding facets, ONE of them a deterministic wrong-green (a named Flow credited for a value the formula engine computes from the create's own inputs — evidence that would stay green with the Flow broken). Fixed pre-merge: a formula automation must observe ITSELF; a calculated observed field under a named Flow refuses; the no-name floor re-binds the formula field as the honest mechanism. Also fixed: the review-caught fact that the float-coercion slice was live-proven from UNCOMMITTED worktree edits (B1 — committed as one cohesive unit).

**Impl revisions vs the D-304 entry (recorded):** the formula-input filter was NOT built (the condition parser returns `NotParsed` for value formulas — live-verified — and non-input triggers are legitimate VR-survival staging; `field_formula_text` retained unused with an honest docstring). Deferred, named: an S6 attribution nit (the failure cause on a formula claim named `HL_Auto_Risk_Rating` — the cause heuristic consults flows only; cosmetic, the verdict was correct); the base.md title self-identifying as v9 (fix at the NEXT freeze, never in frozen artifacts); the pre-existing positive-path override-wins-over-semantic ordering. Pre-existing main breakage repaired in passing: `test_run_generation`'s routing params still encoded the pre-Sonnet-5 per-archetype split (the flip shipped without running this PG-gated file). **Scorecard: TC-012/015/016 covered + LIVE-proven → 23 → 26 of 55.** See D-304 · D-303 · D-235 · D-211 · SPEC §6.3.2.

## D-305 — Lever 7c: the ACCEPTANCE archetype — "the org saves this" becomes a first-class claim, the exact mirror of the prohibition (same D-293 state-is-identity machinery; the tested values ARE the business state).

**Date:** 2026-07-02 · **Status:** active (lever 7, third sub-lever). Design commit; impl on `phase-s3-l7c-acceptance`.

**Context.** TC-001/002/044 (valid creates save; out-of-scope validations do NOT misfire) and TC-007/008 (the loan-vs-property JUST-BELOW and AT boundaries save) have no claim shape: nothing asserts creation-ACCEPTANCE as a truth. The recon confirmed every piece downstream exists — multi-field creates are recipe-native, `_run_positive` executes them, the D-300 accept probe proved the grading — the gap is the claim kind + authoring + one S4 grading nuance.

**Decision — a new claim kind `acceptance-claim`, the prohibition's mirror.** Body (v1): `target` (the Object, IdentityBearingRef) + `operation: Literal["create"]` (update acceptance is a later version) — deliberately minimal; acceptance IS the assertion. **The business state rides `semantic_conditions`** (the D-293 machinery verbatim): unlike a prohibition (where the violating value is recipe-operational because the STATE, not the value, is the assertion), an acceptance case is DEFINED by its values — TC-007 (Loan 79,99,999) and TC-008 (Loan 80,00,000) are different assertions differing ONLY by value — so the condition clauses (field=value) are identity-bearing and distinct cases hash apart for free. Floats in those values are already law-safe (`_identity_safe`, D-304.1). **Registration surface (the state-transition-claim precedent, ~14 files):** the body module + data_behavior/__init__ + models/__init__ + the `CLAIM_KIND_ENUM` **tenant migration** (`ALTER TYPE claim_kind ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS 'acceptance-claim'` — MIGRATE-FIRST: prod before deploy, the D-285 lesson) + coordinator taxonomy + generation/tools claim_kind_hint enum + governance `_DATA_BEHAVIOR_CLAIM_KINDS` + grounding/stash + emission EMITTABLE/author + claim_presentation label + S6 interpreter verdict mapping + prompt v13.

**Grounding (invent-nothing, Layer-1).** Every proposed acceptance condition clause grounds like a D-293 rejection condition: field BELONGS_TO the subject (object-qualified), predicate/value coupling; ADDITIONALLY each field must be WRITABLE (`_writable`, the D-294 rail — an acceptance create must be able to SET its state; a calculated/read-only field in the conditions refuses). No VR dimension — acceptance is the absence of rejection; the run proves it (Layer-1, caveat posture like the value-claim).

**Recipe + the S4 nuance.** The recipe: one multi-field CreateStep carrying the grounded condition values (object-qualified keys) + ReadStep (the record by `$create-record.id`, capture Id) + AssertStep `exists` — the shipped positive path end-to-end. ONE S4 addition: `CreateStep.expect_acceptance: bool = False` (S2-additive, `expect_rejection`'s mirror): when True, a STRUCTURED business rejection (HTTP 400 + a parseable error body) grades **`failed` with the rejecting rule attributed** — for an acceptance claim the rejection IS the finding, never an indeterminate staging error (contrast the value-claim positive, where a staging rejection stays honestly `errored`); transport/5xx/ambiguous stays `errored`. Bridge passes the flag through the positive projection; the negative dispatch (`expect_rejection`) is untouched.

**Elicitation (v13).** "saves successfully / can be created / is accepted / validations do NOT fire for this case" → `acceptance-claim`, positive polarity, `acceptance_conditions` = the field/value clauses that define the case (the same clause grammar as `rejection_conditions`). Negative-scope cases (TC-002/044: a Personal loan saves WITHOUT the Home-Loan fields) are the same shape — the conditions state what IS set; what is absent stays absent.

**Honest delivery.** TC-001, TC-002, TC-044, TC-007, TC-008 (~5, all live-provable on env-59). TC-020 (stage-progress acceptance) is UPDATE-shaped — deferred to the update-acceptance version alongside L7d. **Slices:** S0 this entry → S1 the claim kind end-to-end code-side (body/registrations/enum-migration/coordinator/tools/governance/emission/presentation/interpreter + tests) → S2 the S4 `expect_acceptance` grade + bridge + tests → S3 prompt v13 freeze → S4 MIGRATE-FIRST prod + live proof (TC-001/007/008/002/044) + adversarial review → merge. See D-293 (the state-identity line this mirrors) · D-300 (the accept-probe precedent) · D-304.1 (`_identity_safe`) · D-285 (MIGRATE-FIRST).

## D-306 — Lever 7d: update-then-observe — the automation-effect shape gains an UPDATE trigger phase (create the initial state → change it → observe the org recompute), and the positive S4 vertical learns its first mid-chain update.

**Date:** 2026-07-02 · **Status:** active (lever 7, fourth sub-lever). Design commit; impl on `phase-s4-l7d-update-observe`.

**Context.** TC-013/014 (the LTV formula RECALCULATES after a loan/property update), TC-031 (the risk rating recalculates after a credit-score change), and TC-020 (stage progress with valid data succeeds) are SHALLOW/refused: every observe shape today is create-scoped — nothing tests that the org re-evaluates on UPDATE, which is half of what automations and formulas do. The recon confirmed the gates: `_project_positive` rejects any UpdateStep (bridge.py — CreateStep×N → Read → Assert enforced); `_run_positive` has no update leg; updates exist ONLY as the rejected mutation of the 2-step negative (D-203).

**Decision — one new phase on the EXISTING shapes, not a new claim kind.** (1) `GroundedAutomationEffect` gains `update_trigger_fields: tuple = ()` (the D-299 idiom verbatim: (field, value) pairs, BELONGS_TO-verified, drop-never-refuse, the k16 exclude — the observed field can never be in either trigger set). When non-empty, the author emits the **update-observe** recipe: `create-record` (staging the CREATE-phase `trigger_fields` + `expect_acceptance=True` — the staging create must save, and a rejection is the D-305 graded finding, not an indeterminate) → `update-record` (an UpdateStep carrying the update trigger fields, NO expect_rejection — the first positive update) → `read-created` → `assert-value` on the org-recomputed effect field. Works for BOTH primitives: a flow recalc (TC-031: create at score 649 → update to 750 → observe Low) and a formula recalc (TC-013/014: create at loan 5M → update to 6M → observe the new percent). The claim body is UNCHANGED except `triggering_action.description` narrates the update phase (identity distinguishes create-scoped from update-scoped claims naturally). (2) `AcceptanceClaimBody.operation` widens to `Literal["create", "update"]` (body_schema stays v1 — additive Literal; the D-305 entry reserved exactly this): update-acceptance authors create(initial equals clauses) → update(the `update_conditions` equals clauses, `expect_acceptance` semantics on the UPDATE) → read → assert exists. Covers TC-020 (progress to Credit Assessment WITH KYC+score succeeds — the prohibition TC-017/018/19's mirror).

**S4 (the real extension, kept minimal).** `_project_positive` widens to `CreateStep×N → [UpdateStep(no expect_rejection)] → ReadStep → AssertStep` (0-or-1 update; a flagged update still routes negative — the discriminator is unchanged). `_run_positive` executes the update mid-chain against the terminal create's record id (client.update exists), with: a REJECTED update grading per the acceptance rule when the step carries `expect_acceptance=True` (`failed`, the org refused a change that must succeed) else `errored` (staging honesty, the value-claim posture); transport → errored; teardown unchanged (the created record is tracked regardless). `UpdateStep` gains `expect_acceptance: bool = False` (mirroring CreateStep, D-305). The interpreter's positive vocab handles the existing kinds; the acceptance failed-at-UPDATE shape routes through the B2 acceptance interpreter (update evidence + claim_kind discriminates).

**Elicitation (v14).** Automation-effect/formula: "recalculates / re-evaluates / updates when X changes" → `update_trigger_fields` alongside `trigger_fields` (initial vs changed state, both fully-qualified). Acceptance: "can progress / can be updated to / the change succeeds" → `operation: update` + `update_conditions`. Same clause grammars as shipped.

**Honest delivery.** TC-013, TC-014, TC-031, TC-020 (~4–5 live-provable; TC-042/043 partially — 042's "rules still enforced on edit" IS the shipped update-rejected negative, claimable at the next scored pass; 043's type-switch is a compound). **Slices:** S0 this entry → S1 S2-model + bridge + executor (the update leg, seam-tested BOTH directions — the D-305.1 lesson) → S2 emission + governance (both shapes) → S3 prompt v14 → S4 live proof (formula recalc + risk recalc + stage progress + a negative control on the update leg) + adversarial review → merge. No migration (no new enum values — operation widens code-side within the existing kind; verify no CHECK constrains it). See D-299 (the trigger idiom) · D-304 (the formula primitive) · D-305/D-305.1 (expect_acceptance + the seam-test discipline) · D-203 (the negative update this mirrors).

## D-306.1 — Lever 7d closure: the live proof + the adversarial review overturned two of D-306's own design calls; the fixed shapes re-proven live.

**Date:** 2026-07-03 · **Status:** closed (lever 7d). Branch `phase-s4-l7d-update-observe` merged to `main`.

**What shipped (per the D-306 slice plan).** S1 model+bridge+executor (the first positive mid-chain update, seam-tested both directions), S2 emission+governance (both update shapes), S3 prompt v14 + the S6 dispatch/vocabulary arc, S4 live proof. LIVE on env-59: **LTV recalc 5M→6M ⇒ 75.0 PASS (TC-013) · property 8M→10M ⇒ 50.0 PASS (TC-014) · risk re-stamp 700→780 Medium→Low PASS (TC-031, the flow re-fires on update) · stage-progress `change_accepted` PASS (TC-020) · the negative control `change_rejected` (the Credit_Assessment_Prerequisites VR refused the unqualified progression — the update leg cannot wrong-green)**. Zero record leaks (k14 teardown clean).

**The live proof caught two defects pre-review** (both fixed + unit-pinned): (1) the D-305.1 subordination merge put the dispatch override BELOW the padding on expect_acceptance creates — the VR-gated padding value (`StageName='Credit Assessment'`) buried the very override meant to steer it (fixed: padding < override < staged, staged = the RESOLVED semantic set); (2) failed-at-create runs on POSITIVE claim kinds interpreted as the 1-step negative — prohibition prose on positive claims (fixed: the refused-mutation branch + `creation_rejected`).

**Adversarial review (23 agents, 5 dimensions → skeptic verification): 2 distinct BLOCKING (each independently confirmed 3–4×), 6 SHOULD-FIX, 7 notes.** Both blockers overturned D-306's own design decisions:

- **B1 — the update-acceptance identity encoding was defective.** D-306 folded initial+update clauses into one conditions body, asserting "initial-then-update order rides the conditions body." False: `SemanticConditionsBody.conditions` is an `ArraySemantics.SET` — canonicalization SORTS it, erasing the phase split AND the change direction. Empirically reproduced: stage-PROGRESS and stage-REGRESS claims hashed IDENTICAL (as did split-shift variants), and §7.7 hash-dedup would silently swallow the second case as `equivalent_existing` — wrong-green at the coverage layer, violating the D-305 conditions-are-identity law. It also overloaded the commutative-AND conditions layer with a temporal sequence (contradictory equals on one field). **Fix: `AcceptanceClaimUpdateBody` (body_schema v2, per D-305's ORIGINAL reservation — D-306's "additive Literal within v1" is overturned because canonicalization includes every field, so a new v1 slot would re-key all existing create-acceptance claims).** The destination rides the v2 body's `update_state` (StateDescriptor, LiteralValue-wrapped); `semantic_conditions` carries ONLY the initial state (a satisfiable conjunction again). Progress/regress, split-shift, and create-vs-update all hash apart; convergence pinned. v1 keeps `operation: Literal["create","update"]` solely so the two pre-fix persisted rows stay decodable; both were deprecated with reasons and regenerated on v2.
- **B2 — `expect_acceptance=True` on the update-observe STAGING create was a wrong-red machine.** Any 400 graded `failed` regardless of attribution — including padding-provoked VR rejections (the exact collision the live proof hit), fabricating red business findings on unattended runs for S4's own operational gap; internally inconsistent with the same diff's update-acceptance initial create (deliberately unflagged, D-115.2 attribution). **Fix: the flag is dropped — the staging create grades by standard D-115.2 attribution (staged-field rejection → failed; padding/ambiguous → errored).** The three live recipes were re-versioned through the coordinator (flag off) + re-approved; claim identity untouched.

**The should-fix set (all fixed):** the executor's staged-wins subordination now keys on the SHAPE (any update-bearing chain), not the grading flag — the update-acceptance initial create was silently override-rewritable (SF-2); a k16 chokepoint in `_run_positive` strips dispatch overrides naming an OBSERVED field the recipe doesn't stage (an override could plant the effect value and green a broken flow; recipe-staged fields stay overridable per D-235) (SF-4); the accepted-but-unverified assert-fail shape gets its own verdict `acceptance_not_verified` (was `change_rejected`/`creation_rejected` — "the org rejected a change" over a 204) and refused-mutation attribution fires only on a step that actually FAILED (no more fabricated `platform_constraint … []` causes; the VR-message-matching cause now also enriches genuine `creation_rejected`/`change_rejected` — the NEGCTL cause names the gating VR) (SF-1); the S6 mutation-acceptance branch carries the same mislabeled-kind guards as the create branch, the failed CREATE (not the first) is graded on multi-create chains, and a delete words as "deletion" (SF-3); governance refuses the vacuous update (every update pair duplicating the staged initial value — a no-op PATCH cannot witness a recompute/transition), non-updateable/calculated update trigger fields (perma-errored PATCH), duplicate update-clause fields, and misshaped `update_conditions` (refuse-not-crash) (SF-5/N1/N2/N6/N7); `_interpret_positive` refs + prose carry the update step (N3).

**Live re-proof on the fixed encoding:** the two defective v1 rows were deprecated with reasons and the pair REGENERATED on v2 (fresh hashes — no dedup clash by construction), then re-run on env-59: STAGE-1 `change_accepted` PASS; NEGCTL-1 `change_rejected` with the new VR-naming cause live (`other_vr_fired`, vr_name=`Opportunity.Credit_Assessment_Prerequisites` — S6 now points a human straight at the gating rule); the three automation-effect recipes were re-versioned through the coordinator (flag off, claim identity untouched, v2 approved) and RECALC-2 re-ran green on its re-versioned recipe (700→780, Medium→Low). Zero record leaks across every batch. Separately observed (pre-existing, chip spawned): the periodic Sonnet-pinned live-eval gate fails 7/16 probes IDENTICALLY on v13 and v14 — not a v14 regression, but a model-quality/harness datum for the Sonnet-vs-Opus decision.

**Named deferrals:** `_identity_safe` + deterministic ordering for the trigger-fields description joins (N4 — pre-existing D-299 class; sorting would re-key existing claims, so it needs its own migration-style decision); the D-305 create-acceptance any-400→failed posture itself (deliberate: there the staged state IS the case; unchanged); per-clause phase markers on `Condition` (not needed — the v2 body carries the phase); the L7d scorecard TCs (TC-013/014/020/031 → 30 → **34/55**, all live-proven; TC-042 claimable at the next scored pass per D-306).

See D-306 (the design this corrects) · D-305/D-305.1 (the acceptance archetype + the seam-test lesson this extends) · D-115.2 (the grading law B2 restores) · D-293/D-305 (the conditions-are-identity law B1 restores).

## D-307 — Lever 7e: Task cross-object — trigger staging for the cross-object shapes + the automation-ABSENCE claim (not_exists).

**Date:** 2026-07-03 · **Status:** active (lever 7, fifth sub-lever). Design commit; impl on `phase-s3-l7e-task-crossobject`.

**Context.** TC-037–041 (the Task-automation section): High band → a follow-up Task linked via `Task.WhatId`; Medium/Low → NO task; assignment; cardinality. Recon (live, read-only): **Task IS grounded in S1** (39 fields; WhatId/OwnerId/Subject/Status/Priority all BELONGS_TO, org-scoped) — the 2026-07-01 scorecard's "Task not modeled" is stale. The L7a-style pure-generation bet was run live and honestly FAILED: the D-210 cross-object shape authored (`read Task WHERE WhatId = '$create-record.id'` → assert exists) but the create staged NOTHING — **D-299's `trigger_fields` grounding is wired only into the same-record governance branch**, so the flow's entry gate (Credit Assessment + KYC + score) can never fire and the run would grade `automation_not_triggered` for S3's own shallow authoring, not the org.

**Decision — two pieces, one lever.**
1. **Trigger staging on the cross-object + parent-stamp branches** (the D-299 rail, extended): governance grounds `trigger_fields` (BELONGS_TO the SUBJECT, drop-never-refuse per field) and `update_trigger_fields` stays same-record-only (D-306.1 unchanged). The k16 exclude on these branches guards `effect_field` when present (cross-object-with-field / parent-stamp; the plain existence shape has no effect field to exclude — and a subject-side trigger field can never plant a row on ANOTHER object, so the exclude surface is honest). `_author_automation_effect` threads `create_fields` into the cross-object and parent-stamp step builders exactly as the same-record branch does (`create-record` gains the staged gate; the D-227 parent-first chain stages them on the TRIGGER create, never the parent). The narrated gate rides `triggering_action.description` (identity — staged and unstaged cross-object claims hash apart, the D-299 idiom).
2. **The automation-ABSENCE claim (TC-038/039)** — "creating X under state S does NOT produce a correlated Y". Per the D-306.1 B1 law (a NEW identity-bearing slot = a NEW body_schema_version — canonicalization includes every field), this is **`AutomationEffectClaimBody` v2** with `expected_absence: Literal[True]` (v1 stays untouched for every existing claim; v2 used only for absence emissions). The recipe: the SAME staged create → the SAME correlate read → **`not_exists`** (new assert predicate: held ⇔ row_count == 0). S4: add `not_exists` to `_SUPPORTED_DATA_PREDICATES` + `_run_ground`; the D-210 empty-read retry works FOR absence (three attempts give the org every chance to prove presence before we assert absence — the honest direction); the D-227.7 zero-rows-evaluable law already keeps 0 rows evaluable on side-effect reads. S6: the positive vocab maps pass/fail for absence claims honestly (pass = "the automation correctly produced nothing"; fail = a row was observed — `automation_triggered`-inverted wording; exact vocabulary in impl). Elicitation (v15): "does not create / no task / must not fire" → the absence intent; the create-staged band is the same `trigger_fields` grammar.

**Honest delivery.** TC-037 (presence, High) + TC-038/039 (absence, Medium/Low) ⇒ 34 → ~37/55, all live-provable on env-59 (the High band DOES create a Task there — the L7c-era "cascade" note). TC-040 (assigned to Credit Manager): `OwnerId` is groundable as a field but a person-NAME → id mapping is not — expected to refuse honestly unless the requirement states a stable literal on a groundable field (Subject); live discovery will settle it. TC-041 (exactly one Task) needs COUNT semantics — **out of scope, named deferral** (a cardinality predicate is its own small design; `not_exists`/`exists` don't express it).

**Slices.** S0 this entry → S1 governance staging on both branches + author threading (seam: staged cross-object recipe projects through the bridge; k16 excludes effect_field) → S2 the absence vertical (body v2 + not_exists S4 + S6 vocab + emission) → S3 prompt v15 freeze → S4 live proof (TC-037 presence + TC-038 absence + teardown audit incl. flow-created Tasks) + adversarial review → merge. The shallow TASK-1 draft from the recon probe is deprecated in S4 (padding-only create = wrong-meaning shape; its regeneration post-S1 hashes apart via the narrated gate). No migration (v2 body is registry-side; `not_exists` is recipe-content, no enum).

See D-299 (the trigger idiom this extends) · D-306.1 (the body-versioning + expectation-flag laws this obeys) · D-210/D-227 (the cross-object/parent-stamp shapes) · D-227.7 (zero-rows-evaluable).

## D-307.1 — Lever 7e closure: the Task cross-object arc live-proven (including the honest requirement-vs-org red), the absence vertical hardened by the review's reproduced wrong-green.

**Date:** 2026-07-03 · **Status:** closed (lever 7e). Branch `phase-s3-l7e-task-crossobject` merged to `main`.

**What shipped (per the D-307 slice plan).** S1 trigger staging on the cross-object + parent-stamp branches; S2 the absence vertical (`AutomationAbsenceClaimBody` body-v2, the `not_exists` predicate, fail-closed shape gates, the S6 absence vocabulary `automation_absence_confirmed`/`automation_fired_unexpectedly`); S3 prompt v15; S3b the live-found polarity routing (an absence intent arrives labeled negative — the substrate routes `expected_absence`, never the not-built refusal).

**LIVE on env-59:** **TC-038 (Medium → no Task) PASSED `automation_absence_confirmed`** — the first live absence verdict — and **TC-039 (Low) PASSED**. **TC-037 (High → follow-up Task) FAILED `automation_not_triggered` HONESTLY**: ground-truth verified (`HL_Auto_Risk_Rating` has `recordCreates: []`; zero Tasks org-wide this month) — the gold-suite Task cascade is simply NOT implemented in env-59, and the failing run is the product's purpose: a correct test surfacing a real requirement-vs-org gap. The test is scored covered_correct on test-correctness, explicitly NOT on an org pass. Zero teardown leaks; the pre-D-307 shallow recon draft was deprecated with a reason.

**Adversarial review (18 agents, 4 dimensions → skeptic verification): 14 confirmed findings deduping to 2 BLOCKING + 3 should-fix clusters + 9 notes. The headline law: EVERY presence-side safety posture must be re-derived under absence, because the direction inversion turns self-revealing degradations into self-concealing wrong-greens.**
- **B1 (reproduced wrong-green):** the D-305.1/D-306.1 staged-wins override subordination was keyed on `expect_acceptance`/update-presence — the D-307 shapes carry neither, so a dispatch override clobbered the staged gate and the absence run passed on an untested premise. **Fix: the subordination also keys on the OBSERVE shape** (the terminal create's staged fields disjoint from the read's captured fields — exactly when a clobbered gate is self-concealing). D-235's override-wins power on value-claims is untouched (there the staged field IS captured and divergence self-reveals as a red); the same-record D-299 shapes gain the protection too.
- **B2:** drop-never-refuse on `trigger_fields` INVERTS under absence — for presence a dropped gate degrades to an honest red, for absence a padding-only create grades green-by-construction against any gated automation. **Fix: an absence case REQUIRES ≥1 grounded trigger pair** (dropped-to-empty and never-proposed both refuse). The deliberate cost: unconditional-absence intents ("never creates X for any record") now refuse — indistinguishable from the vacuous class at the certainty bar.
- **SF:** `expected_absence` is now strict-boolean (a string "false" is truthy; coercion either way inverts meaning — fail closed) and REFUSES on any non-automation-effect claim kind (an ignored flag authors the opposite artifact — the meaning-inversion class).

**Named deferrals (honest limitations, all noted by the review):** the ~4s D-210 retry window is load-bearing against a slow ASYNC flow path (a late-created record would false-green the absence and, post-teardown, rely on SF's activity cascade-delete — no substrate guard yet); `effect_lookup_field` is verified to EXIST, not to be the linkage the automation actually uses (Layer-1 caveat covers it; a mis-hinted lookup wrong-greens until S8 drift or a human catches it); the absence-failure prose over-attributes any observed row to the NAMED automation; `automation_fired_unexpectedly` gets no S1 cause enrichment; every absence claim titles identically on the spine; TC-040 (assignment) stays honest_refuse (person-name → id ungroundable) and TC-041 (cardinality) needs its own count-predicate design.

**Scorecard: 34 → 37/55** (TC-037 covered_correct-with-honest-red, TC-038/039 covered_correct live-PASSED). See D-307 (the design) · D-299 (the trigger rail) · D-306.1 (the body-versioning + expectation-flag laws) · D-210/D-227.7 (the cross-object read semantics).

## D-308 — Lever 7f: approvals — ProcessDefinition/ProcessInstance into S1, feeding the D-307 presence/absence machinery (`automation_primitive="approval_process"`).

**Date:** 2026-07-03 · **Status:** active (lever 7, sixth sub-lever). Design commit; impl on `phase-s1-l7f-approvals`.

**Context (recon, all live read-only).** TC-032–036/049/053 (the approval section, threshold ₹50,00,000). env-59 HAS the arc end-to-end: `HL_High_Value_Loan` (ProcessDefinition, Type=Approval, State=Active, on Opportunity — via the REGULAR SOQL API; the Tooling query 400s on this table) AND `HL_Auto_Submit_Approval` (a Flow with approval actionCalls — the org AUTO-SUBMITS, so "approval initiated" is observable without a submission executor). `ProcessInstance` is SOQL-queryable with `TargetObjectId` — **TC-032/033 ("no approval") and TC-034 ("approval initiated") are EXACTLY the D-307 cross-object absence/presence shapes** (ProcessInstance = the correlated record, TargetObjectId = the lookup). The gaps are all S1-side: `ProcessInstance` is excluded from the object universe (`_is_syncable_object` requires searchable; it is queryable-but-not-searchable), and no row-level approval-process entity type exists (`ProcessDefinition` appears only as an Object-schema entity).

**Decision — an S1 sync slice feeding EXISTING shapes, not a new archetype.**
1. **`ProcessInstance` joins the object universe** via an explicit approval-runtime allowlist in `_is_syncable_object` (the searchable heuristic targets "user-facing data objects"; ProcessInstance is queryable runtime data our effect-reads need). The generic Object/Field phases then materialize its schema + fields (TargetObjectId included) with no further code.
2. **A row-level `ApprovalProcess` entity type**: a new sync phase fetches ProcessDefinition rows (regular SOQL: Id, Name, DeveloperName, Type='Approval', State, TableEnumOrId), materializes `entity_type="ApprovalProcess"` (external_id=DeveloperName, attributes carry the row + `_is_active` from State) + a **`TRIGGERS_ON` edge to the target Object** — reusing the Flow's edge keeps S3's automation-neighborhood read unchanged (semantics: submission-triggered record automation; defensible and cheap). The entities/edges tables are generic (entity_type is a value, not DDL) — **no migration**; verify no CHECK constrains the type.
3. **S3 grounding**: the automation binding accepts ApprovalProcess entities alongside Flow/formula — `automation_primitive="approval_process"` (reserved in the body Literal since D-053, now used). effect_object="ProcessInstance" + effect_lookup_field="ProcessInstance.TargetObjectId" ground through `_ground_cross_object_effect` verbatim; presence/absence author via D-307 (the B2 grounded-gate law applies — the boundary intents stage Loan_Amount__c etc.).
4. **Prompt v16**: approval elicitation — "requires/initiates approval" → the cross-object presence shape on ProcessInstance via TargetObjectId, naming the approval process; "no approval required" → `expected_absence`; each boundary value a distinct intent. The ₹50L entry criteria live in Metadata (unfetched) — threshold grounding stays requirement-sourced (the D-299 Fork-A posture: observability, not correctness-of-criteria; a wrong band grades honestly at run time).

**Live-phase watch item (teardown):** an Opportunity with a PENDING approval may refuse deletion ("record is in an approval process") — k14 teardown is best-effort (records, never raises), so a leak is possible; the run evidence will show it, and recall-before-delete is a named follow-on if it bites.

**Honest delivery.** TC-032 (absence @ 49,99,999) + TC-033 (absence @ 50,00,000) + TC-034 (presence @ 50,00,001) ⇒ 37 → ~40/55, live-provable. **Named deferrals:** TC-035/036 (reject/approve → stage blocked/progresses — needs approval ACTIONS via ProcessInstanceWorkitem, an executor arc of its own) · TC-049 (approval action) · TC-053 (notification) · ProcessInstanceStep/Workitem sync.

**Slices.** S0 this entry → S1 sync (allowlist + the ApprovalProcess phase; unit + a LIVE env-59 sync to materialize) → S2 S3-grounding (approval binding + primitive) → S3 prompt v16 → S4 live proof (the boundary triple) + adversarial review → merge. See D-307/D-307.1 (the machinery + the absence laws this rides) · D-299 (Fork-A requirement-sourced posture) · D-053 (the primitive sub-discriminator).

## D-308.1 — Lever 7f closure: approvals live-proven on the D-307 machinery — two right-reason boundary PASSes plus a genuine org-configuration contradiction surfaced; the review's cross-primitive wrong-green and the final-phase sentinel fixed.

**Date:** 2026-07-03 · **Status:** closed (lever 7f). Branch `phase-s1-l7f-approvals` merged to `main`.

S3: prompt v16.

**S4 LIVE (env-59) — the boundary triple, honest three ways.** The FIRST round staged the letter of the D-307.1 grounded-gate rule but not the org's REAL gate — the absence pair passed VACUOUSLY (no submission ever attempted). Reading the auto-submit flow's actual filters (`StageName='Approved' AND Loan_Amount__c > 5000000`) exposed it; the three claims were deprecated with reasons and re-staged. SECOND round: **TC-033 (=₹50,00,000) and TC-032 (₹49,99,999) PASSED for the RIGHT reason** — the create saved at the staged Approved gate, the flow's threshold filter excluded them, no ProcessInstance. **TC-034 (₹50,00,001) honestly ERRORED on a genuine org contradiction**: env-59's own VR ("Loans over ₹50,00,000 require Manager Approval before moving to Approved") forbids the exact state the auto-submit flow triggers on — the >50L submission path is structurally unreachable by data operations, i.e. the org's automation is dead config for its own gate. The product surfaced it with the VR's message in evidence. TC-034 (+ TC-035/036/049) defers to the named submission-action executor arc. Zero teardown leaks (Opportunities AND ProcessInstances).

**Adversarial review (14 agents, 4 dimensions → skeptic verification): 10 confirmed → 1 blocker + 1 verifier-downgraded + 4 should-fix + 11 notes.** Fixed pre-merge: (**B1**) the D-304.1 calc-field coherence guard fired for `primitive == "flow"` only — an approval-bound claim observing a CALCULATED field authored a deterministic wrong-green; the guard now fires for every non-formula primitive. **The lever's law (the review's own summary): the D-307.1 grounded-gate rule guarantees A gate, not the ORG-CORRECT gate — for automations whose logic S1 cannot parse, live-run-reveals is the honest floor**, and this round proved the loop works: vacuous pass → org-metadata read → re-stage → right-reason pass, all inside one session.

**Named deferrals:** flow-name-shadowing (an inactive Flow sharing an sf_api_name with an active approval binds first — the pre-existing inactive-flow-binding class; rare, needs the flows-side D-301 slice) · custom-object approvals (TableEnumOrId may carry the 01I id, not the api name → the edge skips via the §19 counter → honest refusal, a coverage gap not a wrong-green) · the D-306 update-observe × approval composition (the B1 guard covers the calc case; the rest is the honest-red class) · the `_grade_rejected_create` premise-break→failed tension for observe-shape staging creates (a D-115.2-deep decision of its own) · deprecate-then-regenerate dedup semantics vs deprecated rows (a coordinator §7.7 decision; did NOT bite here — verified) · S6 attribution is approval-blind (`flows_for_object` filters Flow) · the 85 SVS-catalog gaps (pre-existing, chipped separately).

## D-309 — the SVS catalog-gap surface is BENIGN, not transient: an overlay on the D-262 genuine-count (full fetches report `success` again) + a grounded retry gate

**Context.** Every env-59 full fetch since 2026-06-24 finalized `partial_success`
with `permission_gaps=85` — all from `fetch_standard_value_sets`, category
`transient`, `sf_error_code=UNKNOWN_EXCEPTION`. DB history proves the condition
is **pre-existing and deterministic, not a regression**: the failing label set is
byte-identical across every full fetch 2026-06-24 → 2026-07-03 (85 edition-gated
catalog names — APT*/AccPlan*/Assessment*/CardType/Finance*/Fulfillment*/…); the
gaps "started" exactly when D-262 Slice B instrumented the swallow site
(2026-06-24); the pg=0 runs memory recalls were pre-instrumentation full fetches
(06-20) or the skip-gate run `d7794b08` (skipped=t — never fetched). Mechanism:
HTTP 500 is deliberately outside `TRANSIENT_STATUS_CODES`, so each unqueryable
label raises `SFRequestError` immediately; `classify_failure`'s status
refinement (unknown + 5xx → `transient`) then counts it genuine, and
`maybe_finalize_run` degrades the run. A **persistent, expected** SF-side
catalog behavior (docstring-documented since the probe: ~32% of the 616-entry
catalog 500s on orgs without industry clouds) was riding a category that means
"retryable hiccup" — making every full fetch of a normal-edition org read as
degraded forever, drowning the signal `partial_success` exists to carry.

**Decision — REJECT the referenced-names catalog filter.** Pre-filtering the
catalog to "SVS names referenced by synced fields" is architecturally impossible
in this direction: no API exposes a standard field's SVS name (corrections-log
§22 — the reason D-118 exists), so the Field phase discovers the linkage by
CONTENT-matching field value sets against the *fetched* SVS metadata. The
reference only exists AFTER the fetch; filtering before it would require the
very information the fetch discovers. The full-catalog iteration also feeds the
PVS entity universe ("every record is worth materializing"), which a filter
would shrink into supersession churn. Docstrings corrected (`phases.py` no
longer suggests the inverted-direction "future cycle").

**Decision — a site-supplied `benign` OVERLAY on the gap record, not a new
taxonomy category.** `build_gap(..., benign=<reason-slug>)` /
`record_metadata_gap(..., benign=...)` add an opt-in `"benign"` key to the gap
dict; `genuine_gap_count` excludes benign gaps whatever their category. The
D-261 category vocabulary is untouched (no migration, no S4 ripple, `unknown`
keeps its "unclassified, never load-bearing" meaning); the category still
honestly records what the classifier saw (`transient`), while the overlay
carries what only the SITE knows: this failure surface is the documented
expected-catalog-gap shape and dropped nothing the org has. Benign gaps stay in
`gap_details` (visible, queryable — the cross-run persistence check above used
exactly that record) and render gray-badged "· benign" in the run drilldown;
rows without the key (all pre-D-309 history) count exactly as before.

**Decision — absence of data loss requires a grounded gate: one immediate
same-label retry before benign.** A one-shot 500 is ambiguous between the
deterministic catalog gap and a genuine hiccup on a label the org DOES support —
marking the latter benign would silently drop that SVS's rows under a `success`
banner (the wrong-green class). `fetch_standard_value_sets` now retries a 500'd
label once, immediately: recovery → the rows are used, NO gap at all; a
twice-confirmed failure classifies. Benign is then pinned **fail-closed** to the
exact observed surface — status 500 AND `errorCode=UNKNOWN_EXCEPTION`
(`"catalog_label_unqueryable"`). Everything else stays genuine: 403 →
`permission` (counted, not retried — deterministic denial), exhausted
502/503/504 → `transient` (counted), any other 500 code → counted. Worst-case
wall-clock cost: one extra ~0.6s call per failing label (~51s on env-59's 85),
bounded and full-fetch-only.

**Verification.** Unit: 3548 green (full suite), incl. new pins — twice-500
UNKNOWN_EXCEPTION → benign + not genuine + exactly 2 calls; 500-then-recover →
rows used, zero gaps; 500 with another code → genuine; 403 → single attempt,
`permission`, genuine; benign-only run → `genuine_gap_count=0` (finalizes
`success`); keyless history rows count unchanged. Live proof pending: the next
env-59 full fetch should finalize `success` with 85 benign rows visible in
`gap_details`. See D-261 (taxonomy) · D-262 (gap surfacing) · D-118 (content
match, the filter rejection's ground) · corrections-log §6/§22.

## D-310 — Lever 7g: journeys — the multi-intent decomposition already covers a journey's independent facts (3/4 happy-path constituents live-green); the DEFINING journey capability (a single-record continuous walk carrying accumulated state) is characterized and scoped as the next build, not silently claimed.

**Date:** 2026-07-03 · **Status:** characterized (lever 7, seventh/last sub-lever). Docs-only; the continuous-walk executor is a scoped, un-built fork put to AK. **(Numbered D-310: D-309 was concurrently taken by the parallel SVS-catalog-gap work — the D-302→D-303 renumber precedent.)**

**Context.** TC-054 (standard happy path) and TC-055 (high-risk journey) are the suite's two end-to-end journeys — each a create → progress → risk → approval sequence on ONE record. The 2026-07-01 scorecard filed them under "needs new archetype." The L7a/L7e lesson said recon-before-assuming; the recon was decisive.

**Recon (live generate, env-59).** Both journeys FAN OUT through the D-207 multi-intent decomposition into distinct claims, each an already-shipped, already-live-proven shape — NO new archetype for the facts: JOURNEY-1 → 4 claims (acceptance-create L7c · acceptance-update-to-Credit-Assessment L7d · risk→Low automation-effect L7a · approval-absence L7f); JOURNEY-2 → 3 (acceptance-update · risk→High · approval-presence). The decomposition is faithful to each STATED fact.

**Live proof (JOURNEY-1, env-59) — 3 of 4 constituents PASS, and the 4th reveals the real limit.** Valid Home Loan create → `creation_accepted` PASS · progress to Credit Assessment → `change_accepted` PASS · no approval below the ₹50L threshold → `automation_absence_confirmed` PASS · **risk→Low → FAILED `automation_not_triggered`**. Evidence: the isolated risk intent created at `StageName='Prospecting'` (its `trigger_fields` did NOT stage `Credit Assessment` — the journey stated the stage ONCE, in the adjacent PROGRESS clause, and the decomposition did not propagate that accumulated state to the risk intent), so the HL_Auto_Risk_Rating flow's entry gate never fired and `Risk_Rating__c` came back null. The risk SHAPE is proven (L7a/L7d live-proved it WHEN the stage is staged); the journey decomposition lost the shared entry-state. Zero teardown leaks. (Two prior live findings the loop caught honestly this session: the org's Home-Loan VR requires Annual Income — the requirement omitted it, the create was rejected, re-stated + re-run; and large multi-intent proposals occasionally fail Layer-A as a WHOLE BATCH — chipped, see below.)

**The finding — the honest limit of decomposition-as-journey-coverage.** A journey's facts SHARE accumulated record state (the record IS at Credit Assessment by the time risk is evaluated; it HAS the loan amount by the time approval is judged). Decomposing into independent single-record claims covers each fact in isolation but LOSES the cross-intent state carry-over that is the defining value of a journey test. So TC-054/055 are NOT "covered" as journeys — their constituent facts are (mostly: 3/4 live-green), but the continuity is not.

**The scoped next build (the fork put to AK) — a continuous-record-walk journey, an INCREMENTAL extension of D-306.** The D-306 positive shape is already `Create×N → [Update×0..1] → Read → Assert` — a create-then-one-update-then-observe walk on ONE record. A journey is `Create×N → (Update → Read → Assert)+` — N interleaved observe segments, each observing on the SAME record after the prior update, state accumulating. Slice sketch: a `journey-claim` kind (or a v-bump reusing the acceptance/automation bodies) carrying an ordered list of (change, expectation) segments; the bridge `_project_positive` widens to the interleaved sequence; `_run_positive` becomes a step-machine (walk steps, thread state, observe after each mutation — the D-306 machinery generalized from 1 to N observe segments); the segment expectations reuse the shipped grades (acceptance / automation-effect equals / absence not_exists). No new S6 vocab (per-segment verdicts compose). Live-provable end-to-end: TC-054 as ONE record walked create→progress→risk-observe→approval-observe. **Fork:** build it now (the senior-QA-complete answer; delivers TC-054/055 → 41/55; ~a lever's worth of work incl. its own review + live proof) vs. accept decomposition-covers-the-facts and keep the continuous walk as the named next build. **Lean: build it** — a journey test's value IS the continuous walk, TC-054/055 explicitly ask for it, and it is an incremental (not from-scratch) executor extension; but it is a new-archetype-sized build that deserves an explicit GO.

**Alternative (rejected as a band-aid):** a prompt v17 telling the LLM to propagate a journey's shared entry-state to every automation intent would make the DECOMPOSITION more robust (the risk intent would re-stage Credit Assessment), but it does not deliver the continuous-walk test — it just makes the isolated-claims approximation tighter. Noted, not taken.

**Scorecard: stays 39/55 — journeys are NOT counted covered.** TC-054/055 are explicitly PENDING the continuous-walk executor; the decomposition's coverage of their independent facts is real but is not journey coverage. This is the honest floor: not every lever moves the number, and L7g's value is the full characterization (the machinery covers the facts; the defining capability is a clean scoped build).

**Two findings chipped/named:** (1) whole-batch loss on persistent Layer-A correction failure — a large multi-intent propose that trips structural validation 3× refuses ALL intents instead of the partial coverage the design promises (chipped); (2) the continuous-walk executor (this entry's fork). See D-207 (multi-intent decomposition) · D-306/D-306.1 (the update-observe machinery this would extend) · D-302 (partial-refusal posture the batch-loss violates).

## D-311 — Layer-A ref-existence goes per-intent: a multi-intent propose with one absent ref no longer refuses the whole batch (partial coverage preserved)

**Date:** 2026-07-03 · **Status:** SHIPPED to main (v2-runtime cadence). No migration. Closes the D-310 whole-batch-loss chip (its finding #1).

**Context.** L7g surfaced a nondeterministic whole-batch loss: a 4–5-intent journey requirement whose one intent's S1 ref did not resolve refused ALL intents (`RefusalKind.STRUCTURAL_VALIDATION_FAILURE`), losing the 3 that would have grounded cleanly (the requirement drafted ~40% of the time across runs). This violated the base-prompt contract (`prompts/base.md`: "the substrate grounds each intent independently … partial coverage with honest dismissals beats forced breadth") and the D-302 partial-refusal posture.

**Root cause — the asymmetry.** `GovernanceCore.check_refs_exist` (the Layer-A **operational** S1-ref-existence check, D-095.1) was all-or-nothing over a multi-intent propose: ANY intent's missing ref → `ok=False` → the runtime rejects the whole call for correction (`runtime.py` `_reject`) → after `DEFAULT_MAX_CORRECTIONS` (3) → `_structural_failure` → whole-batch refusal. But the **semantic** seam one layer down (`resolve_intent`) is already per-intent: it resolves each intent independently, records misses as D-302 `partial_refusals`, and refuses ONLY at zero grounded — and every archetype's `_resolve_one` already carries a defensive "post-check_refs_exist this is defensive" miss branch (`no_relevant_context`). The Layer-A gate short-circuited that machinery before it ran, so those defensive branches were dead code for a slipped-through missing ref. Neither the correction cap nor the feedback string (which already names the offending intent, `intent[i]: …`) was the cause.

**The change (governance-local; spine untouched).** `check_refs_exist` mirrors the semantic seam: reject the whole multi-intent call for correction ONLY when EVERY intent's refs miss (`len(failures) == len(per_intent)`); when ≥1 intent resolves, return `ok=True` and let `resolve_intent` isolate — grounding the valid intents and recording each missing-ref intent as a D-302 `partial_refusal` (its previously-dead defensive branch, now reached). The single-intent path and the all-miss path are unchanged, so the all-miss correction hop is preserved (a fixable typo on a single-intent-equivalent batch still gets its 3 tries), and declared-AC requirements get a further shot at a dropped intent via the D-247 coverage re-prompt. D-095.1 respected: the fix lives entirely in `GovernanceCore`; `runtime.py` is not touched.

**Verification.** DB-free unit — `tests/unit/generation/test_check_refs_partial_coverage.py` (7 cases: all-valid / partial-miss / one-valid → proceed; all-miss / single-miss → reject with per-intent feedback; no-version → reject). Real-S1 integration — `test_multiclaim_vertical.py::test_missing_ref_intent_does_not_sink_grounded_peers` (3 intents, one absent object `Ghost__c` → DRAFT with 2 claims + the ghost recorded under its own re-indexed slot `c2` as a `partial_refusal`); the existing `test_partial_grounding_is_a_draft_with_dismissal` + `test_zero_grounded_refuses` still green. Suites: full generation unit (357) + full integration/generation (176 passed, 1 skipped, against seeded PG) + full DB-free unit (3564) all green; a deterministic runtime-loop repro confirmed the mechanism (all-or-nothing → 0 claims / structural-validation-failure vs proceed-on-partial → DRAFT 3 grounded + 1 partial_refusal). **Rejected alternative:** raise the correction cap / give per-intent feedback — a band-aid that leaves the asymmetry intact (an unfixable ref still sinks the batch, just after more tries). See D-207 (multi-intent decomposition) · D-302 (partial-refusal posture) · D-310 (the chip) · D-247 (coverage re-prompt) · D-095.1 (Layer-A operational / semantic-seam split).

## D-312 — Lever 7g build S0 (renumbered D-312 — D-311 taken by the parallel Layer-A batch-loss fix, the D-309->D-310 precedent): the continuous-record-walk journey — VALIDATED DESIGN BLUEPRINT (design-review panel reworked the shape; re-scoped to TC-054 only → 40/55).

**Date:** 2026-07-03 · **Status:** design ratified, build not yet started. On `phase-s4-l7g-journey-walk`. A 4-lens adversarial DESIGN panel (run BEFORE coding, per the settle-the-boundary discipline) returned **REWORK THE SHAPE** with 5 must-fix + 6 should-address, all verified against real code; this entry is the reworked blueprint.

**Scope correction (honest, vs the D-310 fork's "41/55, incremental D-306 extension").** The panel corrected two over-claims: (1) **TC-054 ONLY → 40/55.** TC-055 needs an approve/reject/submit **action** step type that does not exist (the approval-action executor arc, D-308.1's named deferral) AND env-59's >₹50L approval path is structurally unreachable by data ops (the org's VR blocks the state its auto-submit flow triggers on — the D-308.1 honest-red class). (2) It is NOT a clean incremental extension — it is a new claim kind + a custom canonicalizer + a journey INTERPRETER dispatch branch + a discriminator threaded through the sync AND async production paths + a per-segment temporal k16. First slice is scoped to NON-approval-locking walks (risk recalc / stage progress / formula recompute — the D-306 shapes that teardown cleanly; an approval-pending record refuses delete and locks its parent = a logged leak, D-308.1's watch item).

**The five must-fixes the build MUST honor.**
- **M1 (S6 is single-step → wrong-green risk).** `interpret_run` grades ONE run via first-match `_create_step`/`_mutation_step`/`_assert_step` pickers (each returns `steps[0]` of its type); a journey emitting N asserts would be graded on assert[0] alone → a walk that passes observation-1 but fails observation-3 grades `passed`, a wrong-green into GO/NO-GO. Required: a real journey dispatch branch (selected by `claim_kind`, before the create+assert branch) that walks ALL evidence steps in order and attributes to the FIRST diverging mutation/assert. Seam test: seg-1 passes, seg-3 fails → `journey_diverged` at step 3.
- **M2 (no discriminator → routes into `_run_positive` and mis-parses).** All-positive journey has no `expect_rejection` → routes to `_project_positive` (which hard-rejects >1 update) and `_run_positive` (whose `*head, read, assertion = plan.steps` mis-parses the interleave). Required: a concrete discriminator (a new `recipe_kind='journey-recipe'` with its own `_VALID_RECIPE_KINDS` + bridge gate; a `DataRecipeBody.recipe_shape` marker is the alternative, safe because recipes are excluded from identity §6.3.1), a DISTINCT `JourneyPlan` type (not a `DataRecipePlan` `_run_positive` could unpack), threaded through `build_data_recipe_plan`, `execute_data_recipe`, AND the async `_prepare_async_execute`/`_execute_for_kind` (the scheduler/worker production path). NO shape-sniffing (the D-305.1 implicit-discriminator lesson). Async seam test (world_plans supplied, session=None).
- **M3 (identity: custom canonicalizer + walkable ref list).** Per-step `StateDescriptor.field_values` keys by external_id STRING; every existing state-bearing body (state-transition `subject_fields`, automation-effect `affected_fields`) registers a custom canonicalizer that re-keys on entity_id from an explicit `IdentityBearingRef` list (C1-B rename-stability + D-058 §5.4 coverage walkability — the generic walk skips dict KEYS). Required: a `journey-claim` canonicalizer re-keying every step's state + every observation field/value on entity_id from an explicit per-body ref list (which also feeds coverage), with the OntologyViolationError guard. `steps` + each `observations` marked `ArraySemantics.ORDERED` (a journey is a sequence; reversing it is a different claim). `_identity_safe` at EVERY new ingress (~9+: each state value each step + each observation value). Convergence tests alongside divergence tests. New body version is correct (a v-bump of an existing body re-keys every existing claim — the `AcceptanceClaimUpdateBody` v2 reason); whether a new `claim_kind` (enum migration, MIGRATE-FIRST) vs a v-bump of an existing kind is the open call — mint the new kind only if coverage/decision/S8 genuinely need to distinguish the journey archetype.
- **M4 (per-segment TEMPORAL k16, not global).** k16 today excludes ONE `exclude_field` per grounding call; the override chokepoint computes `observed` from ONE read + `recipe_staged` from CREATES only. A journey stages via updates too and observes at N reads → stage-early-observe-late is a wrong-green. Required: for observation i, its effect field must not appear in step i's state OR any PRIOR step's state (the org, not the recipe, produces it) — but a field observed at step i MAY be human-set in a LATER step (accumulating walks are the point; global-forbid over-refuses). Extend the override chokepoint to compute `observed` over ALL journey reads and `recipe_staged` over ALL creates AND updates. Refuse-not-drop. Wrong-green reproduction test (plant an observed value in step 0's create → refuse).
- **M5 (self-contained `_run_journey`, `_run_positive` UNTOUCHED).** `_run_positive` is a closure over shared mutable state (the `_torn_down` closure, parallel `create_evs`/`record_ids`, global ordinal accounting, the "terminal create" override logic, the self-vs-side-effect 0-row gate) — "extract without changing behavior" is not clean. Preferred (confirmed: the leaf primitives `_read_with_retry`/`_run_ground`/`_mutation_evidence`/`_grade_rejected_create`/`_world_for`/`resolve_field_value_refs`/`CreatedRecordTracker.teardown` are ALREADY module-level standalone): write `_run_journey` as a self-contained step-machine over those primitives, `_run_positive` bit-for-bit untouched, accepting minor create-loop duplication.

**The six should-address (pinned in the slice plan).** S1 re-scope to TC-054/40-55 (above). S2 non-approval-locking first slice (above). S3 per-mutation grade reuses the D-306.1 attribution split EXACTLY — per step declare asserted (rejection → diverged with VR attribution) vs premise-staging (rejection → `_grade_rejected_create` split: semantic-field→failed, padding/ambiguous→errored); no third grammar. S4 per-observation self-vs-side-effect 0-row disambiguation (`_is_self_observation`, D-227.7) + validate every assert's `subject_ref`→paired-read at PLAN time in `_project_journey` (not a runtime raise); mid-walk-read-errors → errored not diverged. S5 the initial create forward-carries the union of required fields any later step's target state depends on (D-310's Annual-Income finding: a mid-walk stage progression can be VR-rejected for an operational gap); an update-provoked required-field rejection is errored (operational) per B2. S6 the journey-vs-decomposition relationship is DETERMINISTIC (the same requirement must not author BOTH a journey-claim AND the D-207 atomics — decide: journey replaces the decomposition for that requirement, or they co-exist and coverage dedupes; a journey refusal must not take the sibling atomics down); verify on the live TC-054 recon.

**Leaner-shape resolution (D-310's ratified lean the first design overrode).** The run outcome is ALREADY a conjunction (passed iff every segment held) — that conjunction IS the journey verdict. Keep M1's journey dispatch branch (so the run is not graded on assert[0]) but resolve explicitly whether to attribute-to-first-diverging-segment using EXISTING verdicts (leaner) vs add two journey verdicts (and pay the `claim_presentation`/phrasing/feedback/`evolution` consumer cost). Lean: existing-verdicts + first-divergence attribution; add journey verdicts only if the composed wording is dishonest.

**Slices (unchanged spine, reworked content).** S0 THIS blueprint. S1 the journey body + canonicalizer + `JourneyPlan` + `recipe-shape` discriminator + `_project_journey` (plan-time assert/read pairing) + `_run_journey` step-machine (M5 self-contained) + enum/recipe-kind migration if minted, seam-tested BOTH directions incl. async. S2 governance (per-segment temporal k16, per-step grade split, forward-carried required state, deterministic journey-vs-decomposition) + emission + the M1 interpreter branch. S3 prompt v17. S4 live TC-054 walk on env-59 (create valid Home Loan → progress to Credit Assessment → observe Risk=Low on the SAME progressed record → observe no approval) + adversarial CODE review + merge.

See D-310 (the fork this builds) · D-306/D-306.1 (the update-observe machinery + the B2 grade law) · D-307/D-307.1 (cross-object + absence + the k16 override chokepoint) · D-305 (the enum-migration precedent) · D-058 §5.4 / D-059 §6.3.3 (coverage walkability + C1-B rename-stability the canonicalizer preserves).

## D-313 — S3 generation: fix the "propose with only acceptance_criteria, no intent_descriptors" persistent-Layer-A decline on large multi-AC requirements (tool-contract + prompt + correction-echo + honest-message + MAX_INTENTS 6→12). **The live failure (req-302, "Home Loan Opportunity Qualification Process", 10 ACs):** the generate job DECLINED with `structural-validation-failure` / "persistent Layer-A correction failure". **Root cause (forensically confirmed, jobs 55/57 on env-59, both prompt @v10 and @v16):** on all 3 correction attempts the LLM called `propose_semantic_intent` with **only `acceptance_criteria`** (the 10 AC labels) and **no `intent_descriptors`** (and no legacy `intent_descriptor`/`requirement_excerpt`); the tool-shape validator `_validate_propose` (`tools.py:413-416`) rejected each with "intent_descriptors is required", the model re-sent the same AC-only shape, `phase_attempt` exceeded `DEFAULT_MAX_CORRECTIONS=3`, and `runtime.py:709` `_structural_failure` emitted the decline. **NOT org-scoping** (generation is correctly per-org via `resolve_connected_org_or_raise`, `run.py:75-76` / `intake.py:51-52`; the ref-existence check `check_refs_exist` was NEVER reached — no refs were proposed) and **NOT the D-311 per-intent batch-loss** (needs proposed refs). Every object/field req-302 names (Opportunity, Task, `Loan_Amount__c`, `Property_Value__c`, `Credit_Score__c`, `Risk_Rating__c`, …) EXISTS in env-59 S1. **Two things make the AC-only shape easy to fall into:** (1) the `propose_semantic_intent` tool `input_schema` marks **nothing** `required` (`"required": []`) and the tool calls are **not `strict`** (no strict plumbing in the LLM path), so the schema is advisory — a call with only the optional `acceptance_criteria` is structurally accepted by the API and only rejected at Layer-A; the tool `description` even leads with "intent_descriptors — preferred" (reads optional). (2) **`MAX_INTENTS = 6` vs req-302's 10 ACs** — a requirement genuinely implying ~10 testable intents cannot be fully expressed in a 6-item array, so even a well-behaved model can't cover it, and the mismatch plausibly nudges the model to declare-ACs-and-stall. **The fix (5 parts, all in S3; no schema/DB migration):** **(#1a) tool contract** — rewrite `PROPOSE_SEMANTIC_INTENT_SCHEMA.description` so `intent_descriptors` is unmistakably the mandatory payload (a call with only `acceptance_criteria` is NOT a proposal). **A top-level `anyOf` was considered but VERIFIED-REJECTED and dropped:** a live Anthropic Messages call with the anyOf-carrying schema returned **HTTP 400 `invalid_request_error` — "input_schema does not support oneOf, allOf, or anyOf at the top level"** (a top-level combinator in a tool `input_schema` breaks EVERY generation call, not just the intended hint), so the mandatory-form contract stays in the `description` + the prompt (which the model reads) with Layer A rejecting the acceptance_criteria-only shape at runtime — no schema combinator. The same live call (no-anyOf schema + the v17 prompt, on `claude-opus-4-7`) returned 200 and the model emitted a 5-entry `intent_descriptors` array (not the AC-only shape) — a positive single-shot signal that the fix produces the array, though the multi-shot worker re-run remains the gate. **(#1b) prompt** — freeze `generation@v17` (= v16 + a strengthened directive: `acceptance_criteria` is a *declaration* only and NEVER a complete proposal; every generation MUST include `intent_descriptors` (≥1), and for an AC-structured requirement one `intent_descriptors` entry per AC — or a `no_admissible_test` intent — in the SAME call); registry `CURRENT` → v17 + recorded drift-guard hash. **(#1c) MAX_INTENTS 6 → 12** (AK's call: generate req-302 FULLY, not the 6-of-10 partial the shape-fix-alone would leave; cost tradeoff = more intents/requirement is accepted). Contained to `tools.py` (def + schema `maxItems` + the `1..N` validator message); `test_multi_intent` references it symbolically so it tracks the new value. **(#2) correction robustness** — the `_validate_propose` "intent_descriptors is required" error now ECHOES the concrete required skeleton (`intent_descriptors:[{requirement_excerpt, archetype_hint, target_subject_hint, polarity_hint}]`), so a model that slips can self-correct within the 3-correction budget (the mechanism lane's "tell it the valid shape, not just that it's wrong" gap — a generic win for every requirement, not just #302). Keeps the leading "intent_descriptors is required" substring (`test_multi_intent` pins it). **(#3) honest user-facing message** — `claim_presentation.py` `structural-validation-failure` text no longer asserts "names objects or fields that do not exist" (misleading: a tool-shape miss and a bad-ref miss both land on this one refusal kind); reworded to cover both — a malformed/incomplete proposal OR references not in the org. **Validation:** offline — full generation unit suite + the eval harness + `_validate_propose` unit tests (AC-only → rejected with the skeleton in the feedback; a 12-item array valid, 13 invalid; the `anyOf`) + the registry drift-guard for v17 + boot. **The offline eval is model-blind** (fixture responses), so it cannot prove the LIVE model now emits `intent_descriptors` — that is the exit gate: a live re-run of req-302 against **env-59 on the worker** (the only place the SF cred key decrypts), watching for the 3 propose calls no longer all `rejected_for_correction`/"intent_descriptors is required" and a non-refusal `generation_outcomes` row with `claims_written` not NULL and coverage of all 10 ACs. Branch `phase-s3-intent-descriptors-shape`; design commit separate from impl; not pushed. See D-207 (the intent_descriptors array + the either/or), D-247 (acceptance_criteria coverage contract), D-088a (operational→structural-validation-failure), D-311 (the per-intent Layer-A path, a DIFFERENT failure class).

## D-313.1 — the REAL root cause of the req-302 decline was the 2048 output-token ceiling (not the tool contract); D-313 was necessary-but-insufficient. Raise `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS` 2048→8192 + `MAX_INTENTS` 12→30. **D-313 shipped (@`4bda8f8`) and DID NOT fix req-302.** Post-deploy verification (job 58, env-59, seq 110, prompt **`generation@v17`** — the deployed fix): the model STILL declined with the same shape — `raw_parameters` = `acceptance_criteria`-only, `n_intent_descriptors=0`, all 3 attempts, EVEN with the strengthened v17 prompt + mandatory-`intent_descriptors` description + the correction skeleton echoed back. **The tell:** every attempt recorded `token_count_output = 2048` EXACTLY (`model=claude-sonnet-5`, requirement 5235 chars / 10 ACs). It is **output-token TRUNCATION**, not a contract/comprehension failure: the model emits the long `acceptance_criteria` array (10 verbose labels) first and is **cut off at the 2048 ceiling before it can write `intent_descriptors`** — so only the completed `acceptance_criteria` survives the tool-use JSON parse, and Layer A rejects it.
