The ceiling is `generation/gateway_binding.py:19 DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 2048`, passed straight into `gateway.tool_turn(max_tokens=…)`; both callers (`run.py:68`, `eval/live.py:40`) rely on the default (neither overrides), and the prod `out=2048` matches it exactly. **Why D-313's smoke gave a false-positive:** it used `max_tokens=3000` + a tiny 3-AC synthetic requirement — it did NOT reproduce prod's 2048 + this large requirement (the "verify with production parameters" lesson). **Live proof of the real cause + the fix (`claude-sonnet-5`, the actual req-302 text, the v17 prompt):** at `max_tokens=2048` → `stop_reason=max_tokens`, `out=2048`, keys `['acceptance_criteria']`, **0 intent_descriptors** (reproduces the exact decline); at `max_tokens=8192` → `stop_reason=tool_use`, `out=4233`, keys `['acceptance_criteria','intent_descriptors']`, **22 intent_descriptors** (a complete proposal covering all 10 ACs). **The fix (2 constants, both live-proven necessary; no schema/DB migration):** **(a) `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS` 2048 → 8192** (`gateway_binding.py`) — the operative fix; a *ceiling*, so normal-size requirements are unaffected (they finish under it) and only large ones use more. **(b) `MAX_INTENTS` 12 → 30** (`tools.py`) — the model produces **22** intents for req-302; with the D-313 cap of 12 the token fix ALONE would just move the failure from "truncated to AC-only" to "22 > 12 → rejected" (`_validate_propose`'s `1..MAX_INTENTS` gate + the schema `maxItems`). 30 covers the observed 22 with headroom = AK's "generate fully". D-313's other pieces (v17 prompt, mandatory description, skeleton echo, honest message) are RETAINED — correct, just insufficient alone. **Follow-on recorded (PENDING, AK):** relook generation model efficiency + design the right per-task/per-complexity model + token budget (a flat 8192 ceiling + one routed `claude-sonnet-5` is blunt; the AC count is known at intake and could scale the budget) — a scheduled design task, not this fix. **Validation:** offline — generation unit suite + a 22-item array now validates + a `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS >= 8192` guard + boot; the exit gate stays a live worker re-run of req-302 on env-59. Branch `phase-s3-gen-token-ceiling`; design commit separate from impl; not pushed. See D-313, D-106.1/D-106.2 (gateway_binding + route_model), D-207.

## D-314 — the UI "Generate/Regenerate" button was a permanent no-op after the first run; add the missing re-queue TRIGGER (`force_rerun`) that completes the migration's documented "retry in place" model — no schema/DB migration. **The symptom (AK, live):** after D-313.1 shipped the token fix, clicking "Regenerate test plan" on req-302 "ran twice, nothing seems to happen" — and the deployed worker never re-ran the requirement, so the D-313.1 exit gate could not be reached from the UI. **Root cause (read-confirmed, not org/token/contract):** `GenerationJobStore.create_or_get_job` (`generation/jobs.py`) enqueues with `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (requirement_key, s1_version_seq) DO NOTHING`. `s1_version_seq` only advances on a new S1 sync, so every generate at the same org-version resolves to the SAME `(requirement_key, s1_version_seq)` row. Once that job reaches a TERMINAL state (`completed`/`failed`/`cancelled`) the `DO NOTHING` returns it unchanged — no new `queued` work — and the worker's `claim_next_queued_job` (which drains `status='queued'`) has nothing to take. req-302's job 58 (the pre-D-313.1 refusal, seq 110) is exactly this dead end: the UI POST resolves to job 58, flashes "Generating…", the page polls, but the job is already `completed` so the poll immediately stops and nothing runs. Verified live: no job 59+ was created by the two clicks; the queue held 40 jobs, all `completed`. **The design this completes:** the base-table migration `20260525_0020` documents the intent explicitly — "*one logical request, ever (S3 retries **in place** via start_attempt* … *retried in place via start_attempt*)" — deliberately choosing retry-in-place over v1's "new job after terminal" partial-unique. `start_attempt` already mints a fresh `request_id` + bumps `attempt_count` (`s3_generation_job_attempts` owns the per-run history); the ONLY missing piece was a trigger to move a terminal job back to `queued` so the consumer re-runs it. So this is a completion of the recorded model, not a new architecture, and needs no migration (the full `UNIQUE(requirement_key, s1_version_seq)` stays). **The fix (all S3 + the two v1 user-trigger routes; no schema/DB migration):** **(a) `create_or_get_job(…, force_rerun=False)`** — when `force_rerun=True` and the conflicting row is TERMINAL, `ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE SET status='queued'` + clear the run fields (`current_request_id`, `progress_pct/msg`, `claimed_at`/`started_at`/`completed_at`/`heartbeat_at`, `error_code`/`error_message`) + refresh the enqueue-pinned fields to THIS trigger (`requirement_text`, `environment_id`, `s1_version_name`, `created_by` from `EXCLUDED`), guarded `WHERE s3_generation_jobs.status IN ('completed','failed','cancelled')`. `attempt_count` is intentionally NOT reset so `start_attempt` bumps the retry lineage (2, 3, …). The terminal guard makes a re-click during an ACTIVE run (`queued`/`claimed`/`running`) a **no-op** — the `DO UPDATE` matches nothing, the in-flight job + its attempt are untouched, and the trailing SELECT still returns the running job (double-click safe; Postgres locks the conflicting row so a concurrent pair yields exactly one re-queue → one worker claim). `force_rerun=False` is byte-identical to the prior `DO NOTHING` — the auto/scheduled/repair callers stay idempotent, so there is no re-generate storm (there is no scheduled S3 enqueuer today regardless). **(b)** thread `force_rerun` through `intake.enqueue_s3_generation` + `s3_generation_console.trigger_s3_generation`. **(c)** the two EXPLICIT user "Generate/Regenerate" triggers pass `force_rerun=True`: the HTMX route `POST /requirements/<id>/generate-substrate` (`views.py`) and the API generate-enqueue `POST` (`views.py`). The rest of the UX loop already exists and is unchanged — `requirements/detail.html` renders the "Regenerate test plan" form when the latest job is terminal, swaps to the progress panel + polls `/api/s3-generation-jobs/<id>` every 3 s while the job is `active`, and reloads on `completed` so the new claims appear; the re-queue simply flips the job back to `active` on the redirect so that machinery re-engages. **Validation:** offline — 6 new `test_s3_generation_jobs` cases (terminal→re-queued in place, same row/id, run fields cleared, `attempt_count` preserved + next attempt = 2; a `failed` job re-queued + error cleared; `force_rerun=False` leaves a terminal job untouched; an ACTIVE job is NOT disturbed; a never-generated key is a plain create; enqueue-pinned fields refreshed) + the full generation unit (361) + integration (182) suites green + boot. **The live exit gate (unchanged and now REACHABLE from the UI):** click Regenerate on req-302 (env-59) → job 58 re-queues → the deployed worker (≥`adc6296`, 8192 ceiling) runs it → a non-refusal `generation_outcomes` row with ~22 intent_descriptors covering all 10 ACs, and the page reloads to show the test plan — closing the D-313/D-313.1 gate. **Adversarial review (3-lens parallel + refute pass) — 3 CONFIRMED findings applied, 1 refuted:** **(F1, major)** the S3 API enqueue route `api_s3_generation_enqueue` validated the client-supplied `environment_id` with only `get_environment` (tenant-scope), not `is_environment_accessible` (group-scope) — the outlier vs the UI generate route + the S4 async API, and `force_rerun=True` escalated the pre-existing gap to *repeated* LLM cost against a group-inaccessible env → added the D-245 group-scope `403 FORBIDDEN` gate, mirroring `api_s4_execution_enqueue`. **(F2, minor)** on an ACTIVE job `force_rerun` correctly no-ops but the UI flashed a false "Generating…" success and silently dropped the user's edited inputs → the UI route now flashes an honest "a run is already in progress; regenerate again afterward" (`info`) when the returned status is `claimed`/`running`. **(F3, minor)** the `DO UPDATE` refreshed `created_by = EXCLUDED.created_by`, silently transferring job OWNERSHIP (the cancel endpoint gates on `created_by`) to whoever last clicked Regenerate → dropped that one column from the refresh so ownership/cancel-rights stay with the original creator (inputs `requirement_text`/`environment_id`/`s1_version_name` still refresh — same org by the seq-scope invariant). **Refuted:** a "reaper re-queues a job while its original worker still runs → two concurrent `run_generation`" finding — killed because the worker is single-threaded per tenant tick (no two concurrent workers for one job). **Follow-up (noted, not this slice):** the repair-agent re-enqueue (`repair_agent.py`) hits the same `DO NOTHING` dead end at a fixed seq and stays `force_rerun=False` here — a separate decision (an automated re-generate has different idempotency needs than an explicit human click). Branch `phase-s3-ui-regenerate` (touches S3 + the v1 web layer; ff to main at close, D-313 precedent); design commit separate from impl; not pushed. See D-106.4 (the two-layer idempotency + retry-in-place model this completes), D-313/D-313.1 (the token/contract fix whose exit gate this unblocks), D-130.A (S4's partial-active-unique — the alternative "new row after terminal" model, deliberately NOT mirrored here since S3 chose retry-in-place).

## D-315 — a "Run status" panel under the requirement Test plan: the last generation run's status + what it produced + the LLM model/cost that produced it (read-only; no schema). **Ask (AK):** "a status section just under Test plan on a requirement so we can see the status of the run — model and cost etc." **Where the data lives (three sources, one reader):** the JOB (`s3_generation_jobs` — status/attempt_count/timing), the OUTCOME (`generation_outcomes` — `jsonb_array_length(claims_written)` = tests produced, `outcome_kind`), and the LLM COST (`public.llm_usage_log` — `model`/`input_tokens`/`output_tokens`/`cost_usd`/`prompt_version`). **The cost-attribution seam:** generation's gateway calls are NOT tagged with a `requirement_id` — `build_tool_turn_fn` (`gateway_binding.py`) passes only `task`+`model`, so `llm_usage_log.requirement_id` is NULL for generation rows. Attribution is therefore by **(`tenant_id`, `task='generation'` [= `GENERATION_TASK`, `run.py`], `ts` within the job's `[claimed_at, completed_at]` window)** — reliable because the worker runs one generation per tenant **sequentially** (one `claim_next_queued_job` per tenant per tick), so within a job's window the `generation` calls are that job's; a D-314 re-run resets `claimed_at`, so the window tracks the LATEST run (the panel shows the current run's cost, not stale prior-attempt cost). The window read reaches `public.llm_usage_log` because the tenant conn's `search_path` includes `public`. A tagged-attribution upgrade (thread `requirement_id`/our `request_id` through `build_tool_turn_fn` → exact, not window-based) is a noted future option — deferred because it changes the substrate write path and doesn't help already-written rows; the window is precise for the single-worker queue. **Implementation (all read-only; no schema/DB migration):** **(a)** `s3_generation_console._read_generation_run_status(conn, tenant_id, key, *, now)` runs the three reads + `_shape_run_status(job, outcome, llm, *, now)` — a PURE shaper (duration = `completed_at`−`claimed_at`, or `now`−`claimed_at` while active; `tz`-naive `now` swallowed to `None` so it never 500s the page) — behind the best-effort `read_generation_run_status(tenant_id, key)` (never raises; `{available, run}`). `_GENERATION_TASK='generation'` is a literal (not an import of the generation runtime onto the requirement page) drift-guarded in tests against `run.GENERATION_TASK`. **(b)** the requirement detail route passes `gen_run` to the template. **(c)** `requirements/detail.html` renders a "Run status" card **just under the Test plan card** — a status badge (green/red/gray/indigo by state) + a stat grid: Tests produced · Model · Cost (`$%.4f`) · Tokens (in/out) · LLM calls · Attempts · Duration · Finished/Started (title=prompt version) + a red error row on `failed`. Rendered only once a run exists (the Test-plan card already owns the never-generated empty state); a queued/never-claimed job shows the status with `—` for cost (nothing ran yet); an in-flight run shows `—` for cost until the existing page poll reloads on completion. **Validation:** 6 pure `_shape_run_status` unit tests (completed+llm, active-uses-now, queued-no-duration, failed-surfaces-error, naive-now-no-crash, task-literal drift-guard) + the console integration suite + boot + a Jinja compile + an isolated panel render proving the formatting (`completed · 22 tests · claude-sonnet-5 · $0.0123 · 1000/4233 · 12 s`). Same branch `phase-s3-ui-regenerate` as D-314 (companion requirement-page work); design commit separate from impl; not pushed. See D-314 (the re-run trigger this observes), D-206.1 (the refusal-visibility surface it sits beside), migration 031 (`llm_usage_log`), D-313.1 ([[model-efficiency-relook]] — the per-task budget work this panel now makes visible).

## D-316 — the D-315 single-run panel becomes a "Generation history" TABLE — ALL runs, newest first, each with status + tests-produced + LLM model/cost + any error/refusal reason (read-only; no schema). **Ask (AK, immediately after D-315 shipped):** "it's only showing last generating — I want to see all the generations on that requirement; a table, most recent at top, with the status and any error message." **The unit of "a generation" is an ATTEMPT** (`s3_generation_job_attempts`): D-314's retry-in-place means a re-run REUSES the job row and mints a fresh attempt (own `request_id`), so the job table alone (one row per S1 version) hides re-runs — the attempts table is the true per-run history. Live-confirmed on req-302: **4 runs across 3 jobs** — seq 100 (Opus 4.7, refused, $0.99), seq 108 (Sonnet-5, refused, $0.16), seq 110 att#1 (Sonnet-5, refused, $0.17) then att#2 (Sonnet-5, **generated 16 tests**, $0.35) — the D-313.1 success is att#2, exactly the history the single panel was hiding. **Implementation (all read-only; replaces the D-315 single-run reader; no schema/DB migration):** **(a)** `_read_generation_runs(conn, tenant_id, key, *, now, limit=50)` runs ONE query joining each attempt → its job (`s1_version_seq`, `error_message`) → its outcome (`generation_outcomes` by `request_id` — `draft`/`refusal` + `claims_written`) → a per-attempt LLM cost `LATERAL` (`public.llm_usage_log`, `task='generation'`, `ts` within `[a.started_at, a.finished_at]` — attempts are sequential per tenant so windows never overlap), ordered `started_at DESC`. **(b)** `_shape_run_row(row, *, now)` — a PURE shaper — merges the attempt status with the outcome into ONE `status_label`/`status_tone` (running=indigo · failed=red · cancelled=gray · refusal→"refused"=amber · draft+tests→"generated"=green · draft+0+existing→"matched existing" · draft+0→"no new tests") and a `detail` = the refusal reason (`refusal_plain`) or the failure error (`attempt_error_code` → `job_error_message`). **(c)** `read_generation_runs(tenant_id, key)` best-effort (`{available, runs}`); the route passes `gen_runs`; `requirements/detail.html` renders a scrollable table under the Test plan (When [+ `S1 v{seq} · attempt N`] · Status badge · Tests · Model · Cost [tokens on hover] · Duration · Details) — rendered only once a run exists. The D-315 `read_generation_run_status`/`_shape_run_status` single-run reader is REMOVED (subsumed). **Validation:** 9 pure `_shape_run_row` unit tests (generated/refused/failed/failed-fallback-to-job-message/running-uses-now/matched-existing/no-new-tests/naive-now-no-crash/task-drift-guard) + the console integration suite + boot + a Jinja compile + a LIVE `read_generation_runs('req-302')` returning the real 4-run history (verified above). Branch `phase-s3-gen-history` (touches the S3 v1-bridge + web layer; ff to main at close, D-313 precedent); design commit separate from impl; not pushed. See D-315 (the single-run panel this replaces), D-314 (re-runs that mint the attempts this lists), D-106.4 (`s3_generation_job_attempts` = the per-run history B-layer this reads).

## D-317 — behavioral test intents fail "subject None:None did not resolve" because the LLM names the subject object under `object`, not `{entity_type, sf_api_name}`; normalize `object` → the entity ref at the single funnel — no schema. **The symptom (AK, live on req-302):** the generation "declined 32 of the proposed tests", 32× `ACn: … subject None:None did not resolve at version 110`. **Root cause (forensically confirmed from the STORED raw model output, `llm_calls.raw_parameters` for outcome `ca14d498`):** the subject-resolvers read `target_subject_hint.{entity_type, sf_api_name}` (`governance_core.py:1006-1010` behavioral path + `:911` check_refs_exist default branch; `AdmissibilityEngine.resolve_subject`). The model emits that entity-ref shape ONLY for `existence-claim`; for EVERY behavioral kind it names the subject under `object` alongside the claim-kind fields — `prohibition-claim` `{object, operation, rejection_conditions}`, `state-transition-claim` `{object, trigger_field, expected_value, …}`, `automation-effect-claim` `{object, automation_name, effect_object, …}`, `acceptance-claim` `{object, acceptance_conditions, …}` — so `hint.get("entity_type")`/`get("sf_api_name")` are both None → `None:None` refuse, even though the object IS named. Per the raw params: of 48 proposed intents (2 propose calls, 22+26), the 8+8 existence-claims resolved and the 32 behavioral ones all failed on the shape. The model's rich shape is CORRECT in spirit — the pipeline already expects `rejection_conditions` INSIDE `target_subject_hint` (`governance_core.py:1094`) — it just uses `object` for the entity name; the tool schema declares `target_subject_hint` as a bare `{"type":"object","description":"An S1 entity reference or a descriptive selector."}` (no property enum, non-strict), so `object` is within contract. **The fork (AK chose A):** **A (chosen)** — accept `object` at the resolver (deterministic, fixes all behavioral kinds + existing + future, no dependence on the non-strict model); **B** — prompt/schema force `{entity_type, sf_api_name}` (fragile: the model reliably prefers `object`, matching the rest of the hint; only helps future runs; non-deterministic live re-verify). **The fix (one point, no schema/DB migration):** `tools.py` `_inject_subject_entity_ref(desc)` — when `target_subject_hint` is a dict with NEITHER `entity_type` NOR `sf_api_name` but a string `object`, inject `{entity_type:"Object", sf_api_name:<object>}` on a COPY (non-destructive: `object` + the claim-kind fields stay for their resolvers; an explicit ref or a Field-subject existence-claim is untouched; a genuinely-absent object still fails ref-existence — no fake-green). Called by `normalize_propose_input` — the SINGLE funnel both `check_refs_exist` and `resolve_intent` use — for the array AND legacy-singular forms (legacy copies the descriptor first so the caller's raw params, later persisted to `llm_calls.raw_parameters`, are never mutated). **Validation:** **deterministic replay proof (real model output + real env-59 S1, NO LLM):** the 48 stored `ca14d498` intents → `normalize_propose_input` → `resolve_subject` at seq 110 = **16/48 resolve BEFORE → 48/48 AFTER (+32 newly grounded)** — exactly the 32 declines. Plus 6 `test_multi_intent` unit cases (inject / explicit-ref-not-overwritten / no-object-left-alone / no-caller-mutation / legacy-form) + 2 `test_refusal_vertical` integration cases driving an `object`-shaped hint through the REAL `check_refs_exist` (Account resolves; `NoSuchObject__x` still refuses) + the full generation unit+integration suite (548→green). **Adversarial review (3-lens + refute): 1 CONFIRMED nit, applied** — the `object` subject-key is an EMERGENT model convention (no prompt/fragment documents it; only `{entity_type, sf_api_name}` is documented) and no test drove the `object`→resolve path end-to-end, so a future prompt/model drift away from `object` would SILENTLY regress behavioral subjects to the pre-fix refusal (a SAFE failure — a refusal, never a wrong-green — but silent). Closed the test half (the 2 integration cases fail loudly if the injection is removed or the resolver drifts). **Deferred follow-up (nit's other half):** document the `object` subject-key in `prompts/fragments/data_behavior.md` so prompt + substrate agree (needs a prompt version bump) + a periodic live eval to catch MODEL-convention drift (a hand-built fixture can't). Branch `phase-s3-subject-hint-object`; design commit separate from impl; not pushed. See D-293 (the prohibition behaviour-instance `{object, operation, rejection_conditions}` contract the model mirrors into the hint), D-294/D-295 (the rejection_conditions grounding this unblocks), D-207 (`normalize_propose_input`, the funnel), D-313/D-313.1 (the token fix that first let the model emit all 48 intents, surfacing this).

## D-318 — automation-effect intents decline "automation-effect needs a verifiable effect" because grounding requires the LLM to NAME the org's internal Flow; bind the Flow by the EFFECT it produces instead — parse the Flow's already-synced Metadata, no schema. **The symptom (AK, live on req-302 after D-317):** "the engine declined 14 of the proposed tests — automation-effect needs a verifiable effect: `field_name`+`expected_value` on the subject, or `effect_object`+`effect_lookup_field`; only 15 test cases generated although the log says 29." **Root cause (forensically confirmed from `llm_calls.raw_parameters` + env-59 S1):** automation-effect grounding demanded `automation_name == flow.sf_api_name` at BOTH the admissibility gate (`governance_core.py:640-671`) AND the binding block (`:1466-1527`). The LLM cannot know the org's internal Flow api-name (`HL_Auto_Risk_Rating`) from a business requirement ("Risk Rating is automatically set"), so it invents names (`RiskRatingAssignment`) → no name-match → refuse — **even though env-59 HAS those Flows, edge-connected to Opportunity (`TRIGGERS_ON`), and their effect is already in S1**: each Flow entity's `attributes['Metadata']` carries `recordUpdates[].inputAssignments[] = {field, value}` (same-record effect) and `recordCreates[].object` (cross-object effect). The model already supplies the effect it wants tested (`field_name`+`expected_value`, or `effect_object`); it just can't name the mechanism that produces it. **The fork (AK chose "same-record + cross-object" scope; Design A over B):** **A (chosen)** — bind the Flow by matching the claim's declared effect against each neighborhood Flow's parsed Metadata (find the Flow that *verifiably produces* the effect); removes the internal-name requirement, resolves the D-299 "which of 3 Flows?" ambiguity **by the effect itself**, and is **strictly safer than today's name-match** (which never verified the named Flow's effect). **B (rejected)** — steer these to `acceptance-claim`: an acceptance-claim asserts only that a record *saves*, not that the org *produced* the effect — it would pass even if the Flow were deleted (a wrong-green); `GroundedAutomationEffect` exists precisely to observe-the-org (create WITHOUT the field, let the org stamp it, read back — the k16 exclude). **The fix (Slices 1–3; reads Metadata already in S1 → no sync change, no schema, no migration):** **Slice 1** — new pure `flow_effects(attributes)` in `semantic/entity_attributes.py` (appended to the D-203.1 shape-tolerant extractor family): parses `Metadata.recordUpdates[].inputAssignments[]` → `same_record` = `frozenset[(bare_field, literal_scalar|None)]` and `recordCreates[].object` → `cross_object` = `frozenset[object_api]`; any non-dict/non-list at any level → skipped, never raises. **Slice 2 (riskiest)** — `governance_core._flows_producing_effect(flows, field, value, object)` = the subset whose parsed effect contains the claim's effect (same-record: bare-field-tail match + typed-tolerant value equality; cross-object: `effect_object` present). Wired (a) at the **gate** (`_evaluate_positive`, effect hints `expected_value`/`effect_object` threaded through `evaluate` from the call site) as a fallback AFTER the name/approval/calc-field attempts miss, and (b) at the **binding block** — Rule 2 (name given, no name-match): 1 producer → bind, >1 → refuse ambiguous ("produce the claimed effect"), 0 → refuse; Rule 4 (no name): 1 producer → bind, else `flows[0]` fallback (preserving the downstream calc-field rebind + single-flow no-name floor). Exact name-match stays the fast path — the **D-304 formula / D-308 approval name-only primitives run BEFORE the effect-resolver and are untouched**. Seed test flows are Metadata-less → `flow_effects` returns empty → every pre-D-318 test falls back to today's name-trust/`flows[0]` behavior (zero regression). **Slice 3** — deterministic replay (req-302's real intents from `llm_calls.raw_parameters` + env-59's real `HL_Auto_Risk_Rating`/`HL_High_Risk_Task` Metadata, NO LLM): the previously-refused automation-effect intents flip **0 → 4 PROCEED** (Risk-Rating High/Medium/Low bands + the Task create), the rest refuse HONESTLY (LTV `Loan_to_Value__c` has no `expected_value` + is not a record-triggered stamp; the approval is name-bound) — no fake-green. **Validation:** 6 `flow_effects` unit + 4 `_flows_producing_effect` unit + 6 `test_automation_bind_by_effect` integration (no-name bind / invented-name bind [the req-302 case] / no-producer still-refuses / cross-object bind / ambiguity refuses / naming-one-of-two binds) over an isolated `Loan__c` island fixture + full generation+semantic suite **593 green** + boot. **Adversarial review (3-lens: wrong-green / regression / extractor + refute pass; 5 raw → 4 CONFIRMED all minor, 1 REFUTED):** **(fixed)** numeric value miss — the effect comparator used `_identity_safe` (canonicalizes only float→repr), so a numeric effect (LLM `expected_value` int `110`/str `"110"` vs a Flow's `numberValue` float `110.0`) silently missed → refuse (coverage loss, direction is miss→refuse, NEVER wrong-green); replaced with S3-local `_effect_values_equal` mirroring the S4 D-211 typed-tolerant comparator (bool-guarded, numeric-when-both-parse) — kept local, NOT imported from S4, to respect the substrate boundary. **(fixed)** `flow_effects` could raise `TypeError: unhashable` on a dict/list under a scalar value-key (not reachable from spec-conformant Salesforce data, but violated the extractor's never-raises contract) — `_flow_assignment_value` now returns only hashable scalars (a non-scalar → no-literal `None`). **(noted)** the new integration test file was untracked → `git add` at commit. **(REFUTED)** the "`flow_effects` conflates `$Record` vs related-record updates = wrong-green" finding was proven NOT wrong-green — the emission independently re-verifies the effect field `BELONGS_TO` the subject and the recipe reads back the SUBJECT's field, so a related-record contamination lands on red-or-refuse (safe), never a false GO; the underlying `$Record`-precision refinement is a safe, deferred follow-up. **Slice 4 (prompt v18 freeze):** `data_behavior.md` now tells the model it does NOT need to name the internal Flow (describe the effect; the substrate binds by it) and to set `automation_name` ONLY to break a same-effect tie — approvals stay name-required (D-308) and calculated fields name the computed field (D-304), both preserved verbatim; it also documents the `target_subject_hint.object` behavioral subject-key (closing the D-317 prompt-doc follow-up). Frozen to `generation@v18` via the compose→freeze→register ritual (`CURRENT`=v18, sha recorded, guard-test bumped). **The freeze surfaced — and this slice fixes — a pre-existing working-source drift: the D-313 intent-mandatory directive (`the intent_descriptors array IS the proposal`) lived ONLY in the frozen v17 file, having drifted out of the working `base.md`, so composing v18 from the working source would have SILENTLY DROPPED it (regressing the very fix that let req-302 emit all its intents). Restored both D-313 passages into `base.md` verbatim from v17 (compose_working() now differs from v17 by exactly the intended automation_name + object-key edits) and added a new registry guard `test_working_source_composes_to_current` asserting `compose_working() == get(CURRENT)` — the drift class the frozen-hash guard structurally cannot catch (it only catches edits to already-frozen files, not content that drifts out of the working source before a freeze).** Slice-4 adversarial review (3-lens + refute, 7 agents): 4 raw → 0 CONFIRMED, 4 refuted (the drift-guard-gap the one real-but-safe observation, now closed by that test; the review verified v18 STRENGTHENS the approval-name guard — 3 in-prompt directives to name approvals vs v17's 1). **Deferred:** the `$Record`/related-record precision filter (safe today) + the LIVE worker re-generate of req-302 on env-59 (the exit gate — the risk-rating-band + Task automation declines should turn into real tests; LTV/approval honestly refuse). Branch `phase-s3-automation-effect-bind`; design commit separate from impl; not pushed. See D-299 (name-required Flow disambiguation this generalizes to effect-binding), D-304 (calc-field/formula primitive — name-only, runs before the effect-resolver, untouched), D-308 (approval-process primitive — name-only, untouched), D-317 (the subject-normalize fix that let these 29 behavioral intents emit in the first place), D-204 (the raw-`attributes` storage contract these extractors read), D-211 (`data_executor._values_equal`, the typed-tolerant comparator `_effect_values_equal` mirrors).

## D-319 — cross-object automation-effect `effect_field`/`effect_lookup_field` falsely refuse a BARE field name; tolerate the bare tail (no prompt/schema). **The symptom (live req-302 on env-59, v18):** an `automation-effect-claim` asserting a created Task's `Subject` declined `emission-deferred` "effect field 'Subject' does not exist on Task" — but **`Task.Subject` IS synced** (39 Task fields at seq 110). **Root cause:** `_ground_cross_object_effect` (`governance_core.py:~2118`) builds `eff_fields = {r.entity.sf_api_name: r.entity}` keyed by the FULLY-QUALIFIED api name (`"Task.Subject"`), then looks up the model's hint DIRECTLY (`eff_fields.get(hint["effect_field"])`); the LLM sent the BARE `effect_field="Subject"` (it qualifies `effect_lookup_field="Task.WhatId"` but not `effect_field` — the prompt gives no qualified example for the effect field) → miss → false refuse. Same bare-vs-qualified class D-317 fixed for the SUBJECT. **Fix (mirror the bare-keyed `_grounding_field_metadata:497`):** key `eff_fields` by the BARE tail (`sf_api_name.rsplit(".",1)[-1]`) and bare-tail both hint lookups; field api-names are unique per Object so the tail is unambiguous; the bound endpoint keeps the entity's qualified `sf_api_name` (emitted SOQL / asserted field unchanged — only the lookup key changed). **Validation:** live replay on real env-59 (`_ground_cross_object_effect` on the actual AC10 hint → GROUNDED, `effect_field=Task.Subject`) + 2 integration tests (bare `effect_field`, bare `effect_lookup_field` on the `Order__c`→`Order_Log__c` fixture) + full generation+semantic suite **602 green** + a 3-lens adversarial review (wrong-green/precedence/regression: **0 findings**). Branch `phase-s3-approval-bind-and-effect-field` (co-slice with D-320); design commit separate from impl; not pushed. See D-317 (the same bare-vs-qualified class for the subject), D-318 (`_flows_producing_effect`'s bare-tail field matching this mirrors).

## D-320 — extend bind-by-effect to APPROVAL processes: the LLM can't name the org's internal approval, so bind the single active approval on the subject by its ProcessInstance effect (mirror D-318 by ENUMERATION; no schema/migration). **The symptom (live req-302 on env-59, v18):** an approval `automation-effect-claim` (`effect_object="ProcessInstance"`) declined `ungrounded-claim` "the org has no rule or configuration backing this" — but env-59 HAS exactly ONE active approval on Opportunity (`HL_High_Value_Loan`, live-verified in the subject's neighborhood at seq 110). **Root cause (forensic, from `llm_calls.raw_parameters`):** the model sent `automation_name="<UNKNOWN>"` — it cannot know the org's internal approval-process api-name. D-308 binds approvals BY NAME only; D-318's effect-resolver binds only Flows (`_flows_producing_effect` reads `flow_effects`; an approval-process is a flat ProcessDefinition carrying no Flow Metadata) → the gate dismisses (`insufficient_grounding`). The exact "can't name the internal automation" problem D-318 solved for Flows, not yet extended to approvals. **Fix (mirror D-318's rule-4; the ApprovalProcess already `TRIGGERS_ON` the subject and is in its scoped neighborhood — the D-308 name paths already read it, so NO schema change):** two module helpers — `_active_approvals(neighborhood)` (the active-ApprovalProcess twin of the `flows` list) + `_names_a_subject_approval(neighborhood, name)` (True when `name` matches a real approval on the subject, active OR inactive — a deliberate reference that must NOT be overridden). **GATE** (`_evaluate_positive`): after the `_flows_producing_effect` check, when still ungrounded AND `effect_object=="ProcessInstance"` AND the name doesn't reference a real subject approval, admit if a single active approval exists. **BINDING** (a local `_approval_binding()` closure called in BOTH the named-unresolved fallback AND the no-name branch, BEFORE the D-318 Flow resolver): gated on `effect_object=="ProcessInstance"`; skip when the name references a real approval (respect it); else 1 active approval → bind (`primitive="approval_process"`), >1 → refuse ambiguous ("name the specific approval process" — the D-299/D-318 law), 0 → refuse. So a `<UNKNOWN>`/invented/absent name all fall through to the enumeration, while a **named real approval is left to the name paths — active binds (D-308), inactive refuses (D-301) — never silently rebound to a different active approval**. Emission is name-free already (uses `automation.external_id` + `automation_primitive`); `_ground_cross_object_effect` still verifies `ProcessInstance`+`TargetObjectId`. **Safety:** the gate and the binding use the SAME `_names_a_subject_approval` + `effect_object=="ProcessInstance"` guard, so the gate never admits what the binding refuses — a real over-call surface: an early build regressed `test_inactive_approval_process_never_grounds` (it rebound the active approval when the model named the INACTIVE one), fixed by that shared guard. **Validation:** live replay on real env-59 (gate admits + binding binds `HL_High_Value_Loan` with `automation_name="<UNKNOWN>"`; the D-301 inactive-name path + the named-real suppression both hold) + 4 integration tests (nameless single-bind / invented-name binds [the req-302 case] / >1-active refuses-ambiguous [an isolated `Deal__c` two-approval island] / naming-one-of-two binds) + 2 `_active_approvals`/`_names_a_subject_approval` units + full generation+semantic suite **602 green** + a 3-lens adversarial review (wrong-green/precedence/regression: **0 findings**). **Prompt v19 (built):** `data_behavior.md` now makes the approval-process name OPTIONAL — mirroring the D-318 Flow guidance ("you do NOT need to name the approval process; the substrate binds the single approval on the object; name it ONLY to break a tie when the object has >1"); calculated fields stay named (D-304) and the D-308 approval BLOCK (ProcessInstance/TargetObjectId/expected_absence) is otherwise intact. Frozen to `generation@v19` via the compose→freeze→register ritual; the `test_working_source_composes_to_current` drift guard (D-318) stays green and a v19-vs-v18 line-diff confirms exactly the intended approval edits (no drift); its own 2-lens adversarial review returned 0 findings. The substrate fix (above) already clears AC9 on v18; v19 only stops the model emitting the `<UNKNOWN>` placeholder. Branch `phase-s3-approval-bind-and-effect-field` (co-slice with D-319); design commit separate from impl; not pushed. See D-318 (Flow bind-by-effect this mirrors for approvals), D-308 (the name-only approval binding this extends), D-301 (the active-only law), D-299 (the wrong-automation class the ambiguity refuse prevents).

## D-321 — the READABLE test-case body: a derived read-side projection that renders a claim as a verbose, plain-language test case (title / "what this checks" / preconditions / test data / steps / expected result) above the unchanged raw dump. Deterministic-first, two stages; NO schema, NO substrate, NO identity/anchor work. **The gap:** the claim-detail page (`/claims/<test_id>` → `claims_detail`) jumped from the one-line title straight to `render_value`'s raw `asserted_truth` dump (`ref_kind pinned, entity_id …, body_schema_version 1`); a BA/QA never got the recognizable middle. **Decision (like coverage — derived, not stored):** a read-time projection reads a claim + its current recipes + the org label map and produces a typed readable body; the claim stays canonical, the technical detail stays exactly where it was, one click below. **Stage 1 — deterministic skeleton, no LLM (`intelligence/readable_body.py::build_readable_body`):** a PURE, never-raises function → a frozen `ReadableBodySkeleton` (headline / depth / checks / preconditions / test_data / steps / expected_result / probes / grounded_tokens / skeleton_content_hash). It COMPOSES the existing D-206/D-267 spine helpers (`claim_presentation.claim_title / claim_depth / _ref_name / _label / _object_label_of / _expected_value / _first_field_change / _property_sentence`) + `entity_labels.label_map` — the "keep API names / flow names / schema terms OUT of the spine" rules are reused, not re-derived. All seven v1 kinds get a shape: existence/property → headline + a one-line configuration-check gloss (behavioral sections omitted); value/prohibition/acceptance(v1+v2 update)/state-transition/automation-effect(v1 field-change/blocked + v2 absence) → the full body; an UNREGISTERED kind is ENVELOPE-ONLY (headline + a grounded target/subject line + conditions; steps/test-data/expected OMITTED — it never reads a recipe, never fabricates steps). **KEY (drives the design):** for an automation-effect/value-band claim the boundary INPUT (e.g. 649) lives ONLY in the recipe's create `field_values` (+ free-form `triggering_action.description`), NOT in `asserted_truth` (see D-303/D-300) — so Test-data + Steps read the recipe (`observation_realization.steps`, a NEW `_recipe_step_narration` — `claim_presentation.step_plain` narrates S4 EVIDENCE steps, a different shape, and is NOT reused); a `strategy_kind=='bva'` claim with >1 data-recipe (`coordinator.current_data_recipe_ids`) surfaces its probes as "Boundary cases". `skeleton_content_hash` = `sha256(canonical_serialize(<rendered facts> + SKELETON_SHAPE_VERSION))` — the `identity_hash_version` discipline (D-059), a SEPARATE presentation hash that never touches `identity_hash`/`test_id`/the claim schema. `grounded_tokens` is DERIVED as a SUPERSET of every named token rendered (a final `_ground_all` pass over the assembled strings), so a faithful restatement can never be flagged. **Stage 2 — constrained LLM phrasing + fail-loud validator (`intelligence/readable_body_phrasing.py`, mirrors the D-117 interpretation-phrasing enricher):** Haiku restates the skeleton into `{plain_terms, step_narration[]}` (task `readable_body_phrasing_generation`, Haiku chain in `router._CHAINS`, prompt `llm/prompts/readable_body_phrasing.py`, invent-nothing SYSTEM). A deterministic grounding validator (`_validate_grounding` over the shared `readable_body.extract_named_tokens`) confirms every number, quoted literal, and multi-word label span in the prose is in `grounded_tokens` — any miss FAILS LOUD (`log.warning` with the offending tokens) and the reader falls back to the Stage-1 baseline; the reader NEVER sees unverified prose. Numbers/quotes are strict (reject-on-doubt — catches a fabricated boundary "650" when the skeleton grounds "649"); label spans are stop-word-trimmed ("The Loan" → single word, not label-checked) so ordinary rephrasing never false-positives (residual: a single-word fabricated field is not caught — the value vector is). **Fork — cache WITHOUT a schema change:** the D-117 precedent persists phrasing to `s6_interpretations.phrasing` via migration 050; deliberately NOT copied. v1 uses a PROCESS-LOCAL, content-addressed LRU keyed `(skeleton_content_hash, PROMPT_VERSION)` — no table, no migration; a warm process serves repeats free, a cold process re-phrases once, loss on restart is acceptable (best-effort, Stage-1 always available). A durable cross-process cache is a deliberate FUTURE decision (would need a migration). **Fork — flag WITHOUT a schema change:** gated OFF by a global env constant `PLIMSOL_READABLE_BODY_PHRASING` (not a new per-tenant column); `readable_body_phrasing_enabled(db, tenant_id)` accepts args for a future per-tenant gate that would reuse an existing settings flag. **Wire-in (last):** `s3_generation_console._read_claim_detail` (the existing best-effort read) now surfaces `strategy_kind` + `current_data_recipe_ids`, builds the skeleton in the SAME tenant session (labels already resolved), and attaches `claim["readable_body"]` (a JSON-safe display dict via `to_display_dict`) + `claim["_readable_skeleton"]` (the object for phrasing); a projection failure degrades to no readable body (the raw drawer still renders). `claims_detail` invokes the flag-gated phrasing (`_resolve_any_llm_key` from the caller's accessible envs) and passes `readable_phrasing`; `templates/claims/detail.html` renders the card in the seam BETWEEN the identity header (`:102`) and the unchanged "Technical details" `<details>` drawer (`:228`) — prose prefers a grounded `plain_terms`/`step_narration[i]` (length-guarded), else the deterministic skeleton verbatim. **Validation:** 24 Stage-1 units (one byte-stable + pinned-hash regression per kind, section-omission incl. the unregistered never-fabricate guarantee, bva probes, the boundary-grounded-but-description-prose-not guard, never-raises, no-API-name-leak) + 14 Stage-2 units (fabricated number/label/step-number REJECTED → Stage-1 fallback, clean phrasing passes + caches, cache hit avoids a 2nd call, cache busts on a fact change, rejection caches nothing, flag default-OFF, the common-word false-positive guard) — **97 green** across `test_readable_body` + `test_readable_body_phrasing` + the reused `test_claim_presentation` + `tests/unit/llm`. `detail.html` compiles (tag balance intact); `primeqa.views` imports clean; the block renders correctly for a real bva risk-band skeleton on both the baseline and phrasing paths (+ empty when absent, so mocked-detail view tests are unaffected); registry+router resolve the new task to Haiku. **NOT live-previewed** — this environment has no `DATABASE_URL`, so the Flask app can't boot and the DB-backed render was not run (the isolated real-skeleton render is the rendered-output proof). Branch `readable-test-case-body`; design commit separate from impl; not pushed. See D-206 (the triage-first plain-English spine this extends), D-117 (the interpretation-phrasing enricher + validator pattern this mirrors), D-267 (the business-label spine / `label_map` this reuses), D-059 (the canonicalization / `identity_hash_version` discipline the skeleton hash mirrors), D-300/D-285 (the `strategy_kind` + bva probe recipes surfaced as boundary cases), D-303 (the band-edge-lives-in-the-recipe fact that shapes Test-data/Steps).

## D-322 — `is_production` must be an explicit human decision: loud toggle + confirm-not-production guard + activity_log (the 2026-07-07 Prod1 incident prevention). **The incident:** env 78 "Prod1" — a REAL production org — was connected with `environments.is_production` at its server default FALSE: the environment forms never exposed the flag at all AND the create path never passed it (`EnvironmentRepository.create_environment` dropped the kwarg — the flag could not be set at birth by ANY caller), so nothing forced the decision, and the (since-removed, 511fa6f) approve-time auto-verify dispatched record-creating S4 runs at production. The flag was corrected + audit-logged by hand; this is the prevention. **Decision — three mechanisms, all at the service chokepoint (`core/service.py EnvironmentService`) so the web forms AND the raw API (`POST`/`PATCH /api/environments`, which previously passed client JSON straight to the repo — the flag was PATCHable with zero checks or audit) resolve identically:** (1) **The flag is a first-class, loud form control** — environments/new + edit render a red-bordered "This is a PRODUCTION org" panel naming the concrete gates it activates (run-picker + scheduled-run exclusion, Admin-only mutating dispatch per `execution_engine/run.py`, bulk-run confirm, repair-agent never-auto-apply); a production connection pre-ticks it; and `env_type='production'` now DEFAULTS `is_production` True at the service (setdefault — an explicit False still faces the guard). (2) **Refuse-not-default:** saving `is_production=False` raises `ProductionConfirmationRequired` (a ValueError subclass; the API surfaces distinct code `CONFIRM_NOT_PRODUCTION_REQUIRED`) unless `confirm_not_production=True`, whenever any production signal fires: (a) the name matches `PROD_NAME_RX` — letter-boundary lookarounds `(?<![a-z])(production|prod|live)(?![a-z])`, deliberately NOT `\b`, because the incident name "Prod1" has a digit after "prod" so `\bprod\b` would NOT match it, while "product"/"Preprod"/"delivery" stay clean; (b) `env_type='production'`; (c) the linked connection's declared `org_type='production'` — **chosen over a live `IsSandbox` describe** because org_type is load-bearing (it selects login.salesforce.com as the OAuth host, so a wrong value doesn't authenticate) and is a zero-cost plaintext-config read at save time, where the describe needs a token refresh + an HTTP round-trip inside a form save (kept as a fallback idea only). On update the guard evaluates whenever the save touches `{is_production, name, env_type}` and would leave the flag off — a partial-PATCH rename to "Prod1" cannot slip past; a policy-only PATCH on an already-confirmed env doesn't nag. The forms mirror the signals in JS (an amber "I confirm this is NOT a production org" panel + blocked submit, `PrimeQA.unlockButton` so loading.js never wedges the button); the server guard is the enforcement (JS-off and API covered — the JS is UX only). (3) **activity_log on every flag transition** via the service: `environment.is_production_changed` (from/to + actor + signals + whether confirmed), `environment.is_production_set` (prod at birth), `environment.not_production_confirmed` (explicit confirmed-not-prod saves) — best-effort (an audit failure never breaks the save), mirroring `release/service.py`'s `_log` idiom. **Also:** `_env_dict` now exposes `is_production` (API parity), and the environments list/detail pages show a solid red PRODUCTION badge + an amber "not flagged production" mismatch chip (type=production, flag off) — the exact incident state is now visible at a glance. **Validation:** 28 new units (`tests/unit/core/test_env_production_guard.py` — regex corpus incl. "Prod1", all three signals, the create/update guard×confirm×log matrix, partial-update no-nag, the connection-marker path); full unit **3740 green**; `tests/test_environments.py` **14/14** vs Railway (its `env_type='production'` create, which omits the flag, now lands `is_production=True` via the service default — the safe direction, and why the API passes the flag presence-conditionally like `cleanup_mandatory`); live in-process proof vs the real DB (read-only — every probed write is one the guard must refuse before any insert/update): the refused API create left no row, and the incident inverse — `PATCH` env 78 `is_production=false` without confirm — **REFUSED** with the flag intact. See D-199/511fa6f (the trigger this incident rode), D-245 (the role-ladder × env-scope model the production dispatch gate lives in), migration 039 (where `is_production` was introduced).
## D-323 — multi-org closure, read surfaces: every blended analytics/browse read gains an `environment_id` scope (None = the exact pre-change query); pickers render only at >1 visible env; `/org-model` REQUIRES an org selection on multi-org tenants. **The gap (AK's full-sweep ask):** the action paths (S1 sync, S3 generate, S4 run, S6 interpret, S7 /ask) were per-org since D-255…D-292, but every read/summarize surface still blended all connected orgs — the landing `/` KPIs + recent runs, `/substrate-insights` (a claim flaky in the sandbox read as flaky for prod), the requirement-detail last-run chips (a sandbox pass rendered where a prod sign-off was being read), `/claims` (no env dimension on the library), `/org-model` (the UNION of every org's entities — ambiguous wherever orgs share api-names; 146+ shared on the live 2-org tenant). **The fix (one pattern):** `get_landing_substrate_stats` / `get_substrate_insights` / `latest_runs_by_test` / `list_claims` / `read_org_model` gain `environment_id=None`; every env predicate is a null-tautology (`CAST(:env AS int) IS NULL OR …`) so None compiles to the pre-change statement; the S6 clustering trio (`cluster_recurring_causes/by_vr/flapping`) gains the same optional kwarg via a run-join (`s6_interpretations` carries no env column — env comes from the run row; shared columns qualified since `recipe_id`/`claim_test_id`/`outcome` exist in both tables). Routes validate `?environment_id` against the caller's accessible envs (`EnvironmentRepository.list_environments` — group-scoped) and pass through; run rows/chips carry the run's env name on multi-org tenants. **Forks:** (a) landing default = **All environments** (the pre-change blended view) with an explicit Org picker — NOT auto-resolve to the user's active env (`resolve_active_environment`'s personal-env fallback chain is arbitrary for a KPI page, and the zero-regression bar wins); the plan's "switcher" turned out to not exist anywhere (release dashboard receives `list_switchable_environments` but never renders it; nothing posts to `/api/users/me/active-env`) — the runs-page GET-param picker is the real pattern and is what's reused. (b) `/org-model` multi-org = a **required selection** (prompt state), never a silent first-env default and never the union: the blend is retired as a bug, not offered as a mode. (c) Knowledge page: **no fake filter** — all three S5 channels are global/tenant-level (system rules + packs file-backed; learned rules derive from `generation_quality_signals`, no env column), so the page is labelled workspace-wide instead of growing a filter that would filter nothing. `render_search` gains an additive `hidden_params` (facet-carry through search submits). Dropped consciously: an env label on the runs grouped-by-requirement summary line — the group rows aggregate latest-per-claim across the scoped set, so a per-group env label is meaningless; the page's existing env picker already scopes the lens. **Validation:** new local-PG integration suites (`test_multiorg_console_scoping`, `test_org_model_browser_scoping`): env-scoped vs env-None identity (`_assemble_insights(env=None)` == the unscoped read), flapping-in-one-org excluded from the other org's view (a cross-org difference is NOT flapping), claims env filter + env-scoped last_run, org-scoped browser reads separate (1 vs 2 objects, per-org version_seq) with the unscoped union documented; adjacent suites + template parses green. Commits aa0bd30 + b857340 on branch `multi-org-closure` (AK-directed feature branch; deviation from the v2 commit-to-main rule authorized for this build); not pushed. See D-255…D-260 (the per-org foundation), D-286/D-292 (the action-path fixes + the residual-reader flags this closes), D-231 (the runs-page facet pattern reused).

## D-324 — per-environment release GO/NO-GO (the deferred "3e"): the decision computes once per env with evidence, rolled up worst-of; the org-blind staleness anchor becomes org-bound. **The gap:** `get_release_substrate_decision` aggregated every org's runs into one verdict — org A green + org B red ⇒ one muddled recommendation; and `_current_s1_seq` read the tenant-wide MAX `version_seq`, so grounding evaluated at org A's own latest read STALE whenever org B synced later (the D-292-flagged residual, live on the 2-org tenant: env-59 seq 89 vs env-78 seq 90). **The design (per-env verdict cards, worst-of roll-up):** `_environments_with_evidence` (one `SELECT DISTINCT environment_id` over the release's claims' runs) activates the per-env path only at **>=2 envs** — 0-1 envs run today's exact body (byte-compatible result + an `environments` echo), so single-org tenants cannot reach new code. Per env: `_assemble_claim_evidence(environment_id, connected_org_id, manual_q)` — the env predicate rides `_COUNTED_RUNS_SQL` + `_NEWER_SUPERSEDED_SQL` as null-tautologies (latest-run, the D-200 flake window, and superseded-newer are all env-scoped: cross-org disagreement is NOT flapping); `connected_org_id` (via the read-only `get_connected_org_for_environment` — unprovisioned env ⇒ `stale=None`, never raises) anchors staleness to THAT org's latest seq; `manual_q` is hoisted so the loop does one quarantine read, not one per env. `_rollup_env_decisions` (pure): recommendation = worst across envs (`no_go < conditional_go < go`, the composer's severity), confidence = that verdict's scheme constant, one `environment` reasoning line per env, `blocking` concatenated + annotated with `environment_id`, `criteria_met` = per-check AND, metrics summed except `pass_rate`=min and `claim_count`=max (shared claims, not a sum), risk = max score; the per-env dicts ride under `environments`. **Consumers proven zero-change:** `decision_composer.evaluate_and_record`, the ledger envelope, `notify_release_decision`, and the CI status route read only top-level keys the roll-up preserves (the full per-env structure rides into the persisted `reasoning` envelope for free). **Template:** the verdict card extracted into a `substrate_verdict_card` macro — multi-org renders one card per org (env-name badge from a direct `Environment` query, NOT the access-scoped repo list: a non-admin reviewer still needs each verdict labelled) under a slim worst-of strip; single-org renders the identical single card (the advisory/gating chip passes as a macro ARG — a Jinja `{% set %}` var does not reach macro scope; caught before commit). The landing dashboard's evidence read threads its env param for the same staleness reason. **Edge accepted:** env enumeration precedes the deprecated-claim filter, so an env whose ONLY evidence is a deprecated claim's runs yields a has-runs-blocked card (far edge; per-env compute guards `applicable` and skips empty-evidence envs). **Validation:** `test_substrate_decision_multiorg` — env-scoped assembly (env B's newer failure never leaks into env A's latest), env-None identity (`==` the pre-parameter rows), the worst-of roll-up end-to-end (A green / B `no_go`, blockers annotated `environment_id=B`, criteria AND, per-env reasoning lines), and the org-bound staleness proof (the SAME grounding row reads `stale=True` org-blind and `stale=False` org-bound — the falsely-stale case fixed); 83 adjacent unit+integration green. Commit ba7e1d5 on `multi-org-closure`; not pushed. See D-198 (the decision engine this extends), D-237 (the explainable blockers the annotation extends), D-292 (the flagged staleness residual), D-232/D-200 (quarantine + flake semantics, now per-env).

## D-325 — per-org S8 grounding (the deferred "3f Slices 2-3"): `s8_grounding_validity` re-keyed `(test_id, version_seq, connected_org_id)`, the recompute loops orgs-with-model, the D-265 refusal retires. **The gap:** grounding rows were org-blind and D-265's Slice-1 guardrail REFUSED multi-org tenants (clearing their rows every tick) — safe but blind: the moment a second org synced, drift/broken detection went dark tenant-wide (every consumer read "not grounded"), including the decision engine's grounding-integrity check. **The build:** tenant migration `20260707_0010` — `connected_org_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES connected_orgs(id)`; backfill attributes a single-org tenant's rows to its one org-with-model (`HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT)=1` — org-blind was vacuously org-correct there); unattributable NULLs deleted (multi-org tenants already empty via D-265; zero-org rows have nothing to bind to); PK re-keyed + org index. `persist_grounding_validity` REQUIRES `connected_org_id` (an org-less verdict is exactly the blend D-265 refused). **The inseparable read change:** `read_grounding_validity`'s org-blind path switches `one_or_none()` → worst-severity-first (`broken < drifted < intact`) `ORDER BY … .first()` — with two orgs' rows the old read RAISES `MultipleResultsFound`, which the decision wrapper would swallow into `available=False` (a silent decision outage); pessimistic worst-of is the safe gate read and is identical on a one-org store. Ships in the SAME commit as the migration — no window where multi-org rows can crash a reader. `list_grounding_validity` gains the org filter + deterministic org ordering. **The recompute (replaces the guardrail):** enumerate orgs-with-model (`DISTINCT connected_org_id` over live entities) → prune verdicts keyed to departed orgs (targeted `!= ALL(:orgs)` DELETE replaces the blanket blend-clear) → per org: org-bound `SemanticOrgModel` pinned at THAT org's latest seq (an org whose versions are gone is skipped), `recompute_grounding(connected_org_id=…)` with per-org freshness + per-org cap (each org resumes independently across ticks; `version_seq` is globally monotonic so per-org comparisons stay consistent). Zero-org tenants ground nothing — an org-less pass IS the blend (accepted behavior change from the old org-blind single pass). One artifact load serves every org (claims are tenant-level). Scheduler tick unchanged. **Readers:** the decision engine's `_claim_grounding` takes the env's org on the D-324 per-env path — each env card's grounding-integrity check reads THAT org's verdicts (the A/B bridge); the release evidence panel stays org-None (worst-of; "signal, not the decision"); insights rows + S7 grounding citations carry `connected_org_id`. **Validation:** the guardrail unit suite REPLACED by per-org loop red-proofs (two org-bound models at their OWN seqs, verdicts keyed per org, targeted prune not blanket, zero-org full clear with no model built, missing-version org skipped while the other grounds); new store tests (two-org PK no-collision, org-scoped reads separate intact-vs-broken, org-blind read = worst, list org filter); every `persist_grounding_validity` call site updated via a shared `grounding_org` fixture; full local-PG tier 393 green / 4 pre-existing baseline failures / ZERO new; the migration itself exercised by the harness's per-session `alembic upgrade head`. **Live at merge (the exit gate):** `alembic -x mode=all_tenants upgrade tenant@head` on Railway, one manual `recompute_tenant_grounding(1)` ⇒ rows tagged with BOTH tenant-1 orgs (env-59 + env-78), the scheduler log free of the D-265 refusal, and the two-env release decision tab rendering per-org grounding checks. **Deferred, flagged in-code:** the bva batch reader (`substrate_decision.py` `_claim_verified` bva arm) needs the same env filter when bva resumes (dormant, D-289); the sync-console residual is closed by D-323's org-scoped browser. Commit cc0353c on `multi-org-closure`; not pushed. See D-265 (the Slice-1 guardrail this retires), D-142/D-143 (the store + recompute this re-keys), D-324 (the per-env decision this feeds), D-286 (the resolver seam).

## D-326 — `verifies` links count as requirement coverage: COVERAGE_LINK_KINDS (`generated_from` + `verifies`) becomes the membership for every business-facing "which tests cover this requirement" read; human curation can put an existing claim on a requirement's plan without regenerating it. **The gap (req-302 full-run analysis 2026-07-07):** the L7a banded Risk-Rating claims (649/651/749/751 + 650/750 boundaries) supersede req-302's three deprecated pre-L7a state-transition claims, but they are linked to the lab key REQ-L7A-BANDS-1 — and every coverage surface filtered `link_kind='generated_from'`, so ACs 6–8 rendered as uncovered on /requirements/302 while the org-proven tests existed. The link vocabulary always distinguished provenance (`generated_from`, S3-written) from curation (`verifies`, human-written per SPEC §9) — but no read consumed `verifies`, so curation was write-only. **The build:** S2 exports `COVERAGE_LINK_KINDS = ("generated_from", "verifies")` (`related_to` deliberately excluded — associative, not a coverage assertion); `list_tests_by_requirement` accepts a sequence of kinds; the coverage-facing consumers switch membership: requirement plan + walk-sequence (`s3_generation_console._read_claims`/`_read_test_sequence`, with test_id dedupe mirroring), the requirements-list chips + coverage filter (3 raw-SQL counts), run-from-requirement dispatch (`s4_execution_console` CI re-verify + `execution_engine/intake.enqueue_claims_for_requirements`), the substrate dashboard key map, the release evidence panel (`release_substrate_console`), and the GO/NO-GO decision engine (`substrate_decision._claim_test_ids`). Provenance reads stay `generated_from`-only (`read_claim_requirement` back-link, claims-library requirement column). A test linked under both kinds dedupes to one match (result order puts `generated_from` first). **The data op:** the six approved L7a banded claims verifies-linked to req-302 via `coordinator.link_requirement(actor='human')` (idempotent PK; `linked_by` records authorship) — /requirements/302 now renders 33 active claims incl. all six Risk-Rating boundary tests; chips/sequence/counts in lockstep (probe-verified). **Validation:** s3-console 34 + discovery/draft-vertical 17 integration tests + run-page 4/4, all green. See D-269 (deprecated exclusion this composes with), D-247 (per-AC coverage), D-317 (the requirement workspace this feeds).

## D-327 — the requirement excerpt leaves the identity-bearing trigger description: S3 narrates triggers from STRUCTURE only, so same-meaning intents with different excerpt slices hash together and persistence dedup (SPEC §7.7) collapses them. **The defect (req-302 duplicate analysis 2026-07-07):** one generation wave (outcome e924c2d7) minted TWO approved claims asserting the identical automation effect (HL_High_Risk_Task → Task.Subject='Review High Risk Loan', same staged trigger Credit_Score=600/KYC=True/Stage='Credit Assessment') — f91fd866 vs 45180120 differ ONLY in the verbatim requirement-excerpt tail S3 appended after the em-dash in `triggering_action.description` ("Whenever the Risk Rating is automatically set to High, create a Task with: …" vs "create a Task with: Subject: …"). The excerpt (Guardrail-3's per-intent anchor) is provenance — it rides the intent + `llm_calls` — but the emission idiom baked it into the identity-bearing description, so `compute_identity_hash` split on prose and `_write_emission`'s same-hash lookup (which correctly dedupes within-batch AND cross-wave via the same session) never fired. **The fix (emission-side, NO canonicalization-policy change):** every `_author_*` description in `generation/emission.py` now narrates the trigger from structure alone — the staged clause stays identity-bearing (D-299/D-307: "creating a X with F=v[ then updating …]", create- vs update-scoped claims still hash apart, and the L7a banded claims still hash apart on their staged Credit_Score values), the " — <excerpt>" tail is dropped, and the excerpt-only fallbacks become stable structural narrations ("creating a {object}", "a data change setting F=v", "creating a {trigger_object} linked to the subject"). IDENTITY_HASH_VERSION stays 1 — the hash FUNCTION is unchanged; only newly-authored bodies differ, so no re-hash pass; the known cost is one supersession round per pre-D-327 claim on its next regeneration (the established regen-supersede pattern). Naive alternatives rejected: dropping `description` from the hash would collapse the six L7a boundary tests (their staged 649/651/749/751 values live in that clause); em-dash string surgery in the canonicalizer is a v2 policy bump for a prose format. **Unit red-proofs:** `test_excerpt_is_not_identity_bearing_same_intent_hashes_together` (same intent, different excerpt ⇒ equal hashes) + the D-299 empty-trigger pin updated to the new bare-create narration; generation unit 387 + integration 207 green. **The data op (human curation, D-ε-1/D-ε-5):** four req-302 duplicates deprecated with forward-explanatory reasons — f91fd866 (excerpt-only dup of 45180120) and the three loose AC4 variants c4ee936b/280e6472/f860f7ee (near-dups dropping the Stage='Credit Assessment' entry condition that gives the KYC/credit-score gate its meaning; superseded by stage-scoped c814cf7c + 6243a4cb). /requirements/302 renders 29 active claims (8 existence / 6 prohibition / 14 automation-effect incl. the D-326 banded six / 1 acceptance). Remaining near-dup class (cross-wave intents with GENUINELY different condition sets) is S3 subsumption reasoning — out of scope, tracked as a lever. See D-059 (canonicalization), D-299/D-307 (staged-clause identity), D-311 (per-intent posture), D-326 (the coverage-link decision this composes with).

## D-328 — bva boundary routing un-gated for tenant 1 + compound-AND boundary derivation: `derive_boundary_set` accepts a top-level AND with EXACTLY ONE integer-threshold conjunct, staging every other conjunct TRUE as a gate in BOTH probes. **Context (AK's item-4 pick, req-302 follow-ups):** D-300 proved the boundary engine live (the amount-cap VR) then disarmed the flag as proof discipline; the named remaining boundary target — the ₹50,00,000 approval threshold — lives in `Opportunity.Block_Approved_Without_Approval`, a COMPOUND VR (`AND(ISPICKVAL(StageName,"Approved"), Loan_Amount__c > 5000000, NOT(ISPICKVAL(Approval_Status__c,"Approved")))`) that the D-300 bare-Comparison-only shape refused, so arming alone delivered nothing new for req-302. (The 650/749/750 credit-score boundaries are Flow-band logic, delivered claim-side by L7a and made visible by D-326 — VR-bva does not apply there.) **The build:** `derive_boundary_set` gains the compound arm — operands partition into ONE `_is_threshold` conjunct (single-field vs INTEGER literal, `>`/`>=`/`<`/`<=`; the D-300 fractional refusal carries over) + gates; both probes merge `_satisfy(gate, True)` payloads with the threshold's firing / just-inside value through the SHIPPED `_merge`/`_unwrap_soft` machinery (D-296 soft/hard semantics: a NOT-ISBLANK gate on the threshold field yields to the boundary value), so no new value arithmetic exists. Gates make the just-inside accept MEANINGFUL: with gates true the only reason the create succeeds is the value being inside. Refusals: zero/multiple threshold conjuncts, Or/Not compounds, an underivable gate (e.g. NOT-ISPICKVAL without the D-294 picklist rail), a gate/threshold merge conflict, fractional literals — all `()`, never a guessed set. The D-300 drift invariant holds on compounds (firing payload == `derive(ast).violating_payload`, same constraint set through the same merge; unit-pinned). The deliberate D-300 "compounds refuse" test pin is REPLACED by the compound contract (5 new red-proofs incl. the exact Block_Approved shape probing 5000001/5000000). Emission's flag-gated author (`_author_negative`) is UNCHANGED — bigger payloads ride through `author_boundary_recipes` as-is. **The arm (data op):** `tenant_agent_settings.llm_enable_bva_boundaries = true` for tenant 1 (the D-300 arm idiom; the column stays deliberately un-ORM-mapped per the deploy-safety note); `_bva_boundaries_enabled(1)` reads True. Future generations of eligible prohibitions stamp `strategy_kind='bva'` + boundary probes; the req-302 regeneration (after the item-3/item-2 generation-side builds) is the live exit gate. **Validation:** generation unit + integration 599 green. See D-300 (the engine + flag), D-294 (the metadata rail gates ride), D-296 (soft/hard merge), D-326/D-327 (the sibling req-302 follow-ups).

## D-329 — the implied valid case (prompt generation@v20): a conditioned rule states its own complement, so the proposal includes the in-scope happy path + one out-of-scope control per distinct scope condition. **The gap (req-302 intent forensics, probe over `llm_calls.raw_parameters` call 636df7b8):** the model's 24-intent proposal covered all 21 declared ACs yet contained ZERO happy-path-create intents and ZERO negative controls — and that was CORRECT behavior under the shipped guidance: the D-305 acceptance triggers key on explicit assertion phrases ("saves successfully", "is accepted", out-of-scope validations "do not fire") which req-302's text never states, and Guardrail-3 forbids inventing intents the text does not state. Every downstream layer already supports the shapes — D-305 acceptance grounding (equals staged, `is_null` deliberately-absent, the B3 required-field-null refusal), `_author_acceptance`'s create/update recipes, and the R1 VR-satisfaction padding which only satisfies VRs ARMED by the staged state (so a `Loan_Type='Personal'` control genuinely leaves the Home-Loan fields absent — the accept is not vacuous). The loss was at PROPOSAL time: nobody told the model a scoped rule ("For Opportunities where Loan Type = Home Loan: … mandatory") implies its complement acceptances. **The fix (prompt-only):** base.md "Decompose for full coverage" gains the **implied valid case** bullet — (a) ONE positive acceptance staging the scope condition + every constrained field satisfied together (values consistent with EVERY stated rule at once, e.g. a Loan Amount that also respects "must not exceed Property Value"), (b) ONE out-of-scope control per distinct scope condition (scope FALSE, constrained fields deliberately absent via `is_null`), both anchored on the rule's own verbatim scope text (Guardrail-3 satisfied — this is reading the complement the text states, not inventing); bounded explicitly (one happy path per scoped rule-set, one control per scope condition — never one per rule, no combinatorial blowup). The data_behavior fragment's acceptance section gains the matching trigger ("or when a scoped rule IMPLIES its complement") + the consistent-values note. **Freeze ritual (D-103.1/D-318):** composed → `versions/generation_v20.md` (sha 540b016f…), registry `_FILES`/`RECORDED_HASHES`/`CURRENT=generation@v20`; the compose-equals-CURRENT drift guard + v20 substance assertions updated (`test_current_resolves_to_v20`). v1..v19 stay frozen + pinned-resolvable. **Validation:** generation unit + integration 599 green. **Exit gate:** the req-302 regeneration (shared with D-328) must propose + ground the Home-Loan happy path and a Personal/Business-loan control. See D-305/D-306 (the acceptance machinery this feeds), D-247 (per-AC coverage), D-207 (multi-intent decomposition this extends).

## D-330 — the cross-field rejection clause: conditions body v2 (`exceeds` + `compared_to` ref) + the predicate-aware VR hard filter — req-302 AC2 ("Loan Amount must not exceed Property Value") derives a real reject-test. **The defect chain (the D-295 "metric-blindness" casualty, now root-caused end to end):** (1) the S2 condition taxonomy had no field-vs-field form, so the model could only flatten AC2 to its scope clause (`Loan_Type=Home Loan` — the degenerate 33d6660a); (2) field-overlap alignment then scored the WIDER mandatory-fields VR above the cross-field VR (3-to-2 with the scope clause present) or refused — the cross-field predicate was invisible to the selector; (3) yet the DERIVATION for the cross-field VR has been shipped since D-294/D-296 (`_satisfy_cross_field` ordered pairs + the soft/hard merge over `AND(NOT-ISBLANK, …, a>b)`) — the loss was entirely upstream of it. **The build:** *S2* — `SemanticConditionsBodyV2` (`register_body("conditions", 2)`, the D-306.1 new-version-not-new-field precedent: canonicalization includes every field, so a v1 slot would re-key every existing claim) with `ConditionV2`: predicate `exceeds` + `compared_to: IdentityBearingRef` (walkable — coverage extraction picks up BOTH condition fields, integration-proven), model-validated coupling (exceeds ⇒ compared_to required + value forbidden; v1 predicates forbid compared_to); IDENTITY_HASH_VERSION stays 1 (a new body schema is not a canonicalization-policy change — the acceptance-v2 precedent). *S3 grounding* — `_ground_rejection_conditions` accepts the cross-field clause `{field, predicate:"exceeds", compared_to}` (both fields must BELONG_TO the subject; value forbidden). *Alignment* — `_claim_condition_fields` counts both fields; NEW `_claim_cross_field_pairs` mirrors D-296's `_vr_cross_field_pairs` on the claim side; `_best_aligned_vr` applies a HARD FILTER before scoring: a claim carrying a cross-field clause only ever aligns to a VR whose formula contains that exact pair (zero matches ⇒ refuse — never a same-fields-different-predicate fallback). *Emission* — `_conditions_body` authors v2 only when a cross-field clause is present (all-v1 clause sets stay byte-identical; getattr-tolerant per the D-288 idiom); the authored AC2 bundle is Layer-2 verified with the D-296 update-reject pair (setup create Loan blank → violating update Loan=1/Property=0, the org's own VR fires; D-297 message binding unchanged). *Presentation* — `condition_phrase` renders "Loan Amount exceeds Property Value" into the D-293 "when …" title clause. *Prompt* — generation@v21: the cross-field clause form ("Never flatten a cross-field rule to just its scope condition; the comparison IS the state") + the derivability list CORRECTED (the stale wording still told the model ISBLANK/picklist/cross-field shapes refuse — they derive since D-294/D-296 — actively discouraging exactly these proposals); frozen per the D-103.1 ritual. **Validation:** 5 alignment red-proofs on the REAL env-59 VR set (incl. the exact 3-to-2 mis-attribution now beaten), 4 grounding, 2 emission (v2 body + ordered violating update; v1 byte-identity), title, the full write_claim v2 round-trip (JSONB + registry decode + coverage rows), registry-size pin updated; full sweep 4410+ green. **Exit gate:** the req-302 regeneration (shared with D-328/D-329) must produce the AC2 prohibition aligned to `Opportunity.Loan_Exceeds_Property_Value` with the "when Loan Amount exceeds Property Value" title. Named residual: `exceeds` is the only cross-field predicate (the live case); the v2 envelope is the door for the rest of the ordering family when a requirement needs them. See D-293/D-294/D-295/D-296 (the ladder this completes), D-306.1 (the v2-body precedent).

## D-331 — per-AC coverage on the requirement page: every acceptance criterion shows its proposed-test count or the honest recorded reason it is not tested. **The complaint (AK, users):** generated test plans read as "not comprehensive" because a criterion with no test is a SILENT gap — the engine's honest machinery (D-247 ac_ref tagging, no_admissible_test declarations, D-302 partial refusals) records exactly why, but nothing surfaced it per-criterion. **The build (read-time assembly, NO schema change):** `read_requirement_ac_coverage` (s3_generation_console) joins, for the requirement's LATEST generation outcome, the propose call's persisted `raw_parameters` (the declared `acceptance_criteria` + each intent's `ac_ref`/`no_admissible_test`/reason — already stored verbatim on `llm_calls`) with the outcome's `attempted_interpretation.partial_refusals` (ac_ref-keyed, D-302/D-311) into per-AC rows: `proposed` (N intents, none refused) / `partial` (some refused, reason shown) / `refused` (all refused) / `untestable` (declared, with the model's reason) / `unaddressed`. Deliberately INTENT-level truth: the intent→claim linkage is not persisted, so no claim mapping is invented (the plan below the panel lists the claims themselves). Pure assembly split out (`_assemble_ac_coverage`) + unit-tested; the read is best-effort/never-raises like every console read. **The surface:** a collapsible "Coverage by acceptance criterion" panel on /requirements/<id> between the generation notes and the test plan — AC chip + label + status badge + the recorded reason under the label; live-verified rendering all 10 req-302 ACs via the test client. See D-247 (the coverage contract this surfaces), D-302/D-311 (the refusal records), D-317 (the requirement workspace).

## D-332 — two live-run-revealed fixes from the req-302 exit-gate batch (the D-308.1 "live-run-reveals is the honest floor" loop working): staged picklist labels bind to the org's actual values, and R1 padding skips OR arms the staged state already falsifies. **The batch:** the 6 D-326…D-331 ships were exit-gated by a req-302 regeneration (40 claims written / 29 dedup-equivalent under generation@v21) + curation (7 approved incl. the D-330 `exceeds` prohibition and both D-329 acceptances; 4 weak drafts deprecated; the 2 pre-D-327 excerpt-hash equivalents superseded) + a full env-59 live run (34 jobs). **Green:** the D-330 flagship — "Rejects editing records on Opportunity when Loan Amount exceeds Property Value" — PASSED live (the org's `Loan_Exceeds_Property_Value` VR fired on the D-296 update-reject pair): req-302's AC2 is covered AND proven for the first time. LTV 80/90, the banded Risk-Rating six, and the whole pre-existing plan: 27/27 passed. Known-red carried honestly: the approval-submission re-mint fails on the org's dead `HL_Auto_Submit_Approval` entry criteria (open AK org action, unchanged). **Fix 1 (S3 — `_bind_picklist_values`):** both D-329 acceptances failed `INVALID_OR_NULL_FOR_RESTRICTED_PICKLIST` — the model staged the REQUIREMENT's labels ("Home Loan"/"Personal Loan") where the org's restricted picklist holds "Home"/"Personal". Staged `equals` values on picklist fields now bind to the org's actual values at grounding (the D-294 rail): exact → keep, unique case-insensitive → org casing, unique word-prefix either direction → the org value; zero/≥2 candidates → refuse naming the valid values. Applied ONLY on the STAGED-value paths (acceptance + update clauses) — prohibition conditions are identity/display, never staged, and rebinding them would re-key every existing prohibition for no run-time gain. **Fix 2 (S4 — R1.1 `_already_false`):** the Task.Subject re-mint ERRORED (AmbiguousRejection) because its staged trigger (Credit_Score=600, Stage='Credit Assessment', no KYC) armed the prerequisites VR and R1's OR-falsifier BAILED at the k16 leaf on `ISBLANK(Credit_Score__c)` — an arm the staged 600 ALREADY falsifies — so `KYC_Complete=True` was never padded and the org rejected the create. `_falsify`'s OR branch now skips arms provably false under the staged values (`_already_false`, the falsifier's counterpart of `_pin_true`, conservative to the same shapes) and demands only from live arms; an all-arms-false OR returns `{}` (safe, no demands) — distinct from `None` (unfalsifiable). The pre-D-332 pass of this claim's ancestor was luck: the old model proposal staged KYC explicitly. **Red-proofs:** 2 world-padding (the exact staged-600 shape + the all-arms-false case) + 4 binding units; full sweep generation+execution 995 green. **Exit:** regenerate the two acceptances (grounding now binds the values), re-run them + the Task.Subject claim on env-59.
