## D-387 — S3 messages-array cache breakpoint: one MOVING breakpoint on the last completed turn (2026-07-25, main @3cfd9e6, deployed). The S3 spine re-sends the whole conversation every turn with only tools+system marked, so every earlier turn re-billed at full input rate — a propose turn's output was paid three times over a re-prompt run (once as output, twice as re-sent input). `_messages_with_cache` (gateway.py) marks the last content block of the most recent completed turn, so each call caches the longest prefix available to it; 3 of Anthropic's 4 breakpoints used (tools, system, messages), asserted ≤4 on every turn shape. **Request content byte-identical modulo cache_control** (asserted programmatically over the real 3-turn conversation shape, PASS at every turn; non-mutating). Turn 1 is DELIBERATELY unmarked: its content is a plain string, and wrapping it in a text block to hold the marker would change the serialized body; the next turn's breakpoint covers it. **Measured:** −18.0% on the messages line (cold run, rows 922-924 vs warm BEFORE 908-910); warm-vs-warm live confirmation post-deploy (rows 928-930 vs 908-910, both 3-call req-301): input-side −$0.009836 = **−10.1%** of the $0.097545 baseline run (raw total −3.6% only because the AFTER run emitted +423 stochastic output tokens; sums reconcile exactly). Fresh input on turns 2-3 fell 13,458 → 43 tokens. **KNOWN REGRESSION, accepted deliberately:** a 2-call run's terminal emit turn writes a cache nothing ever reads — +$0.004650/run at 1.25× write; 58/165 observed outcomes are 2-call, ~$0.27 total exposure, ~20% of the −$1.38 net aggregate benefit. Characterization (live corpus): **50 of the 58 two-call outcomes are FULL successful runs** (propose+emit → draft — the minimal path is 2 calls; a 3-call run is that plus the D-247/D-340 re-prompt hop), so the penalty lands on successful minimal runs, not on correct-refusal behaviour (1-call refusals are unmarked and unaffected). Rejected alternatives: (1) caller-declared continuation flag — terminality is not knowable at request time, since it depends on whether the model emits or calls another tool, so the orchestrator would be guessing too; (2) lagging breakpoint marking the previous turn's end — removes the penalty at the cost of a shorter read span, not modelled, exposure too small to justify. Do not re-litigate below a materially larger exposure. See D-095.2 (tool_turn owns transport), the S3_TOKEN_COST_REVIEW C-2 finding.

## D-388 — llm_usage_log generation attribution: thread what exists, ride `context` for what has no column, name the dead columns (2026-07-25, main @72eed6c, deployed). Generation rows carried cost and cache counters with NO path back to the run that spent them (llm_usage_log had the cost, tenant_1.llm_calls the outcome FK, nothing joined them); gateway_binding dropped parameters the gateway already accepted. Now threaded: `user_id` (the job's owner — the only user identity on the unattended worker path) into the existing column; the S3 `request_id`, `environment_id` and `requirement_key` into the existing `context` JSONB (empty on every prior generation row). The join `llm_usage_log.context->>'s3_request_id' → generation_outcomes.request_id` is live-proven on the deployed Railway path (rows 925-927: user_id=1 = job.created_by, full context, $0.144124 attributed to one run/requirement/environment/outcome). **Dead columns, named:** `run_id`, `test_case_id`, `generation_batch_id` target v1 product tables dropped in migration 053 — they can never be populated again. `environment_id` is NOT a column; riding `context` is an interim shape. **requirement_id — the corrected fact (same-day diagnosis):** the substrate's text key is a two-branch encoding minted at s3_enqueue.py:23 (`jira_key or f"req-{id}"`), fully decodable while the public row exists — 10 of 15 live keys decode (5 via req-prefix incl. every actively-generated one, 5 via jira_key); 5 dangle against DELETED requirements rows (the public table is mutable/deletable while the substrate ledger is append-only). The commit-1 rationale ("does not reliably resolve") tested only the jira_key branch; recording `requirement_key` in context remains the honest shape — the text key is the substrate's identifier and survives row deletion. **The 391 pre-instrumentation generation rows are permanently unattributable** — no persisted key exists in either direction (usage side: provider request_id only; llm_calls side: client-minted call_id never sent to the gateway, timing_start NULL, raw_response only on rejections). Follow-up lean: one MIGRATE-FIRST migration before pilot — drop the three dead columns, promote environment_id to a typed column (and optionally a decoded requirement_id where a row exists). See D-286 (env→org scoping that stopped at run_generation), D-106.4 (the consumer path), migration 053.

## D-389 — Discard accounting is THREE categories, never one number (2026-07-25). The S3 review's "64% of candidate paths produce no claim" invites a false reading as waste. The taxonomy, fixed: (1) **Grounding refusal** (partial_refusals, no_admissible_test, ungrounded-after-reprompt) is correct behaviour — its token cost is the price of the ground-or-refuse contract, i.e. the price of fidelity, not waste; any optimisation aimed at it trades fidelity for tokens and is HIGH-risk by definition. (2) **Layer-A schema rejection** (67/449 calls = 15%, 230/2,866 intents re-proposed) is defect — the model failed the structural contract and a full corrective turn re-ran; this is the ONLY fidelity-neutral optimisation target in the discard surface. (3) **Identity dedup / supersession** (D-339 collapse, persister same-hash no-op, deprecate-then-regen) is a generation-SCOPING question (what should be generated at all), not token-accounted, and belongs to the regeneration-lineage discussion (D-071 prior_request_id, unpopulated). Standing rule: never report a combined discard rate as a waste figure — report the three categories separately or not at all. See D-339/D-353 (dedup + migration law), D-247/D-340 (the coverage re-prompt that generates category-1 volume), S3_TOKEN_COST_REVIEW C-5.

## D-390 — S3 console cost attribution: timestamp window → request key; timestamp correlation REJECTED as an attribution mechanism codebase-wide (2026-07-25, main @4e31f94). The Generation-history and run-detail cost reads summed `llm_usage_log` rows whose `ts` fell inside the attempt's `[started_at, finished_at]` window. Measured against the live log: **267 of 417 generation rows ($27.46 of $43.90 = 63%) fell outside every attempt window** and were silently dropped from the per-requirement surface while still counted in settings totals — the two cost surfaces disagreed by construction; and the window's single-worker assumption (one generation per tenant sequentially) was **already violated** by local direct-`run_generation` runs and eval runs, so a concurrent run's rows were mis-attributed into whichever attempt window contained them. 72eed6c/D-388 made key attribution possible; both joins now key on `context->>'s3_request_id' = attempt.request_id`, and the window predicate is DELETED — not kept as a fallback for untagged rows. **Standing law: timestamp correlation is not an acceptable attribution mechanism anywhere in this codebase** — not for backfills, not for "just this surface"; a row either carries its key or is honestly unattributable. Pre-instrumentation attempts (no keyed rows) render **"not attributed"** with a tooltip naming why — never "$0.00" (the `llm=None` absence precedent). Known residual, reported not patched: 2 tagged requests (8 rows, $0.34 — this arc's local direct-`run_generation` verification runs) carry the key but no attempt row exists, so they are invisible to the attempt-oriented history while visible in settings totals — the direct-invocation path creates no attempt; a follow-up decides whether that path should. Source-level test pins the key join and forbids the window predicate. See D-388 (the key), the S3_TOKEN_COST_REVIEW §A.3 (the correlation this retires).

## D-391 — Analytics-layer v1 residue: dead task predicates fixed; fabricated zeros replaced with ABSENCE (2026-07-25, main @6e5d6ab). Same species as D-388's dead columns, one layer up. **The sweep found:** (1) `dashboard.efficiency_summary` filtered `task = 'test_plan_generation'` (cache/cost/generations) and `task IN ('test_plan_generation','agent_fix')` (escalation) — v1 task names under which **zero rows have EVER existed** (verified live; the live path logs `task='generation'`, and the repair path logs `repair_proposal`), so the superadmin panel reported "0 generations / $0.000000 / 0/0 cache hit rate" through divide-guard fallbacks; (2) `quality_proxy_summary` returned a hard-coded ZERO SHAPE post-D-238 — rendered as a green "0.0% regeneration rate" indistinguishable from a measured zero; (3) `feedback_rules.correction_rate` — the same fabricated-zero species feeding /settings/my-llm-usage's green "0.0% correction rate" hero; (4) REPORTED, not fixed (outside the analytics layer): `gateway.py:153`'s `task == "test_plan_generation"` feedback-injection gate is dead code (no llm_call task carries that name — the D-247 "Common mistakes" block is never auto-injected for live generation), `router.py` `_CHAINS` entries for `test_plan_generation`/`agent_fix`/`story_view_generation` are unreachable routing config, and the `llm/__init__.py` docstring example names the dead task. **Decisions:** predicates read the LIVE name only (no dual-match — matching a name with zero historical rows preserves nothing); "generations" counts DISTINCT attributable runs (`context->>'s3_request_id'`; one run = 2-5 calls — the old per-call count was a v1 shape where one call WAS one generation), with untagged pre-instrumentation calls surfaced as their own number; **cache hit rate is PER TENANT** (Anthropic scopes prompt caches per API key and each tenant resolves its own — a cross-tenant average is meaningless); every empty-denominator metric returns ``None``/``measured: False`` and the templates render "not measured" — the s3_generation_console `llm=None` precedent, now the analytics-layer law: **absence is reported as absence, never as a zero-valued shape**. Also fixed: the daily-spend chart drew every bar 0px tall (percentage heights against auto-height wrappers inside an `items-end` flex row) — wrappers now stretch and bottom-align via `justify-end`; rendered result awaits visual confirmation. Escalation stats cover all ok calls (its true reading today: 0 of 579 escalated — a measured zero, kept). See D-238 (the drop-readiness that left the zero shapes), D-388/D-390.

## D-392 — AMENDMENT to D-387: the unread cache write is a TERMINAL-TURN property, not a 2-call property (2026-07-25). D-387 framed the accepted regression as "2-call runs pay for a cache never read". Restated correctly from the live rows: **the LAST turn of EVERY run writes a messages-span cache nothing ever reads** — on the 3-call Railway runs, turn 3 wrote 1,281 unread tokens (rows 925-927) / 1,291 (rows 928-930) after reading turn 2's span; a 2-call run is simply the case where no offsetting read exists at all, so the write is a pure penalty instead of a net win. Exposure and the accept/reject decision are unchanged (the terminal write rides every run and is already inside the measured −10.1% net); the mechanism is restated so a future "skip the breakpoint on the terminal turn" idea is evaluated against the right shape: terminality is not knowable at request time (D-387's rejected alternative 1), so the terminal write is the price of the moving breakpoint, on every run, not a 2-call quirk. See D-387.

## D-393 — The requirement key is a DERIVED EXPRESSION over mutable state, not persisted identity (2026-07-25, read-only diagnosis — no fix this arc). s3_enqueue.py:23 recomputes `jira_key or f"req-{id}"` on EVERY enqueue, so the substrate's text key changes the moment `jira_key` is later set on the row — and `jira_key` IS settable on an existing row via a plain PATCH: the update route passes raw JSON through and the repository field list (test_management/repository.py:247-252) excludes exactly 7 fields, `jira_key` not among them (sync never changes it; import refuses duplicates; nothing guards update). **Claim identity is UNAFFECTED, by design:** `compute_identity_hash` (test_representation/identity_hash.py:77-94) takes only (archetype, claim_kind, asserted_truth, semantic_conditions) — no requirement key — so the persister's same-hash lookup re-versions the existing tests correctly under any key. **Requirement-level linkage DOES fragment:** jobs (unique on requirement_key + s1 seq), outcomes (`requirement_ref->>'key'`), generation history, and the `generated_from` links (persistence.py D-166, `external_key` = the text key) all key on the text key; and the coverage filter (test_management/repository.py:220-224) switches a row from the `req-<id>` branch to the `jira_key` branch the moment the key is set — the old links stop matching, so **a requirement with live claims reads as UNCOVERED**. **REMEDIATION (the accepted shape):** persist `requirement_key` ONCE at creation and read it thereafter — the key becomes immutable data rather than a derived expression. Blocking `jira_key` mutation is containment, not remediation, and is explicitly NOT the accepted fix. The migration composes with D-388's follow-up (drop the 3 dead llm_usage_log columns + promote environment_id) — one MIGRATE-FIRST migration. **The fix arc OPENS with a repro** (set jira_key on a covered requirement, re-generate, assert coverage reads uncovered): the fragmentation mechanism is code-read, not yet runtime-confirmed. See D-388 (the composing migration), D-394 (the deletion half of the same referent problem).

## D-394 — Purge deletes a referent with NO referential guard (2026-07-25, read-only diagnosis — no fix this arc). `POST /api/requirements/<id>/purge` (test_management/routes.py:279-286, admin-gated) hard-deletes requirement rows with no check against substrate references. Live damage, counted: 5 substrate keys (PA-4, req-280, req-282, SQ-206, SQ-211) reference purged rows — **15 s3_generation_jobs, 15 generation_outcomes, 5 test_requirement_links** point at requirements that no longer exist. The rows are hard-GONE, not soft-deleted: `deleted_at` exists and is NULL on all 10 survivors, so the soft-delete path was not what removed them. **Same defect shape as D-291 one layer up** — a mutable/deletable referent (there: entity-version surrogates; here: requirement rows), an append-only referrer that never learns of the change, no close-on-change or referential guard between them — but WORSE: the substrate's text keys are logical references with no FK, so nothing can reconstruct what was purged; the D-291 backfill had a twin to guard on, this has nothing. **REMEDIATION:** purge REFUSES when substrate references exist (jobs / outcomes / links by the row's derivable keys — both branches of the D-393 encoding). Soft-delete is the default and its infrastructure already exists (`deleted_at`/`deleted_by`, restore route). See D-291 (the species), D-393 (the key encoding a guard must check both branches of).

## D-395 — Dormant machinery reported as HEALTHY. Root cause: the task name is an UNTYPED dispatch key (2026-07-25). A task name is a free string used as a dispatch key with no typed registry and no exhaustiveness check — so renaming a task (v1 `test_plan_generation` → live `generation`) silently orphaned every site keyed on the old name, and nothing could tell. **Three mechanisms have NEVER run in production:** (1) the D-247 feedback injection (gateway.py:153, `task == "test_plan_generation"`) — the "Common mistakes to avoid" block has never been auto-injected into a live generation; (2) escalation — zero `escalated=true` rows have ever existed, under ANY task (tool_turn has no chain; no live llm_call task both supports escalation and runs); (3) the router `_CHAINS` entries for the three v1 tasks — unreachable routing config. **Two of these reported healthy rather than dormant:** `quality_proxy_summary` returned a hard-coded zero shape and `feedback_rules.correction_rate` rendered a green "0.0% correction rate" hero — asserting a working feedback loop that had never run. Fixed in 6e5d6ab for the ANALYTICS LAYER ONLY (absence over fabricated zeros). **REMEDIATION for the class:** a typed task registry, so a rename cannot silently orphan a dispatch site — fixing individual strings guarantees a fourth instance. **EXPLICIT HOLD:** flipping gateway.py:153 to the live task name is NOT a typo fix. It changes what the model sees on every generation (a prompt-content change) and requires before/after output comparison plus a grounding-validator check; dormant-first discipline requires the switch be flipped deliberately, with evidence, never by string edit. **COROLLARY RULE (standing):** every dispatch-keyed mechanism must expose a last-fired signal, and never-fired must render as never-fired — not as zero, and never as healthy. See D-391 (the analytics half), D-247 (the mechanism that never fired), D-372/C9 (ops-legibility precedent).

## D-396 — "Generation" has TWO denominators across the cost panels (2026-07-25, recorded; resolution direction fixed). Settings (/settings/llm-usage) counts distinct `s3_request_id` — 4 attributed runs, $0.5787; Generation history counts ATTEMPTS — 2 for req-301, $0.2382. Both are correct over their own denominator; the $0.3405 gap is exactly D-390's residual — direct `run_generation` invocations mint no attempt, so their keyed spend is visible to settings and invisible to the attempt-oriented history. Prior state was $27.46 dropped silently outside all timestamp windows, so the drift is now BOUNDED and EXPLAINABLE rather than invisible — but two panels using one word for different denominators is a legibility defect in procurement contexts (the pilot-gate audience reads both). **Resolution direction (one-resolver-not-two):** attempt creation belongs INSIDE `run_generation`, so every generation is recorded regardless of caller and the two denominators converge on one; panel wording reconciles then, not before. See D-390 (the residual this bounds), D-106.4 (the attempt layer).

## D-397 — Stale-cohort re-run: the S1 detail-completeness defect was HISTORICAL, and D-338's exit gate is CLOSED (2026-07-27, env-59, deployed consumer @c922771). The 25 approved claims parked on stale ≤07-08 verdicts were re-enqueued one at a time through the production S4 job path (deployed Railway worker claiming each; no direct executor call, no racing). **21/21 UnfillableWorld claims cleared it** — 20 `passed`, 1 (`31eaa21e`) advanced past world-construction to a real verdict — and **zero new UnfillableWorld occurred**. Transitions: **errored→passed 19 · errored→failed 1 · errored→errored 1 · failed→passed 1 · failed→failed 3**. Root cause confirmed historical: the 07-08 sync minted a TRANSITIONAL `Opportunity.StageName` entity version (seq 120..121) whose `field_details.picklist_value_set_entity_id` was **NULL**, so `_picklist_value` returned `_UNFILLABLE` (world.py:429-431) and 20 distinct approved claims — several of which had passed 3–9 times the previous day — errored at world-construction before any org write; a second version the same day (seq 121..open, `SVS:OpportunityStage`, 10 active values) healed it. Pre-flight re-verified the heal through the executor's own read path (10 active values; `resolve_operational_padding` → `unfillable=()`; VR-gating steers `StageName` to `Needs Analysis`, away from the VR-named `Credit Assessment`). **D-338 EXIT GATE CLOSED: `a8e05aa2` and `cfa04585` both PASSED** (runs `fcd3183a` / `02a47912`). `ff0cefc5` also recovered failed→passed (the automation-effect record is produced; its 07-02 red was an artifact of the same era). Ledger: +25 run rows, all 595 pre-existing rows intact, insert-only. Duration ≈ 593 s for 25 claims. S4 makes no LLM calls — 0 `llm_usage_log` rows written, so this cost no tokens. The residual 3 reds + 1 errored are analysed in D-399/D-400. See D-341 (the deploy-interrupt/zombie-sync class this resembles), D-291 (dangling-reference species on the details axis).

## D-398 — k16 HELD under adversarial test: S4 declined to touch a semantic field even where touching it would have produced a green (2026-07-27). `f2b072ac` was carried into this arc as a *suspected padding-side wrong-red* — the hypothesis being that operational padding chose a VR-violating `KYC_Complete__c: false` and thereby manufactured the red. **It did not.** The claim's own `semantic_conditions` are, verbatim: `Opportunity.StageName equals 'Prospecting'` and `Opportunity.KYC_Complete__c equals False`. `KYC_Complete__c` is therefore SEMANTIC, and the k16 set-difference (world.py:184, `if not api or api in semantic_fields: continue`) excluded it from the writable padding set entirely — padding contributed only `Name` and `CloseDate`; `StageName` is the claim's own from-state. S4 built **exactly** the world the claim specified: create at Prospecting with KYC incomplete → update `StageName → Credit Assessment` → HTTP 400 `FIELD_CUSTOM_VALIDATION_EXCEPTION` ("KYC must be complete and Credit Score must be populated before moving to Credit Assessment"). **The claim is false; the org is right.** R1 is not implicated — its picklist gating is separately proven by the 19/19 UnfillableWorld recoveries. The load-bearing property: a substrate optimizing for green would have "helpfully" padded `KYC_Complete__c: true` and produced a passing test of a claim the org contradicts — a wrong-GREEN, the most expensive defect class in a release-decision product. The structural guardrail (a set difference, not a discipline) made that unreachable, and the failure surfaced as an honest red instead. Recorded as the first live adversarial confirmation of the D-115 §1 boundary. See D-115 (k16 locked), D-338 (the is_null half of the same set).

## D-399 — S3 authorship defects are reaching APPROVED claims, and VALUE-MEMBERSHIP is unvalidated (2026-07-27). Two verified-bad claims survived approval and executed against a live org: (1) **`f2b072ac`** — a self-contradictory acceptance precondition (the **D-329 implied-valid-case class**): it asserts a from-state (`KYC_Complete__c = false`) that the VR guarding its own target transition forbids, so the claim can only ever be red (D-398). (2) **`31eaa21e`** — an **invented enumerated value**: the recipe stages `Opportunity.Loan_Type__c = "Home Loan"`, and the org's restricted picklist holds exactly `Home`, `Personal`, `Business` — no `Home Loan`, active or inactive (VERIFIED against S1 `picklist_value_details`). The create is rejected `INVALID_OR_NULL_FOR_RESTRICTED_PICKLIST` before any assertion is reached. **`31eaa21e` is the more serious shape:** generation ran with the ORG FIELD VOCABULARY block available and still produced a plausible-sounding label that does not exist — and **the grounding validator validates FIELD grounding, not enumerated VALUE membership**. That is a distinct, unclosed gap: a field can be perfectly grounded while the value asserted against it is not a member of that field's value set. A claim asserting a nonexistent value **manufactures wrong-reds by construction** — it can never go green, so it burns a live org run and an S6 investigation every time it executes, and it degrades any red-rate the pilot reads. **REMEDIATION direction:** value-membership validation against S1 picklist / restricted enumerations at generation time, failing loud (refuse to emit) rather than emitting a claim that cannot pass. Not scoped here; the static-audit sizing is the immediate next question. See D-329 (the implied-valid-case law), D-378 (the vocabulary block), D-384 (the value-free `matches_pattern` precedent — the same "the org owns the value" principle, applied one predicate at a time).

## D-400 — Asserted-vs-observed is NOT persisted; "why did this fail" is unanswerable for value-mismatch failures (2026-07-27). `AssertEvidence` (evidence.py:62-76) stores `step_id / ordinal / predicate / subject_ref / evaluated_row_count / held` — it does **not** store the OBSERVED value, and the ASSERTED value is recoverable only by joining the recipe body. Consequence on live data: `9ba2d3d2` (`Opportunity.Risk_Rating__c`, Flow `HL_Auto_Risk_Rating`) and `0d81c6f9` (`Task.OwnerId`, Flow `HL_High_Risk_Task`) both re-ran to `failed` with the record OBSERVED (`evaluated_row_count=1`) and the value differing — and are **UNDECIDABLE from persisted evidence**: nothing distinguishes a genuine Flow-behaviour finding (the org changed / the automation does not do what the requirement says) from a wrong claim (S3's expected value is incorrect). This blocks the product's core promise — a release-intelligence system whose failure evidence cannot say *what it expected vs what it got* cannot explain a red to the human who must act on it. **`DEFERRED_ITEMS §3` (richer captured trace / the A→B promotion) is hereby PROMOTED to the pilot gate on production evidence** — it is no longer a "when a query need emerges" nicety; the need emerged. **A second, independent invisibility on the same surface:** for D-210 **read-registered** records (rows a read observed that S4 did not create, registered for teardown at data_executor.py:1138-1146), the teardown outcome is invisible in evidence entirely — cleanup rides `CreateAttemptEvidence.cleanup`, and a read-registered record has no create step, so its delete failure appears nowhere in the trace and surfaces only as a `cleaned=false` row. See DEFERRED_ITEMS §3, D-210, D-401.

## D-401 — Metadata-recipes cannot execute via the QUEUE. By design, not dead code — but coverage statements must not overclaim (2026-07-27). `_probe_recipes` (run.py:779-789) filters the selected applicable set to `recipe_kind == "data-recipe"` **only**, per **D-300.1**: ADR-001 defines bva over DATA probes, and a metadata read strict-ANDed into a boundary verdict is a **wrong-green vector**. The filter is applied in BOTH run-all paths, between selection and the D-281 manifest write, so batch and manifest always agree on the probe set. **`priority` is preference ordering, not an admissibility gate** — `priority DESC, version_seq DESC, recipe_id ASC` (coordinator.py:1737) orders the set; the metadata-recipe's `-10` does not exclude it, `recipe_kind` does. **This is NOT D-395's dormancy species:** metadata-recipes have **148 real `s4_execution_runs` rows (2026-06-10 → 07-22)**, executed via the SINGLE-recipe path, which the D-300.1 docstring explicitly preserves ("The single path is untouched"). The narrow, true consequence: under the consumer's default `run_fn` → run-all, **a metadata-recipe never executes**, and **9 of the 25 cohort claims own one whose assertion was therefore not re-verified** by this arc. **Standing rule: coverage/verification statements must not assert "all recipes executed" for a queue-driven run** — they executed the data probes. See D-300.1, D-281 (the manifest), D-228 (the inspection fallback).

## D-402 — Gate-specification learnings from the cohort arc, recorded so they are not relearned (2026-07-27). **(1) An abort predicate on an eventually-reconciled flag needs an observation window.** The first pass aborted on "any new `s4_created_records` row left `cleaned=false` after teardown" — a `ProcessInstance` registered by D-210 and not directly deletable in Salesforce. The record was never a live org orphan (probe: absent from `query`, `IsDeleted=true` in `queryAll` — cascade-deleted with its parent), and the **deployed stranded reaper self-healed the flag between passes** (stranded_cleanup.py:105-112 selects `cleaned=false` rows with a non-NULL `environment_id`, deletes — 404 counts as success — and flips the flag; row 554 carried `environment_id=59` so it was visible to it). Eventual reconciliation IS the design; the abort fired on a transient. **The correct predicate is LIVE-IN-ORG**, probed with BOTH `query` and `queryAll`, treating `IsDeleted=true` as not-stranded — under which the 20-claim resume produced **zero** stranded rows. **(2) An error-code gate must read STEP level.** The gate compared the run's `sf_error_code` COLUMN against the historical set, but step-level codes live in `evidence.steps[].error_code` — so `INVALID_OR_NULL_FOR_RESTRICTED_PICKLIST` on `31eaa21e` bypassed it entirely. Audited retrospectively: both codes observed in this arc were already among the 8 in the historical corpus, so **no decision changed** — but the gate was weaker than it read. Any future error-pattern gate reads step level. **(3) Serial execution was the correct call** and is reaffirmed: the abort landed on claim 5 of 25; a parallel fan-out would already have written 20 more org states before the condition was observable. Live org mutation under abort gates is not parallelizable work. See D-210, D-394 (the referential-guard species).

## D-399.1 — AMENDMENT to D-399: S1 picklist COMPLETENESS is a hard prerequisite to value-membership validation, not a detail (2026-07-27). D-399 as written would **convert a loud failure into a silent one**. Audit evidence: a naive S1 membership check over the 183 approved claims flagged 15 — of which **4 are validator FALSE POSITIVES**: the org **ACCEPTED** those values with HTTP 2xx, including in runs on 2026-07-27. `Opportunity.StageName`'s captured set omits `'Prospecting'` (accepted live, HTTP 201); `Case.Priority` and `Opportunity.ForecastCategory` are captured with **NO value set at all** (`picklist_value_set_entity_id` NULL) while the org accepts values on them. A naive validator would have falsely refused **27% of flagged claims** on this sample. **The DIRECTION of failure is why this matters:** a wrong-red is LOUD — it lands in the run ledger, burns an org run, and gets investigated. A false refusal at GENERATION time is SILENT — the claim is never emitted, no outcome row exists, nothing appears in any ledger, and coverage carries a hole with **no signal at all**. Refusing on incomplete capture would invert fail-loud while keeping its name — the precise anti-pattern D-391 named at the analytics layer, one substrate over. **BINDING CONSTRAINT:** the validator may refuse **only** where S1's capture for that field is KNOWN-COMPLETE. Where capture is absent or partial it must report **CANNOT VALIDATE**, never **INVALID** — absence over fabricated judgment (the `llm=None` / `measured: False` precedent, now at the validator layer). **A per-field capture-completeness signal in S1 is therefore a hard precondition of D-399, sequenced before it.** See D-399 (the gap this amends), D-391 (absence-over-fabrication), D-403 (the capture gap itself).

## D-403 — S1 picklist capture is INCOMPLETE and nothing detected it (2026-07-27). Standard picklists are captured **partially** (`Opportunity.StageName` — the captured set omits an active value the org accepts) or **not at all** (`Case.Priority`, `Opportunity.ForecastCategory` — `picklist_value_set_entity_id` NULL while the org holds and accepts values). This is the **same species as the 07-08 transitional `Opportunity.StageName` version** whose `field_details.picklist_value_set_entity_id` was NULL — an entity version minted **without its detail row** — which alone produced **45% of the entire errored population** (D-397). That makes this the **third appearance of the D-291 / D-394 family**: a referent recorded without the row that gives it meaning, with no integrity check between them. The first two appearances blocked an EXECUTION (D-397's UnfillableWorld) and a REFERENT (D-394's purge); this one blocks a **VALIDATOR**, and would have made it lie. **No completeness signal exists**, so no consumer can distinguish *"this field genuinely has no values"* from *"values were not captured"* — the two are represented identically (absent/NULL). Every downstream reader inherits that ambiguity. Sized and root-caused in the Phase-2 diagnosis; not fixed here. See D-397, D-291, D-394, D-399.1.

## D-404 — Claim BODY diverges from the executable RECIPE: a legibility defect, and its fix belongs elsewhere (2026-07-27). `0dd02ef6`, `6ebbc232`, `93dff69e` assert `Opportunity.Loan_Type__c = 'Home Loan'` in the **claim body**, while their **recipes correctly stage `'Personal'`**. All three **PASSED on 2026-07-27 for the right reason** — the real VR fired on the update (*"Home Loan requires Loan Amount, Property Value, and Annual Income"*). **Execution is sound; the human-readable assertion is wrong.** In a procurement setting a customer reading an assertion the test did not actually exercise is precisely the credibility failure the readable-body work exists to prevent — and it is worse than a plain red, because it reads as a PASS of something untested. **Note the direction, which determines ownership: generation's STRUCTURED output was CORRECT and its PROSE was WRONG.** So this is not a value-membership defect and the D-399 validator would not fix it (the structured value is a legitimate member); remediation belongs with the **readable-body / claim-narration layer**, whose job is to render only what the recipe actually exercises. Distinct fix, distinct owner. See D-399 (the validator this is NOT), D-327 (identity-bearing narration).

## D-405 — Every guard landing after approval leaves a PRE-GUARD SURVIVOR COHORT, and nothing re-screens it (2026-07-27). `f2b072ac` (claim created **2026-07-02**) is a VR-conflict claim that **D-337's `vr_conflict.py` (landed 07-07) would catch** — its docstring names this exact class ("the claim is perma-red by construction") and covers acceptance conditions plus the D-306 update clauses. Approval never re-screened it, so it survived into production and executed against a live org twice. The contrast sharpens the rule: **`31eaa21e` was created 07-08 — AFTER D-337 — and shipped anyway**, because its defect is value NON-MEMBERSHIP, which no guard covers. Detection for the VR shape **exists and works** (67/67 active env-59 VRs return a parseable formula via `semantic/entity_attributes.vr_formula_text`, read by `world.py:454` `_active_vr_formulas` and by `vr_conflict.py`); detection for value membership **does not exist**. **GENERAL RULE (standing):** a guard that lands after claims are already approved protects only future emissions — the already-approved population is grandfathered in and nothing re-screens it. **D-399's validator will create its own survivor cohort the day it ships unless a re-screen pass over already-approved claims is part of the same change.** A guard without a backfill is half a guard. See D-337, D-399/D-399.1, D-353 (deprecate-then-regen, the existing migration mechanism a re-screen would drive).

## D-406 — Vocabulary TRUNCATION bounds what a validator may fairly refuse (2026-07-27). `vocabulary.py` caps enumerated values at `MAX_PICKLIST_VALUES = 6` with disclosed `"(+N more)"` truncation; reconstructing req-302's actual block shows `StageName` was shown **6 of its 10 values** to generation. **This was NOT the cause of `31eaa21e`:** `Loan_Type__c` appeared **untruncated with all three values** (`picklist: Home | Personal | Business`) and the model emitted `"Home Loan"` regardless — a **hallucination despite availability**, which is why **prompt enrichment is not the fix** and only a hard post-emission membership check closes it (D-399). But the truncation establishes a fairness bound on that check: **a validator must not refuse a value the prompt never showed the model.** Where the block truncated, a non-member value is a *retrieval* failure as much as an authorship one, and the honest verdict is CANNOT-FAIRLY-REFUSE rather than INVALID — the D-399.1 constraint applied on the prompt axis rather than the capture axis. See D-378 (the vocabulary surface), D-399.1, D-362 (the anti-dump discipline the cap serves).

## D-407 — S1 standard-picklist capture goes INLINE-ALWAYS; the D-118 StandardValueSet content-match is RETIRED (2026-07-27). D-118 inferred a standard picklist field's shared StandardValueSet by CONTENT-matching (exact set-equality of active values, fail-closed) because no Salesforce API exposes the linkage (corrections-log §22). Fixing capture required first deciding whether cross-field value-set IDENTITY is load-bearing. Read-only audit on env-59 (current versions): **(a) Nothing depends on sharing.** Every production consumer of `field_details.picklist_value_set_entity_id` is a per-field FORWARD 2-hop (`field → pvs_id → get_picklist_values`) — S4 k16 padding (`execution_engine/world.py:429-431`), S3 grounding metadata + staged-value support (`generation/governance_core.py:935-938, 1365-1369`), resolution symbol table (`resolution/symbols.py:92-97`), S8 field-value grounding (`evolution/s1_reader.py:100-104`), the v1 bridge (`metadata_bridge/s1_reader.py:188-194`), the detail mapper, the edge derivation, vocabulary rendering, presentation. **There is no reverse `pvs → fields` query anywhere in `primeqa/`** (VERIFIED: zero `FROM field_details` in production code, no cross-field join on the column); **zero** current `test_claims` rows reference a `PicklistValueSet`; `s8_grounding_validity` stores no entity ids. **(b) Sharing is rare.** Of 93 populated value sets **88 are used by exactly one field**; the 5 shared ones (`SVS:LeadSource` ×4, `SVS:Salutation` ×3, `SVS:ContactPointUsageType` ×3, `SVS:Industry` ×2, `SVS:ChangeRequestStatus` ×2) cover 14 of 102 linked fields, and de-sharing costs ~+95 value rows. **(c) The one place sharing WOULD be load-bearing is dormant and latently WRONG.** `record_type_picklist_value_grants` has 0 rows and `CONSTRAINS_PICKLIST_VALUES` 0 current edges on every org; worse, that edge targets the fine-grained `PicklistValue` entity (`semantic/edges.py:323-336`), so under sharing an Account RecordType constraining `Industry` would point at the *same* value entities `Lead.Industry` uses — per-field sets make it object-correct. **DECISION: INLINE-ALWAYS.** `standard_value_set_match.py` + `tests/test_standard_value_set_match.py` deleted; `primeqa/sync/picklist_capture.py` replaces them. Supersedes D-118 and the §22 resolution in `PHASE_2_PLAN_corrections.md` (left intact as historical record). **Two live defect classes die with the shared anchor** — (1) *silent link-drop*: D-118's docstring framed fail-closed as a self-heal ("the match fails and the edge correctly drops"), but dropping the edge drops the accepted-values grounding, silently; inline capture has no such transition. (2) *child-row orphaning* — see D-408. **Staleness measured and EMPTY:** across all 102 populated sets (45 objects, 45/45 describes HTTP 200) — 101 COMPLETE, 1 SUBSET, **0 SUPERSET, 0 BOTH**. The wrong-red vector (S1 holding a value the org rejects, which k16 padding could choose) does not exist on this org; the test ran in its strictest form, since across all 164 picklist fields in those describes zero values returned `active: false`. **Cost + cap:** naive inline-always would materialize 19 724 PicklistValue entities — each an EMBEDDED entity — against a 6 355-entity org, but that tail is not business vocabulary (one field, `PromptVersion.TargetPageKey1Ref`, is 55% of it at 10 862 page keys; the rest is timezone ×8, locale ×3, sObject-name lists). `MAX_INLINE_PICKLIST_VALUES = 200` captures the business surface whole — across every object the approved corpus exercises the largest non-timezone picklist is 12 values, and the biggest genuine business vocabulary on the org is `Industry` at 32 — while the 17 fields above the cap record `inline_truncated` rather than being silently partial. Truncation is safe in both consuming directions: it only REMOVES values, so k16 padding can still only choose a value the org accepts, and D-399's validator downgrades to CANNOT VALIDATE rather than INVALID. **Known residue, deliberately NOT fixed here:** the PicklistValueSet phase still fetches the full SVS catalog (~6 min per full sync) and materializes ~37 PVS + ~521 PicklistValue entities that **no field now references**; D-309 rejected a referenced-names filter precisely because the content-match needed the full catalog, and that rationale no longer holds. Narrowing it is a separate scoped change (the GVS half stays load-bearing for custom fields). Flagged in `phases.py`. See D-118, D-204.1, D-309, D-334, D-408.

## D-408 — The root fix: a fail-closed IDENTITY match was allowed to discard CONTENT the describe already carried (2026-07-27). `match_standard_value_set` (retired) collapsed three behaviourally different outcomes — empty value set, 0 matches, ≥2 ambiguous matches — into one `None`, and `phase_field` responded by writing no value-set marker at all. The describe payload it held at that moment contained the field's complete `picklistValues` array. Fail-closed was correct about the **link** (a false link means wrong accepted-values, hence a wrong test) and was silently applied to the **values**, which were never in doubt. Measured on env-59 before the fix: **275 of 377** picklist/multipicklist fields carried a NULL FK — **275 standard, 0 custom** — 73% of the picklist surface holding no values, the entire loss falling on the standard half. Representative losses, both referenced by real approved claims: `Case.Priority` ({High, Low, Medium}) matched **ten** SVSes with identical value sets → ambiguous → dropped, even though `SVS:CasePriority` was synced and contained `High`; `Opportunity.ForecastCategory` matched none at all. **The compounding defect: NULL meant two different things** — "this field genuinely has no value set" and "capture failed" were indistinguishable, and that ambiguity (not the missing values) is what made value-membership validation unsafe to build, since refusing on an uncaptured field inverts fail-loud into a **silent false refusal** (D-399.1). **Fix:** tenant migration `20260727_0010` adds nullable `field_details.picklist_capture VARCHAR` (open text, no CHECK — code owns the vocabulary, D-285 precedent), predict-gated from explicit revision `20260708_0010`, never `head`. `phase_field` stamps every picklist field; `_map_field_details` writes it. Vocabulary: `gvs` / `inline` / `inline_standard` assert a captured set; `inline_truncated` is a disclosed SUBSET; `no_values` is conclusive absence; **NULL means PRE-MIGRATION and must be read as "draw no conclusion"**, exactly like `inline_truncated`. **A second blocker, found by RUNNING rather than reading:** the Field phase aborted with `StringDataRightTruncation` — `picklist_value_details.value_api_name` was `varchar(40)`, sized when S1 only ever captured GVS/SVS/custom-inline business vocabularies. Standard describe values include namespaced sObject api-names: **31 values across 7 fields exceed 40 chars, longest 59** (`ApexTrigger.TableEnumOrId` → `CHANNEL_ORDERS__Customer_Order_Product_History__ChangeEvent`). Widened to 255 (matching the sibling `value_label`) in `20260727_0011`, predict-gated from `20260727_0010`; the phase transaction had rolled back cleanly, so this was a BLOCKED capture, never a corruption. Truncating an api-name was rejected outright — it would mint a value the org does not have, the exact defect class this work removes — so the downgrade refuses loudly rather than shortening real identifiers. **Custom-picklist behaviour is unchanged and PROVEN so** (all 56 were already complete): three tests pin it, including one that hands a custom field *different* values in describe vs Tooling metadata and asserts Tooling wins, and one proving a custom field with an empty Tooling definition still does NOT fall through to the standard path despite carrying describe values. **Also deleted:** the skipped-PicklistValueSet-phase branch that logged at INFO and continued — capture no longer depends on the SVS index existing at all, so a resumed sync that skips that phase captures identically to a fresh one (this is what made D-411 possible). **VERIFIED OUTCOME on env-59 (full sync `89457ebb`, seq 162):** populated value sets **102 → 369 of 377**; marks `inline_standard` 296 / `inline` 56 / `inline_truncated` 17 / `no_values` 8; PicklistValue entities 728 → **6 958**; anchors 151 → **464**; `HAS_PICKLIST_VALUES` edges 369. Churn at seq 162 was **exactly the picklist surface** — 377 Field versions minted and 377 superseded (321 standard + 56 custom), 313 anchors + 6 230 values inserted, plus 1 unrelated `User`; **no Object / Layout / ValidationRule / Profile / PermissionSet / Flow / ApprovalProcess / RecordType churn**, so no D-291 breadth concern. Required+createable picklists with no values — the latent `UnfillableWorld` surface — **54 → 1**, and the survivor (`Location.LocationType`) was verified against the live describe as **genuinely valueless (0 org values)**, as were all 8 `no_values` fields; `no_values` is honest absence, not a fourth silent exit. `Opportunity.StageName` reads **12**. See D-118, D-291, D-334, D-399.1, D-407.

## D-409 — The value-membership audit's true denominator: it was blind to 73% of the picklist surface (2026-07-27). The D-399 audit that reported **15 offending approved claims** examined only the 102 populated fields. Restated honestly against the full surface: **by field, 102/377 = 27.1% validatable and 275/377 = 72.9% outside the checkable surface entirely**; **by claim**, of 183 approved claims 122 assert ≥1 picklist literal, 120 had every such literal on a captured field, and **2 carried ≥1 literal the audit could not check** — `e62a2872` (`Case.Priority = High`) and `0bb8465e` (`Opportunity.ForecastCategory = Closed`). Both ALSO reference captured fields, so each appeared in the audit's population and **passed**; partial coverage presenting as a pass is a more dangerous shape than plain invisibility. Independently cross-checked by a shape-agnostic regex sweep over concatenated claim+recipe JSON: same answer, exactly 2. So the honest statement of the prior result is **15 offenders found / 122 claims examined, 2 of those incompletely covered, 275 of 377 org picklist fields uncheckable**. The exposure was narrow only because the corpus is narrow — 256 of the 275 uncaptured fields sit on objects no approved claim touches, but **19 uncaptured picklist fields are on objects the corpus already exercises** (Task ×7, Contact ×6, Account ×2, Opportunity ×2, Case ×1, ProcessInstance ×1), so any future generation touching those would have landed in the same blind spot. **RE-AUDIT AT FULL COVERAGE (post-fix, 369/377 captured):** 206 literals VALID, **10 offending approved claims**, **0 INACTIVE**, **0 still unvalidatable**. The count moved 15 → 10 because the 4 capture-incomplete FALSE POSITIVES now validate correctly and the 2 formerly-blind claims resolve as VALID (`Case.Priority = High` ∈ {High, Medium, Low}; `ForecastCategory = Closed` ∈ the 6 org values); `Opportunity.StageName = 'Prospecting'` (`1bdde2bd`) also clears now that the orphaned SUBSET is repaired. **This is the direct test of D-399.1's premise and it holds: with capture complete and its outcome recorded, the validator produces no false refusals.** The 10 survivors are all genuine non-membership on fully-captured CUSTOM fields — 9 × `Opportunity.Loan_Type__c = 'Home Loan'` (org: Business/Home/Personal) and 1 × `PLS_FB_Order__c.PLS_FB_Status__c = 'Completed'` (org: Cancelled/Confirmed/Draft/Fulfilled/Submitted). *Caveat (ASSUMED):* `test_claims`/`test_recipes` carry no org column, so attributing all 183 approved claims to env-59 is an assumption; it does not move the counts, since zero referenced fields were absent from env-59's model. See D-399, D-399.1, D-405, D-410.

## D-410 — Vocabulary consequence: for 275 fields the generator was shown a bare type, so inventing a value was the only behaviour available — and `31eaa21e` is the WORSE case (2026-07-27). The capture gap did not merely block validation downstream; it removed the accepted values from the model's input upstream, in both S3 surfaces (VERIFIED by reading): the field vocabulary block (`generation/vocabulary.py:105-115`) emits `" picklist: A | B | C"` only `if f.picklist_values` and otherwise falls through to `elif f.field_type`, so each of the 275 uncaptured fields rendered as `- Priority ("Priority") picklist` — existence and type, **no enumeration**; and grounding metadata (`generation/governance_core.py:933-939`) leaves `picklist_values = None` unless a `pvs_id` resolves, so the governance layer had no list to check an emitted literal against either. With no enumeration in the prompt and no list to check against, a model asked to stage a picklist value had exactly one available behaviour: invent a plausible one. Every such literal on those 275 fields was **unfalsifiable by construction** — neither the generator nor the governance layer could have done better. **That is the benign half, and it sharpens the other half.** `31eaa21e` staged `Opportunity.Loan_Type__c = "Home Loan"`, and `Loan_Type__c` is a **CUSTOM** field — one of the 56 that were fully captured all along (D-334 inline anchors), shown to the model **untruncated with all three values** (`Home | Personal | Business`, per D-406). It hallucinated with the complete enumeration verbatim in context. That is a distinct and worse class: the first is a system that *cannot know*, the second is a system that *was told and did not comply*. **This capture fix does not address `31eaa21e` and must not be credited with doing so** — it converts the first class into the second, i.e. it makes hallucination DETECTABLE, which is precisely the precondition D-399's membership validator needs and nothing more. Expect the offender count to be a floor that rises as coverage grows; that rise is the audit gaining sight, not quality regressing. See D-399, D-405, D-406, D-408, D-409.

## D-411 — INCIDENT: self-inflicted production degradation — a partial sync was resumed by a DIFFERENT code version than the one that started it (2026-07-27). Observed on live env-59 data during the D-407/D-408 resync, from `s1_sync_jobs` / `sync_runs` (all times UTC). **Sequence:** `12:08:22` an in-process full sync on NEW (uncommitted, local) code starts as run `2c79c5cd`, holding the D-341 org advisory lock. `12:08:33 … 12:11:54` the deployed scheduler enqueues jobs 134–137 on a ~65 s tick; **all four are correctly refused** (`error_code=concurrent_sync`). `12:12:57` the run FAILS in the Field phase on the `varchar(40)` blocker (D-408); the phase transaction rolls back cleanly, the lock releases, and the run is left `status=failure` **with a resume anchor**. `12:12:59` — **two seconds later** — the scheduler enqueues job 138, which RESUMES run `2c79c5cd` **on the OLD DEPLOYED CODE**. A resume starts *after* `last_completed_phase`, so it **skips the PicklistValueSet phase**; `ctx.svs_metadata_cache` is therefore empty, `build_svs_index` returns `{}`, and under the old code **no standard picklist field can content-match**. Every one takes the no-marker path. **Result at seq 161: 46 standard picklist fields re-versioned with `picklist_value_set_entity_id = NULL`** — `Account.Industry`, `Account.Type`, `Account.AccountSource`, `Case.Status`, `Case.Origin`, `Case.Reason`, `Campaign.Status`, `Asset.Status`, `Lead.Status`, `Opportunity.StageName`, `Task.Status`, … Populated value sets dropped **102 → 56**; `StageName` went from 10 captured values to **0**. **ROOT CAUSE is NOT `phases.py:561`.** That INFO-shrug is why the loss was INVISIBLE, and deleting the branch (D-408) fixes only the visibility. The root cause is that **A PARTIAL SYNC IS RESUMABLE BY A DIFFERENT CODE VERSION THAN THE ONE THAT STARTED IT**: new code opened the transaction, failed, and old code completed the fragment under different extraction semantics. Nothing in the resume path asserts that the resuming binary shares the originator's extraction contract. **REMEDIATION (not built here):** a partial run records the code identity that started it (build SHA / extraction-contract version) and **refuses resume by any other**; a foreign resume must fail the job, not silently complete the fragment. Added to the pilot gate. **What worked:** D-341's advisory lock behaved exactly as designed throughout — jobs 134–137 and later 140–176 were all refused, and the lock is what bounded the damage to the single window between failure and re-enqueue. **Severity is grounding-LOSS, not wrong-data:** the fields lost their accepted-values list; none gained a wrong value. Downstream that is a bare `picklist` to S3 (D-410) and an unfillable field to S4 k16 — degradation and refusal, never a wrong-green. **REPAIRED** by the subsequent full sync on new code (run `89457ebb`, seq 162): all **46/46** re-populated, each `inline_standard` with its full org value set (`Account.Industry` 32, `StageName` 12, `Case.Status` 4, …), and populated overall at **369/377** — above the 102 baseline, so the repair is a strict improvement rather than a restoration. **ALSO RECORDED — the SetupAuditTrail skip gate is blind to CODE changes.** The first full-sync attempt after the fix returned in 19 s having done nothing (`describe_calls=0`, `last_completed_phase=None`, inserted/superseded/unchanged all 0): the org-level skip gate (1b.1, `engine._evaluate_skip_gate`) asks **"has the ORG changed since the watermark?"** and env-59 had not, so the whole sync was skipped — correctly by its own contract. The gate has no notion of *what S1 EXTRACTS from an unchanged org having changed*, which is exactly what a capture fix is. **Consequence: deploying D-407/D-408 will NOT re-capture any quiet org.** Every subsequent daily sync keeps skipping and the 275 fields stay valueless indefinitely; the fix lands only on the next org metadata change or a deliberate forced re-capture. **This is a correctness gap, not an optimisation** — and it generalises to any future change in extraction semantics (normalization, a new detail column, a mapper fix). Every pilot org needs an explicit per-org re-capture step; the daily schedule is not sufficient. A `capture_generation` / extraction-contract counter on `connected_orgs`, bumped when extraction semantics change and compared in the gate, would make this self-healing; deliberately out of scope here and added to the pilot gate. For this session the gate was overridden **in-process only** (an instance-level `_evaluate_skip_gate` returning `skip=False, server_time=None`), which leaves `connected_orgs.setup_audit_watermark` untouched — `engine.py:773` advances it only when a server time is present — so production skip-gate behaviour is byte-identical afterwards; the nominal alternative (clearing the watermark, the gate's own "first confirmed sync" fail-safe) would have written production bookkeeping and was rejected as the heavier option. The delta path is unaffected either way: only `ValidationRule` is delta-safe (`sync/delta.py:35`), so `Field` always full-fetches once a sync actually runs. **PROCESS FINDING:** a live sync against a real org, driven from **uncommitted local code**, with the **deployed scheduler racing for the same lock**, is an irreversible-decision shape and should have carried a HOLD gate before execution. The task prompt authorised autonomous execution through it and no gate was requested at that boundary; the lesson is that "read-only except the run ledger's own writes" does not describe a sync — a sync REWRITES the semantic model, and doing so from code that is not the deployed code creates a version-skew window that the scheduler will find within seconds. See D-341, D-152, D-250, D-291, D-408.

## D-412 — Value-membership validator: three verdicts, never two (2026-07-27). The D-399 validator is BUILT — `primeqa/generation/value_membership.py`, deterministic, LLM-free, read-only over S1, **NOT wired into any path** (offline/callable only; what a refusal DOES — block emission / emit-with-flag / route to declination — is a product decision that gets its own D-entry before any wiring). **The binding design constraint (D-399.1): THREE verdicts — VALID / INVALID / CANNOT_VALIDATE — never two.** A two-verdict design converts every capture gap into a refusal, and a false refusal is SILENT (the claim is never emitted; coverage grows a hole with no signal) while a wrong-red is LOUD (it fails on a live run in front of a human). Two verdicts therefore invert the fail-loud posture — they trade the loud failure for the silent one — and that inversion is precisely why this validator was unsafe to build before D-408 recorded per-field capture outcomes. The gate reads `field_details.picklist_capture`: `gvs`/`inline`/`inline_standard` → authoritative, may refuse (`gvs` absent on env-59 today but asserts a captured set per D-408, gated identically); `inline_truncated` → CANNOT_VALIDATE always (a disclosed 200-cap SUBSET cannot distinguish "org lacks it" from "we truncated it away", 17 fields); `NULL` → pre-migration, draw no conclusion; **unknown future marks → CANNOT_VALIDATE** (fail toward loud, never toward silent refusal); `no_values` → **refusal is CORRECT**: the mark is written only when the describe payload itself carried zero values and all 8 such env-59 fields were re-verified against the live org (0 values each, D-408) — the set is authoritatively EMPTY, and a member of the empty set does not exist. **Matching:** against `value_api_name` AND `value_label` with `matched_on` carried per check (the earlier audit compared api-name only and nearly misread a label; a label-only match is VALID for membership but the transport may still need the api spelling); ACTIVE values only for VALID, with present-but-inactive a **distinct INVALID reason (`inactive` = org drift, a different owner) from `absent` (= hallucination, generation's defect)** — never collapsed; exact match, no case-folding (a case mismatch in a test assertion is a defect, not noise); multipicklist splits on `;`. **Extraction is structured-only**: `field_values`/`field_changes` maps (claim `from_state`/`to_state`/`expected_effect.changes`, recipe `steps[]`), `{kind:"literal"}` wrappers, and Field-subject condition nodes; free strings are never parsed, so prose (`triggering_action.description`) is excluded by construction. **Fail-loud on its own errors:** unreadable capture column → `ValueMembershipError`, and an org resolving to ZERO picklist fields also raises (an empty index would validate everything vacuously — a wrong-green of the validator's own). **No schema change was needed** — capture marks (20260727_0010) and value rows already carry everything; MIGRATE-FIRST not invoked. **ACCEPTANCE (VERIFIED, corpus run over all 183 approved claims):** exactly **10 flagged / 0 missed / 0 unexpected / 0 must-not-flag violations** — the 9 `Opportunity.Loan_Type__c='Home Loan'` claims + `34868a5a` `PLS_FB_Status__c='Completed'`, every one `absent` on an authoritative `inline` capture; the 4 former false positives (`Prospecting`, `Case.Priority=High`, both `PLS_BM_Stage__c=Qualification`) and the 2 formerly-blind claims all validate VALID. Distribution: claims 173 valid / 10 invalid / 0 cannot_validate; literals 206 valid / 10 invalid; **all 206 VALID matches were api-name matches — zero label-only matches in the live corpus** (the label path is pinned by unit test). `34868a5a` answered: **`Completed` is ABSENT entirely** — the org's 5 values (Draft/Submitted/Confirmed/Fulfilled/Cancelled) are all active, no `Completed` under any api-name, label or active state → hallucination, not org drift; owner is generation, not the org. 17 unit tests pin every branch (label-only match, inactive, truncated, NULL-capture, unknown-mark, prose exclusion, multipicklist fan-out, both fail-loud paths). **The D-405 survivor problem stands:** the day this wires in, every already-approved claim is grandfathered — the 10 offenders sit in the approved population TODAY. A re-screen pass needs: (1) this validator run over approved claims (this corpus run IS the mechanism, already proven); (2) a disposition rule for INVALID survivors — D-353's deprecate-then-regen is the existing migration mechanism; (3) the D-401 caveat that 9 of the 10 share the `Home Loan` literal from one generation era, so regen must post-date prompt v32 (D-384) or it re-mints the same defect; (4) CANNOT_VALIDATE survivors stay approved and untouched (refusing them would be the silent inversion again). Not built here. See D-399, D-399.1, D-405, D-407, D-408, D-409, D-410.

## D-413 — WIRING DECISION: membership INVALID routes to DECLINATION — not block-emission, not emit-with-flag (2026-07-27). The D-412 validator is wired into `finalize_outcome` (post-emission, pre-persistence): every literal an authored bundle asserts/stages against an enumerated field is membership-checked before the persister sees it. **Why declination:** block-emission trades a loud failure for a silent one — the claim vanishes, coverage grows a hole, and nothing signals it (D-399.1's constraint one layer out); emit-with-flag relies on a human noticing, and 10 bad claims already survived approval, so "a human will notice" is empirically false on this exact defect class. A declination is visible, countable and buyer-legible. **Mechanism:** an INVALID bundle becomes an entry on the EXISTING D-302 `partial_refusals` surface (same key, same per-entry shape resolve-time refusals use), `refusal_kind=ungrounded-claim`, its payload sub-discriminated by **`defer_class: "value-membership"`** — resolving the parked sub-discriminator fork on the existing JSONB rather than minting a new top-level RefusalKind. (`defer_class` did not previously exist in code; this is its first realization, as a payload key — the nearest existing mechanism, per the fork's own terms.) The payload carries `violations[]` — field, asserted value, the org's actual (active) value set, and the reason, `absent` (the org never had it — hallucination, generation's defect) vs `inactive` (the org retired it — drift, the org owner's) — plus a one-line `detail` a buyer can read: *"asserted value 'Home Loan' is not a member of Opportunity.Loan_Type__c's value set (absent); org accepts: Business | Home | Personal"*. When EVERY authored bundle declines, the draft routes as a whole-outcome `UNGROUNDED_CLAIM` refusal with the merged payload (same degrade-this-requirement-never-the-batch posture as the D-105.4 backstop). **CANNOT_VALIDATE passes through untouched** — never a declination, never a block; capture gaps must not refuse (D-399.1). **Fail-loud:** a validator error propagates — generation errors rather than emitting unvalidated. **Index construction stays inside the S1 seam:** `FieldCaptureIndex.from_s1` resolves only the fields the bundles actually reference, through `get_entities` → `get_entity_details` (SELECT * carries `picklist_capture`) → `get_picklist_values`, at the batch's pinned seq — no raw connection, no substrate crossing; a batch with no enumerated literals does zero extra reads. **Two validator guards, both CC-originated during the D-412 build and both kept deliberately:** (1) unknown FUTURE capture marks resolve to CANNOT_VALIDATE, so a new capture source can never silently become a refusal source; (2) an org resolving to zero picklist fields is a fail-loud `ValueMembershipError` in whole-org audit mode, because an empty index would validate everything vacuously — the validator's own wrong-green. (In the per-field emission mode a detail row MISSING the capture KEY reads as NULL-capture → CANNOT_VALIDATE, not an error — the key is always present against the real schema and raising on synthetic S1 doubles would break every fixture-based test toward the silent side.) See D-302, D-399.1, D-405, D-412.

## D-414 — ARC CLOSE: picklist capture + value membership, D-403…D-413 (2026-07-28). The arc that began as a read-only diagnosis of S1's picklist capture (D-403) closes with the membership validator wired and the approved corpus clean. **End-to-end movement, all live-verified on env-59:** S1 picklist capture **102 → 369 of 377** fields populated (D-407/D-408, INLINE-ALWAYS, D-118 retired); latent-`UnfillableWorld` required-createable picklists **54 → 1**, the survivor (`Location.LocationType`) org-verified genuinely valueless; audit coverage **27.1% (102/377 checkable) → 377/377 decidable** — 369 authoritative + 8 conclusive-empty, with the 17 `inline_truncated` fields correctly UNDECIDABLE by design rather than silently miscounted; offender count **15 → 10** (the 5 delta were false positives that cleared at full capture — the direct confirmation of D-399.1: with capture complete and its outcome recorded, the validator produced **zero false refusals**); validator acceptance **10/10 flagged, 0 deviations** (D-412); wired as declination (D-413); **survivors re-screened** (D-405/D-353): all 10 deprecated with reasons, both source requirements regenerated post-v32 (req-302 → 16 claims, req-320 → 13), **all 29 membership-VALID, zero declinations, zero hallucination recurrence** — and the regen furnished the arc's cleanest illustration of why membership is per-field: the new req-320 corpus stages `Completed` on `PLS_FB_Fulfilment_Task__c.PLS_FB_Status__c`, where it IS a member ({Completed, Open, Cancelled}), while the deprecated `34868a5a` staged it on the ORDER's status, where it never was. Post-re-screen and post-deploy (main @5f3aea2, all three Railway services): approved corpus **173/173 VALID, 0 INVALID, 0 CANNOT_VALIDATE**; capture distribution unchanged (inline_standard 296 / inline 56 / inline_truncated 17 / no_values 8, seq 162). **Standing residue, tracked in PLIMSOL_FIX_PLAN (pilot-gate cluster), not closed by this arc:** version-mismatched sync resume (the D-411 incident's root cause); the per-org re-capture step + skip-gate code-blindness (env-78 still on pre-D-403 capture, 86/361 marks-NULL — it validates NOTHING until re-captured, which is correct three-verdict behaviour but zero coverage); the `inline_truncated` disclosure audit for the remaining consumers (S3 vocabulary / governance metadata / k16 — the validator's own handling is done); and the wiring's next product seam: a declination is now visible and countable, but nothing yet AGGREGATES declinations for the buyer (per-requirement declination counts on the requirement page / decision surface) — that is everyday-surfaces work, not validator work. See D-399, D-399.1, D-403…D-413.

## D-415 — CAPTURE IDENTITY vs EXECUTION IDENTITY: the severance (parent D-080) (2026-07-29). **The undocumented coupling.** D-266 requires the org's OAuth Run-As user to be a Salesforce System Administrator so S1's FLS-aware describes see everything. S4 execution inherits that same admin identity **only because the two share one credential** — `_resolve_org_token` (`execution_engine/credentials.py:35-65`) resolves environment → connection → token identically for sync and execution. The coupling is accidental, undocumented until now, and one credential CANNOT serve both: pointing the shared credential at a run-as identity would silently corrupt capture (FLS-hidden fields become indistinguishable from nonexistent ones — the exact CF-1 ambiguity D-266 exists to prevent). **RULE:** *capture identity is infrastructure — always admin, per D-266, non-negotiable.* *Execution identity is semantic exactly when the claim asserts identity-scoped behaviour, and is then pinned in the CLAIM; otherwise it is operational, lives on the recipe body, and stays outside the identity hash* — the D-080 boundary (metadata-inspection verifies CONFIGURED state, run-as verifies RUNTIME-EFFECTIVE experience, silent substitution forbidden) extended from recipe-kind to credential. **Q1's schema answer — semantic identity is expressible TODAY for the positive form, and NOT for the negative:** `CapabilityClaimBody.granting_subject: IdentityBearingRef` (`test_representation/models/claims/permission/capability_claim.py:38`) is a pinned Profile/PermissionSet reference INSIDE `asserted_truth`, and `compute_identity_hash(archetype, claim_kind, asserted_truth, semantic_conditions)` (`identity_hash.py:77-119`) hashes it — two claims differing only by `granting_subject` hash differently, no schema change. `Condition.subject: IdentityBearingRef` (`conditions.py:76`) can additionally carry pinned identity refs in the conditions layer. **PROMINENT LIMITATION: "identity X CANNOT do Y" is NOT expressible.** `CapabilityClaimBody` v1 has `granted_capability: str` and no polarity/negation slot (verified: zero polarity/denied fields); the prohibition archetype's bodies are data-behaviour-shaped (org-rejects-action) and carry no acting-identity slot. A denied-capability claim therefore needs a NEW `capability-claim` body_schema_version (or new kind) — **an S2 schema change touching claim identity → TA review required before any S4 identity build that needs the negative form.** The positive form ("Profile P can edit F", verified by run-as attempt succeeding) and the D-290 rejection form (a data-recipe under a run-as identity whose expected rejection is `INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS*` — identity pinned via `granting_subject`-style subject, rejection carried by the recipe's `expect_rejection`) need nothing new. **Operational identity confirmed OUTSIDE the hash:** `run_as_user`/`identity_context` live on `DataMutationTriggerBody` (`triggers/data_mutation.py:54-79`) and the recipe bodies — none of the four hashed inputs — so re-pointing a recipe at a different designated test user re-versions the RECIPE only, never mints a new claim. **Q3's ownership-drift census:** exactly **1 of 201** approved claims touches an ownership field (`0d81c6f9`, `Task.OwnerId` — already the D-400 undecidable specimen); `CreatedById`/`LastModifiedById`: zero. Ownership-sensitivity under run-as is real but currently a 1-claim exposure, not a corpus property. See D-080, D-266, D-290, D-400, D-416…D-419.

## D-416 — IMPERSONATION MECHANISM: JWT Bearer, subject to org-side setup; stored per-user credentials REJECTED (2026-07-29). The JWT Bearer flow (`urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer`) is the decided mechanism for run-as execution. **Rejected: stored per-user credentials** — mechanically cheaper (the `password` grant already exists at `metadata/worker_runner.py:180-183`; adding a username/password per test identity is config, not code) but it imposes per-identity secret custody FOREVER: one password + security token per designated user, per pilot org, rotated on every org policy cycle, all Fernet-at-rest but plaintext-equivalent in use — scaling linearly against SEC-5's posture. Cheap once, expensive always. **JWT feasibility on env-59, measured:** (a) *client side is essentially free* — PyJWT and `cryptography` are already dependencies (app JWT auth; Fernet), RS256 assertion signing is ~20 lines; the private key would live Fernet-encrypted in the connection config, the same custody class as `client_secret` today. (b) *Org side is UI-only and could NOT be verified from here*: the Tooling `ConnectedApplication` query returns only Environment Hub + PartnerTrial — the "Prime QA SFDC" app we authenticate through is not API-readable, so whether it already carries a certificate is UNKNOWN. Prerequisites (AK, one-time, in the org UI): upload/generate an X.509 cert on the connected app, enable "Use digital signatures", set OAuth policy to admin-approved-users-are-pre-authorized, and assign the designated test users' profiles/permission sets to the app. The existing app CAN be extended in place (digital signatures + client_credentials coexist; same client_id) — a new app is not required unless AK prefers isolation. **If the org-side setup is not performed, JWT is BLOCKED and run-as does not ship — we do NOT silently fall back to the password grant.** See D-415, D-417.

## D-417 — TEST IDENTITY PROVISIONING: designate existing users; synthetic managed users REJECTED (2026-07-29). Run-as identities are DESIGNATED existing Salesforce users (synced by S1 — `User` entities with `user_details.profile_entity_id` already exist; 4 on env-59), referenced from claims/recipes by pinned ref. **Rejected: minting synthetic managed users** — Salesforce users cannot be hard-deleted, only deactivated; licenses are finite; so every minted identity is PERMANENT RESIDUE in a customer org, a class the D-196 cleanup machinery (record rows, reverse-order teardown) has no concept of and cannot be extended to cover (there is nothing to delete). Designation's obligation is DRIFT — an admin renames/deactivates/re-profiles the designated user and identity-scoped recipes break — which is exactly the grounding-validity shape S8 already owns (intact/drifted/broken + repair suggestion); no new machinery. Onboarding gains one step: name the designated test identities per org (and pre-authorize them to the connected app, D-416). See D-415, D-416.

## D-418 — TEARDOWN IDENTITY — the k14 corollary: teardown runs as the ADMIN service identity regardless of run identity (2026-07-29). Today teardown inherits the run's client verbatim: `data_executor.py:367/372/406/417` pass the executing client into `tracker.teardown(client, _best_effort_delete)`, and `_best_effort_delete` (`:1541-1554`) deletes through it. Under a non-admin run identity, a record the identity can CREATE but not DELETE (no Delete CRUD, sharing-restricted) strands silently — `_best_effort_delete` records the failure and never raises, and for D-210 read-registered rows the failure appears NOWHERE in evidence (D-400's teardown-invisibility) — so non-admin run-as would GUARANTEE the strand class D-400 can only observe. k14 dictates the fix: teardown is execution ISOLATION, never part of the verdict — it must not inherit the run's constraints, exactly as it must not influence the outcome. **RULE: the run executes as the run identity; teardown always executes as the admin service identity (a second client).** Smallest change: resolve BOTH clients in `run.py` when run identity ≠ service identity and pass the admin client to every `tracker.teardown(...)` site — the four call sites above; `_best_effort_delete` itself is client-agnostic and unchanged. D-210 read-registration cleanup rides the same `tracker.teardown` path → covered by the same change. `stranded_cleanup.py` needs NO change — it resolves its own client via `resolve_data_mutation_client` (`stranded_cleanup.py:120-121`), which is the admin service credential by construction. See D-196, D-210, D-400, D-415.

## D-419 — IDENTITY EXPLAINABILITY: no persisted execution identity anywhere in the evidence chain (2026-07-29). `s4_execution_runs` carries no identity column (columns end at `source` — VERIFIED), `RunEvidence` none (`evidence.py` — the only "identity" is the run's own id), `s6_interpretations` none. Vacuously fine today: every run is the same admin, so identity explains nothing. The moment two identities can execute, any verdict that DIFFERS by identity — the entire point of run-as — is unexplainable from persisted evidence: "passed as admin, failed as sales-user" would read as a flaky re-run, indistinguishable from D-273's transient class. Same shape as D-400's asserted-vs-observed gap (evidence that cannot answer the question the red poses) and it RIDES THAT PILOT-GATE ITEM: when the trace enrichment lands, the executing identity is one more field on the run row + evidence envelope, not a separate mechanism. Phase-2 of the identity build persists it from day one — an identity-scoped run without persisted identity would be D-400 with a mechanism that guarantees it. See D-273, D-400, D-411 (the incident-shaped precedent for version-skew unexplainability), D-415.

## D-420 — PHASE 0 RESULT: the 53 never-run approved claims executed; the D-337 guard boundary measured live (2026-07-29). The never-run-at-current-version approved population (53 claims — NOT the regen cohort, whose 29 writes were 24 drafts + 5 revived already-run identities; premise corrected in-flight) executed serially on env-59 through the deployed worker: **39 passed / 8 failed / 6 enqueue-refused; 25/25 prohibition claims PASSED — the VR arc's live exit.** Zero UnfillableWorld, zero stranded records (all teardown org-verified), zero wrong-reds, zero org-behaviour findings. **All 8 failures are AUTHORSHIP, in three classes:** (a) **placeholder prose staged as typed values** ×3 (`48ff3239` stages the literal string `"provided"` into a DATE field; `602b41d4` stages `"within_enterprise_limit"` into a percent; `caa255be` a string-typed number → `JSON_PARSER_ERROR` before any business logic) — pre-D-338-era vintage, a dead class under current guards; (b) **conditional-VR slips** ×4 (`f02ddece` creates an SMB deal at Discount=30 against a deal-type-gated discount-cap VR; `d0c5aaaf`/`09d08502`/`f856a064` update Stage→'Approved' directly where the org requires the approval process) — **these POST-DATE D-337**: the VRs are cross-field-conditional, Kleene correctly refuses to PROVE conflict, and the guard ADMITS on unproven; (c) **a comprehension failure** ×1 (`5a01ebd9` creates at 250,000.01 → updates DOWN to 150,000 → asserts `Tier='Platinum'` — the stale band — where req-320's own text says "the classification stays current when the value changes"); no deterministic guard catches a claim that contradicts its source requirement's prose. **STANDING ISSUE from (b), now with a measured cost (4 claims): the D-337 guard resolves uncertainty toward emission — optimize-to-green at the guard layer.** When D-337 shipped, the alternatives were emit or silently drop; D-413's declination with `defer_class` now gives "cannot prove conflict-free" a destination that is neither. Not built here; recorded as the third `defer_class` candidate (after value-membership) with its cost quantified. **Two structural notes:** the 6 enqueue-refused (D-223: no S4-executable recipe — 4 existence + 2 automation-effect) are an INVISIBLE COVERAGE HOLE — an approved claim that can never run contributes nothing and warns nobody, the same shape as `79bc47e5`'s permanent undecidability (D-402 family); and the run's one abort — `UNEXPECTED_SOBJECT` on `PLS_FB_Audit_Log__c`, which was the **first-ever FL09 execution**, benign (D-210 read-registered, cleaned, org-verified) — demonstrates that a history-derived allowlist fires on every NEW coverage surface by construction: it is an **anti-novelty gate**, acceptable in a manually attended harness, wrong if automated. See D-210, D-223, D-337, D-338, D-353, D-402, D-413.
